Let H be the homogeneous H^-1 completion of smooth compactly supported even-x, odd-y functions on R^2. Let rho be smooth with that parity, let a=grad rho, and put

    B h=U[h].a,
    C_rho=sup_(r>0) r^(2/5)(|a|+r|Da|) < infinity.

Vector and matrix lengths are Euclidean and Frobenius lengths. For R>=1 define

    w_R=(1+r^2/R^2)^(-11/10).

The operator initially defined on the compact core by

    D_R g=w_R B(w_R^-1 g)-B g

extends boundedly to H, with

    ||D_R||_(H->H) <= 2^53 C_rho R^(-2/5).                    (1)

The constant is intentionally coarse. It proves smallness for a sufficiently large weight radius, not smallness at R=1.

#### Localization of the negative norm

Write t=log_2 r and eta_j=max(1-|t-j|,0). These Lipschitz radial functions sum to one and have overlap at most 2. They are supported in A_j={2^(j-1)<=r<=2^(j+1)} and satisfy r|grad eta_j|<3/2, because log2>2/3. Put r_j=2^j.

Let zeta_j equal one for |t-j|<=1, decrease linearly to zero for 1<|t-j|<2, and vanish otherwise. It has overlap at most 4 and the same derivative bound. Multiplication is interpreted by H^1 duality, so Lipschitz cutoffs are sufficient. The parity Hardy inequality applies to every function odd in at least one coordinate.

For g in H,

    (sum_j ||eta_j g||_H^2)^(1/2) <=4||g||_H.                 (2)

Indeed, for a finite collection of test functions phi_j, the squared H^1 norm of sum eta_j phi_j is at most 4(1+(3/2)^2) sum ||grad phi_j||^2<16 times that sum. Duality proves (2).

For functions f_j supported in A_j and of the required parity,

    ||sum_j f_j||_H <=6(sum_j ||f_j||_H^2)^(1/2).              (3)

To see this, replace a test phi by zeta_j phi on the support of f_j. The sum of squared H^1 norms of zeta_j phi is at most 8(1+(3/2)^2)||grad phi||^2=26||grad phi||^2<36||grad phi||^2. Cauchy-Schwarz gives (3). These inequalities also justify all infinite sums by completion.

#### Kernel bounds and separated annuli

Away from zero the vector kernel of U is

    K(Z)=(-sin(2theta),cos(2theta))/(2pi |Z|^2).

The local identity term in U_2 commutes with every weight and hence cancels from D_R. Complex differentiation of 1/(x-iy)^2 gives the bounds

    |K|<=1/(2pi r^2), |DK|_F<=2/(pi r^3), |D^2K|_F<=6/(pi r^4).

The operator U has norm at most 1 from scalar H^-1 to vector H^-1, by its exact Fourier symbol.

If j>=i+5, then |X|<=2r_i and r_j/4<=|Y|<=4r_j imply |X|<=|Y|/4. The parity projection of K(-Y) against an even-x, odd-y source is zero. Subtract it before pairing with eta_j g. The resulting kernel is bounded by 3|X|/(pi |Y|^3), and its Y gradient by 20|X|/(pi |Y|^4). Including the derivative of zeta_j gives 25|X|/(pi |Y|^4). Its L2 norm is at most

    1600 |X| r_j^-3/sqrt(3pi) <600 |X| r_j^-3.

Therefore |U[eta_j g](X)|<=600|X|r_j^-3||eta_j g||_H. Using ||f||_H<=||r f||_2 on A_i yields

    ||eta_i B(eta_j g)||_H
       <=9000 Gamma_i (r_i/r_j)^3 ||eta_j g||_H,              (4)

where Gamma_i=sup_(A_i)(|a|+r|Da|).

If i>=j+5, subtract the constant K(X), whose pairing with the source is zero. The same calculation gives

    ||eta_i B(eta_j g)||_H
       <=2000 Gamma_i (r_j/r_i) ||eta_j g||_H.                (5)

For example the Y-gradient bound after multiplication by zeta_j is 10/(pi |X|^3), its L2 norm is at most 40r_j/(sqrt(pi)|X|^3), and ||r eta_i||_2<=4sqrt(pi)r_i^2. These bounds are strictly below the rounded constants in (4)-(5).

For neighboring annuli, direct H^-1 multiplication and ||U||<=1 give

    ||eta_i B f||_H<=4 Gamma_i ||f||_H.                       (6)

The product tests a_l eta_i phi have the parity needed for Hardy. No uncontrolled constant mode is introduced.

#### Insert the weight difference

Set s=11/5, delta=2/5 and F(X,Y)=w_R(X)/w_R(Y)-1. For j>=i+5, on the enlarged source annulus and the output annulus,

    |F|+|Y||grad_Y F|
      <=2^16 (r_j/r_i)^s min((r_j/R)^delta,1).                (7)

To verify this, the weight ratio is at most (8r_j/r_i)^s. If r_j<R, its logarithm is at most 8s(r_j/R)^2 and its Y derivative contributes at most 16s(r_j/R)^2 times that ratio. If r_j>=R, use the ratio itself. Since s<3 and delta<2, 24s 8^s<2^16 gives (7). The ratio is radial in Y, so the parity cancellation used in (4) is preserved.

For i>=j+5 the ratio is at most 1, and

    |F|+|Y||grad_Y F|<=2^7 min((r_i/R)^delta,1).               (8)

The same elementary logarithmic and derivative bounds prove (8). Applying (7)-(8) in the separated-kernel proof, with an extra factor 2 to cover the differentiated weight, and using Gamma_i<=2 C_rho r_i^-delta, bounds each separated block of D_R by

    2^32 C_rho R^-delta 2^(-epsilon |i-j|),
    epsilon=3-s-delta=2/5.                                  (9)

For the inward-source direction the actual exponent is 1, so (9) is weaker and valid.

For |i-j|<=4 take the constant w_i=w_R(r_i) and decompose the commutator as

    eta_i (w_R/w_i) B[(w_i/w_R-1)eta_j g]
      +eta_i(w_R/w_i-1)B[eta_j g].                           (10)

On the enlarged source annulus, r_j/4<=r<=4r_j, its radius relative to r_i lies between 1/64 and 64. Put tau=min((r_i/R)^2,1). Direct differentiation gives

    |w_i/w_R-1|+r|grad(w_i/w_R)|<=2^33 tau.

For r_i<R this follows from |log(w_i/w_R)|<=6144(r_i/R)^2, a ratio bound 64^3, and the derivative bound 3*4096*64^3(r_i/R)^2. For r_i>=R the same assertion follows from the uniform ratio bound. Localizing with zeta_j makes its H^-1 multiplication norm at most 2^35 tau.

On A_i, |w_R/w_i|<=8 and r|grad(w_R/w_i)|<=24, so multiplication by eta_i(w_R/w_i)a has norm at most 64 Gamma_i. The second term in (10) has a still smaller bound: |w_R/w_i-1|+r|grad(w_R/w_i)|<=256 tau on A_i. Thus each neighboring block is bounded by

    2^42 Gamma_i tau <=2^43 C_rho R^-delta.                   (11)

#### Sum the blocks

The nine neighboring diagonals in (11) have total majorant below 2^47 C_rho R^-delta. The two separated tails in (9) have total majorant at most

    2^33/(1-2^-epsilon) C_rho R^-delta <2^36 C_rho R^-delta,

since epsilon=2/5>1/4 and 1-2^-1/4>1/8. The l2 norm of the scalar convolution majorant is at most its l1 norm. Combining it with localization constants 4 and 6 in (2)-(3) gives a bound strictly below 2^53 C_rho R^-delta. This proves (1).

The same block proof without the difference factor proves boundedness of w_R B w_R^-1 on H for each finite R: the outer-source exponent is 3-s=4/5>0. Thus (1) is a commutator estimate between two well-defined bounded operators, not merely a formal cancellation.

#### Scope

All estimates are for the specified parity space and the canonical Riesz velocity. The cubic outer-source factor depends on parity. An unrestricted weighted Riesz theorem with the same exponent is not asserted. No numerical approximation enters (1).

### P6.4. A weighted fixed-exponent inverse admitting the growing checkpoint residual

#### Theorem

Let rho_bar be either exact checkpoint 88 or 131, reconstructed from the read-only source as in section P1.1. Let c be its exact exponent and Ubar its canonical velocity. Put

    R=2^200, w_R=(1+r^2/R^2)^(-11/10),
    ||h||_(L,R)=||w_R h||_(homogeneous H^-1).

Let X_(L,R) be the completion of the smooth compact parity core in this norm. The fixed-exponent operator

    L_fix h=(cX+Ubar).grad h-h+U[h].grad rho_bar

has a bijective transport-generator realization on X_(L,R), and

    ||L_fix^-1 f||_(L,R)<=5||f||_(L,R).                       (1)

The two checkpoints' unnormalized residuals belong to X_(L,R), because their leading powers 2/c-1 are less than 1/5. Their leading angular perturbations, scaling direction and exponent-logarithm directions do not belong. The huge radius makes (1) a rigorous existence-of-an-inverse result; it does not give a useful nonlinear residual bound.

#### Coefficient hypotheses

The proof uses 9/5<c<37/20, global M>=19/5 I, and the following bounds, with delta=2/5:

    C_rho=sup r^delta(|grad rho_bar|+r|D^2rho_bar|)<=2^16,
    C_U=sup r^(delta-1)|Ubar|<=2^5,
    C_DU=sup r^delta|DUbar|<=2^5,
    C_D2U=sup r^(1+delta)|D^2Ubar|<=2^15.                      (2)

The matrix and unweighted derivative certificates are already established. The independent script certificate file weighted_background_bounds.py checks (2) by combining those bounds on r<=100 with exact Fourier sectors and a rigorous binomial tail on r>=100. Its JSON files contain the input hashes and all intermediate bounds. The certification argument is detailed below.

#### Exact energy and radial transport weight

For g=w_R h, phi=(-Delta)^-1 g, q=grad phi, set

    b=V.grad log w_R=b0+b1,
    b0=-(11/5)c t, t=r^2/(R^2+r^2),
    b1=-(11/5) Ubar.X/(R^2+r^2).

The exact identity is

    -<w_R L_fix h,phi>
      =integral q^T(M+bI)q -(1/2)integral Delta b phi^2
        -<D_R g,phi>,                                      (3)

where D_R is the commutator in section P6.3. This includes every weight term.

The radial angular-Poincare inequality is especially useful here: for every nonnegative radial a(r),

    integral a(r) phi^2 <= integral r^2 a(r)|q|^2.               (4)

It follows from the circle Poincare inequality at each radius. It is stronger than applying the global Hardy inequality and then taking unrelated extrema.

For r<=R, Delta b0<=0, b0>=-(11/10)c, so the M+b0 part of (3), including Delta b0, is bounded below by 19/5-(11/10)c>2/5.

For r>=R, M>=(2c+1-(C_DU+C_rho)R^-delta)I. Also

    (1/2)r^2 Delta b0=2(11/5)c t(1-t)(2t-1)>=0.

Using (4), the net scalar cost is at most (11/5)c times

    t+2t(1-t)(2t-1)=-4t^3+6t^2-t
       <=1/2+2sqrt(6)/9<21/20.

Consequently this region contributes at least

    1-(31/100)c-(C_DU+C_rho)R^-delta
       >=2/5-(C_DU+C_rho)R^-delta.                           (5)

The pointwise M lower bound is radial here, so applying (4) does not require comparing phi/r and q pointwise.

#### The velocity part of the weight

Write P=Ubar.X and D=R^2+r^2. The definitions in (2) imply

    |P|<=C_U r^(2-delta),
    |grad P|<=(C_U+C_DU)r^(1-delta),
    |Delta P|<=sqrt(2) C_D2U r^-delta.

The last identity uses Delta P=X.Delta Ubar+2 div Ubar and div Ubar=0. Expanding Delta(P/D) gives

    Delta(P/D)=(Delta P)/D-4X.grad P/D^2
                  +P(-4/D^2+8r^2/D^3).

For m=1,2,3, r^(2m-delta)/(R^2+r^2)^m<=R^-delta. It follows that the total energy loss from b1 and Delta b1 is at most

    (11/5)(9C_U+2C_DU+C_D2U/sqrt(2))R^-delta ||q||^2.          (6)

Here the ordinary parity Hardy inequality controls the nonradial Delta b1 term.

The commutator theorem gives an additional loss 2^53 C_rho R^-delta||q||^2. Combining (3)-(6) proves coercivity at least

    2/5-R^-delta [C_DU+C_rho
       +(11/5)(9C_U+2C_DU+C_D2U/sqrt(2))+2^53 C_rho].         (7)

For R=2^200 and (2), the subtracted quantity is less than 1/5. Thus the final margin is at least 1/5, giving the constant 5 in (1).

#### Existence of the generator and surjectivity

The smooth complete Lipschitz flow Phi_t of V preserves parity, fixes the origin and has two-sided finite exponential distortion of distances. On the compact core the transport semigroup is

    T_t h=e^-t h(Phi_t X).

After multiplication by w_R its action on g is multiplication by w_R(X)/w_R(Phi_t X), followed by composition with Phi_t. For each finite time this ratio and r times its gradient are bounded, by the flow distortion bounds and the logarithmic derivative of w_R. The parity Hardy inequality therefore proves boundedness on H^-1. Approximation from the compact core gives strong continuity. The usual resolvent-integral approximation by finite Riemann sums of transported compact core functions proves that this core is a graph core.

The weighted coupling w_R B w_R^-1 is bounded on H^-1 by the final paragraph of section P6.3. Bounded perturbation therefore supplies a C0 semigroup with generator w_R L_fix w_R^-1. The exact core inequality (7) extends to its generator domain. Differentiating the squared norm along generator-domain solutions gives decay at least exp(-t/5). By density the same bound holds on the whole space.

The operator -integral_0^infinity exp(t L_fix)dt consequently converges in operator norm, has bound 5, and is both a right and a left inverse on the strong generator domain. This proves surjectivity as well as injectivity. The unweighted inverse and this weighted inverse are not asserted to agree on every common forcing unless their solutions belong to a common uniqueness class.

#### Certification of (2)

On r<=100 use |grad rho_bar|<=11sqrt(2), |D^2rho_bar|<=77, |DUbar|<=14/5, |D^2Ubar|<=35, and Ubar(0)=0. The last two bounds imply |Ubar(X)|<=(14/5)r. Multiplication by the relevant powers of 100 gives the local bounds in the JSON.

For r>=100 expand each exact potential generator in r^-2 through q=6 and differentiate the resulting angular Fourier polynomials exactly. For an order d=3,4,5 derivative, every omitted coefficient is bounded by

    binom(q+25,q)(2q+32)^d

 times the absolute input coefficient and r^(-2q). The bound 26 on |p_j-k| and the angular frequency bound 18 justify this majorant. Starting at q=7, its successive ratio is at most

    ((q+26)/(q+1))*((2q+34)/(2q+32))^d /100^2 <1,

and decreases with q. A geometric tail is therefore valid uniformly outside 100. Exact angular coefficient sums bound each differentiated sector; Euclidean sums give the vector and tensor bounds. Finally multiply by 100^(2/5-(1-gamma)), which is valid because 1-gamma>2/5. All arithmetic entering (2) and (7) is enclosed with 384-bit Arb. The computation reads our exact source reconstruction and never imports the numerical evaluator.

#### Limitations

The admitted correction exponent is 1/5. The center and nonlinear high regularity are not supplied by this low inverse. A change of the weight radius preserves the underlying weighted space but changes equivalence constants substantially. In particular the norm of the growing residual for R=2^200 can be enormous. No a posteriori smallness condition or nonlinear existence theorem follows from (1).

#### Small Lipschitz velocity perturbations

The same low realization has a uniform estimate under a divergence-free parity-preserving perturbation W of the transport field, provided W(0)=0 and ||DW||_infinity<=1/120. No third derivative of W is required for the energy estimate. Write b_W=W.grad log w_R. The extra transport contribution is

    integral q^T sym(DW)q + integral b_W|q|^2
       -(1/2) integral Delta b_W phi^2.

Interpret the last term weakly as integral phi grad b_W.q. Since |W|<=r||DW||_infinity,

    ||b_W||_infinity<=s||DW||_infinity,
    ||r grad b_W||_infinity<=4s||DW||_infinity, s=11/5.

The total absolute loss is at most (1+5s)||DW||_infinity ||q||^2=12||DW||_infinity||q||^2. Starting with the certified margin 1/5 therefore leaves at least 1/10. The perturbed complete Lipschitz transport flow and the same bounded coupling give an inverse with norm at most 10. Smooth W can first be used on the core; C1 Lipschitz W follows by the same weak energy identity and flow construction. This is a low-norm result only. A high solvability theorem for W=U[k] is not supplied.

### P6.5. Weighted low inverses for three fixed growth classes

#### Statement and dependencies

Let the background be either exact checkpoint 88 or 131. Use the canonical parity realization, coefficient bounds and graph-core construction of section P6.4. For s in {1,2,11/5}, let

    w_(R,s)=(1+r^2/R^2)^(-s/2),
    X_(R,s)=completion of the compact parity core in ||w_(R,s)h||_(Hdot^-1).

Define

    m_1=27/10, m_2=4/5, m_(11/5)=2/5,
    C(s)=C_DU+C_rho+s(9C_U+2C_DU+C_D2U/sqrt(2))+2^53 C_rho,

where C_rho=2^16, C_U=C_DU=32 and C_D2U=2^15 are the independently certified common bounds. If R>=1 and

    mu=m_s-C(s)R^(-2/5)>0,                                  (1)

then L_fix is bijective on its transport-generator domain in X_(R,s), with inverse norm at most 1/mu. In particular, at R=2^179, the following rounded margins and inverse bounds hold for both backgrounds:

| s | growth threshold s-2 | proved margin | inverse bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | -1 | 5/2 | 2/5 |
| 2 | 0 | 3/5 | 5/3 |
| 11/5 | 1/5 | 1/5 | 5 |

These statements concern the original background operator. Its original residual belongs only to the last of these three spaces. A repaired background requires new coefficient certificates before using this theorem with that background.

#### Proof

Every bound in section P6.3 remains valid, with the same constant 2^53, when 0<s<=11/5. Weight ratios and derivative bounds decrease when the upper exponent bound is decreased. The outer-source decay exponent becomes 3-s-2/5>=2/5; the inner-source exponent remains at least 1. Thus

    ||w_(R,s) B w_(R,s)^-1-B|| <=2^53 C_rho R^(-2/5).        (2)

The radial transport calculation is identical with s replacing 11/5. On r<=R it gives the margin 19/5-sc/2. On r>=R, circle Poincare bounds the positive Laplacian term by the polynomial maximum 21/20 and gives

    2c+1-(21/20)sc-(C_DU+C_rho)R^(-2/5).                   (3)

For 9/5<c<37/20, the two unperturbed radial margins are both greater than m_s for the three listed exponents. Explicitly, their lower bounds are

    s=1: min(23/8,271/100)>27/10;
    s=2: min(39/20,163/200)>4/5;
    s=11/5: min(353/200,853/2000)>2/5.

The velocity part of the weight costs at most s(9C_U+2C_DU+C_D2U/sqrt(2))R^(-2/5), exactly as in section P6.4. Combining this with (2)-(3) proves (1). The same transport flow and bounded coupling construct the generator and its exponentially decaying semigroup. The convergent semigroup integral supplies both left and right inverses.

For R=2^179 the common error is less than 1/5. The displayed margins follow by subtracting 1/5 from m_s. The independent Arb check in certificate file low_inverse_family.py evaluates the actual error and checks each strict inequality. The threshold for the original s=11/5 argument to put the error below half its baseline 2/5 lies strictly between 2^178 and 2^179. This is a threshold of this sufficient bound, not a lower bound on the true necessary radius.

#### Interpretation of the growth threshold

A cut-off nonzero homogeneous tail r^p Theta belongs to X_(R,s) exactly when p<s-2, apart from polynomial ambiguities excluded by the parity completion. Therefore s=2 is appropriate for a residual with negative power after removal of the first residual sector; s=1 requires all remaining powers to be below -1. The large radius has not been made practically useful by lowering s. It establishes existence of the low inverse and identifies the quantitative weakness of the present commutator bound.

### P6.6. The far-field threshold is strict

#### Statement

Let 0<gamma<1, c=1/gamma, and let a smooth parity background satisfy

    |Ubar(X)| <= C <r>^gamma,
    |grad rhobar(X)| <= C <r>^(gamma-1).

Let Z_sigma be the completion of compact even-x, odd-y functions in

    ||h||_(Z_sigma)=||<r>^(-1-sigma) h||_2.

On its transport-generator domain, the operator

    L_fix h=(cX+Ubar).grad h-h+U[h].grad rhobar

is not bounded below in Z_gamma. In particular, the equality case sigma=gamma cannot be included in a bounded inverse claim. This corrects the non-strict inequality in an earlier draft formulation. The positive far symbol 1-c sigma requires sigma<gamma.

The proof applies to both exact checkpoints. It is a statement about the specified weighted L2 realization, not an assertion that every possible space with an additional radiation condition fails.

#### A weighted velocity lemma

For -3<sigma<1 the canonical U is bounded on Z_sigma, with the parity of each component understood. This fact can be proved directly without a general weighted singular-integral theorem.

Decompose the plane into a central ball and dyadic annuli A_i of radius r_i, using radial cutoffs with bounded overlap. On nearby annuli, the scalar-to-vector unweighted L2 multiplier norm of U is at most 1; the weight varies by a bounded factor. For separated annuli use

    |K(Z)| <= 1/(2pi |Z|^2),  |DK(Z)| <= 2/(pi |Z|^3).

For an outer source r_j>>r_i, subtract K(-Y), whose integral against a radial cutoff of h is zero by parity. The resulting L2 block bound, after multiplying output and input by their weights, is

    C (r_i/r_j)^(1-sigma).

For an inner source r_j<<r_i, subtract K(X), using the zero integral of the odd source. The block bound is

    C (r_j/r_i)^(3+sigma).

The central-ball cases obey the same bounds with its radius replaced by 1. Both geometric series converge exactly in the stated interval. Schur summation and bounded overlap prove boundedness. The local identity term in U_2 is harmless. The construction extends the canonical compact-core velocity to Z_sigma; no harmonic velocity is added.

For clarity, the unweighted outer-source estimate is C r_i^2 r_j^-2 ||h_j||_2: one factor r_i comes from the kernel difference and the other from the output area's square root. The inner-source estimate is C r_j^2 r_i^-2 ||h_j||_2. Converting ||h_j||_2 to r_j^(1+sigma)||h_j||_(Z_sigma) gives the displayed exponents.

#### Approximate null sequence

Choose a nonzero smooth function chi compactly supported in (0,1), and an allowed nonzero angular sine Theta. For L>=2 set

    h_L(r,theta)=L^(-1/2) r^gamma Theta(theta)
                 chi((log r-L)/L).

It is smooth, compactly supported away from zero and has the required parity. Its support lies in e^L<r<e^(2L). Direct polar integration gives

    ||h_L||_(Z_gamma) -> ||Theta||_2 ||chi||_2 >0.

The same calculation gives a uniform bound on ||<r>^(-1-gamma) r grad h_L||_2. The pure dilation part satisfies

    (c r partial_r-1)h_L
       =c L^(-3/2) r^gamma Theta chi'((log r-L)/L),

so its Z_gamma norm is O(L^-1). The perturbing transport term has norm O(exp(-(1-gamma)L)) because |Ubar|/r has that upper bound on the support.

It remains to estimate the nonlocal coupling. Put delta=1-gamma and T=exp(L/2). On r>=T the background gradient is O(T^-delta), and the weighted velocity lemma gives

    ||1_(r>=T) U[h_L].grad rhobar||_(Z_gamma)
       <= C T^-delta ||h_L||_(Z_gamma) ->0.

On r<T, the source is separated from the observation point. The same parity subtraction in the kernel yields

    |U[h_L](X)| <= C r L^(-1/2) exp(-delta L)/delta.

Indeed its radial integral is bounded by integral_(e^L)^infinity R^(gamma-2)dR. The gradient of the background is bounded globally, while

    ||1_(r<T) <r>^(-1-gamma) r||_2 <= C T^(1-gamma).

The inner contribution is therefore O(L^-1/2 exp(-delta L/2)). Altogether

    ||L_fix h_L||_(Z_gamma) ->0,
    liminf ||h_L||_(Z_gamma)>0.

This proves failure of a lower bound and hence failure of a bounded inverse. The sequence also converges weakly to zero because its support escapes every compact set. Consequently adding finitely many bounded scalar constraints cannot remove this obstruction: every such functional tends to zero on the sequence.

#### Scope

This is an endpoint counterexample, not a counterexample in the strict subcritical interval selected for the current project. It explains why a merely absent exact power eigenfunction is insufficient: arbitrarily long logarithmic annuli produce approximate null vectors at the threshold.

### P6.7. Why a direct weighted-potential test does not replace the commutator estimate

#### Exact identity

Let h=-Delta phi with smooth compactly supported phi, let v be smooth positive, and let the coefficients have the conventions of the fixed-c problem. Put q=grad phi, A=[[rho_y,-rho_x/2],[-rho_x/2,0]], D=div(vV). Integration by parts gives

    -integral L_fix(-Delta phi) v phi
      = integral v q^T [(1+c+(1/2)V.grad log v)I
                         +sym DV+sym(V tensor grad log v)+A] q
        -(1/2)integral [Delta(D+v)+div div(vA)] phi^2.           (1)

Here div V=2c and sym uses the average of a matrix and its transpose. Every term is retained. This identity is local in phi, but its principal matrix differs from that of the Hilbert norm ||w h||_(H^-1).

To verify(1), the transport term is integral V.grad Delta phi v phi. Moving its first derivative and then the Laplacian gives

    integral [(D/2)|q|^2+q^T sym D(vV) q]
      -(1/2)integral Delta D phi^2.

The -Delta phi term gives integral v|q|^2-(1/2)integral Delta v phi^2. The coupling term is -integral v phi A_ij phi_ij, yielding integral v q^T A q-(1/2)integral div div(vA) phi^2. Summing proves (1).

#### Failure at the far field

For V=cX, A=0 and v=r^(-2s), the principal matrix is

    (1+2c-sc)I-2sc e_r tensor e_r.

Its radial eigenvalue is 1+2c-3sc. This is negative at the s=11/5 weight used to admit the growing residual, and at s=2. Smooth rapidly oscillating potentials supported in a small ball around a distant point, oscillating in its radial direction, make the phi^2 term negligible relative to the gradient term. Their reflected parity copies have disjoint supports and preserve the sign. Thus (1) cannot give a positive gradient-energy bound in these cases.

The reason is a concrete algebraic one: the pairing integral h v phi is not the symmetric evolution pairing of a Hilbert energy when v is nonconstant. The extra sym(V tensor grad log v) term cannot be dropped. The successful conjugated H^-1 identity avoids this term at the price of a nonlocal weight commutator.

### P6.8. A weighted negative-order bilinear transport estimate

#### Statement

Let H_minus denote the homogeneous H^-1 parity spaces used in section P6.3. Scalar inputs are even in x and odd in y; the two velocity components have their induced parities. For R>0 and 0<=s<=11/5, set

    w=(1+r^2/R^2)^(-s/2),  ||h||_L=||w h||_(H_minus).

Let g be a parity function with

    Z(g)=||grad g||_infinity
         +15 (||D^2g||_2^2+||r D^3g||_2^2)^(1/2) < infinity.     (1)

Weak derivatives suffice. The canonical velocity and the product extend from smooth compact inputs, and

    ||w U[h]||_(vector H_minus) <= 2^35 ||h||_L,              (2)
    ||U[h].grad g||_L <= 2^35 Z(g) ||h||_L.                  (3)

The constants are uniform in R. They are deliberately coarse; the result establishes the mapping property, not useful numerical smallness.

For the weighted high norm of section P6.1, with sigma<=1 and 0<a<1, define the equivalent strengthened norm

    ||g||_(H*)=(||g||_H^2+||grad g||_infinity^2)^(1/2).

Whenever that high space has the stated gradient embedding, (3) gives the fully explicit estimate

    ||U[h].grad g||_L <=2^39 ||h||_L ||g||_(H*).              (4)

Here (4) uses only the displayed norm, not an uncomputed embedding constant. The high ball with this strengthened norm is still closed in the low metric. This supplies the low bilinear hypothesis of the abstract quasilinear theorem for these spaces; high solvability remains separate.

#### Weighted velocity on H_minus

Use the radial partition eta_i, enlarged cutoffs zeta_i and localization constants 4 and 6 of section P6.3. Set w_i=w(r_i). The same kernel estimates, with the multiplier coefficient a omitted, give the unweighted separated block bounds

    9000 (r_i/r_j)^3, j>=i+5;
    2000 (r_j/r_i), i>=j+5.

They hold for the vector H_minus norm: the Fourier symbol has scalar-to-vector norm at most 1, and each output component has an odd coordinate for Hardy. The kernel cancellation at the outer source follows from parity and the inner-source cancellation from zero integral.

For j>=i+5, the weight ratio is at most (8r_j/r_i)^s and its logarithmic source derivative is at mosts/r. In the differentiated dual kernel, a factor 2^12(r_j/r_i)^s safely covers both effects. Thus the weighted outer block is at most

    2^26 (r_i/r_j)^(3-s).

For i>=j+5, the ratio is at most 1; the derivative factor is below 4. The block is at most 2^14(r_j/r_i).

For |i-j|<=4, write the block as

    eta_i(w/w_i) U[(w_i/w) eta_j f],  f=w h.

On the enlarged source annulus, r/r_i lies in [1/64,64]. The ratio w_i/w is at most 64^(11/5)<2^14, and the radial multiplier norm after multiplication by zeta_j is at most (5/2+s) times that ratio, hence below 2^17. On the output annulus the multiplier eta_i(w/w_i) has norm below 2^6. The vector Riesz norm is at most 1. Every neighboring block is therefore below 2^23.

The neighboring diagonals sum to 9*2^23. Since 3-s>=4/5 and 1-2^(-4/5)>1/4, the outer tail is below 2^28; the inner tail is below 2^15. Their total is below 2^29. Multiplication by the localization factors 4*6 gives a bound below 2^34; the rounded constant 2^35 in (2) is valid. This also constructs the extension, and the local identity term of U_2 is included in the neighboring-block estimate.

#### A cylinder Sobolev inequality

For a scalar or vector F on C=R_t times S1_theta, with angular period 2pi,

    ||F||_(L4(C)) <= sqrt(6) ||F||_(H1(C)).                  (5)

A direct proof starts from the planar inequality

    ||f||_4^4 <=2 ||f||_2^2 ||grad f||_2^2.

For compact f, the fundamental theorem of calculus bounds f^2 separately along each coordinate line. Multiplying these two bounds, integrating, and applying Cauchy-Schwarz proves this inequality. The same argument applies to |f| for vector f.

Extend F periodically in theta and multiply by a Lipschitz cutoff equal to 1 on [0,2pi], supported in [-2pi,4pi], with derivative at most 1/(2pi). The planar L2 norm is at mostsqrt(3)||F||_2. Its squared gradient norm is at most 6||grad F||_2^2+6/(4pi^2)||F||_2^2<=6||F||_(H1)^2. The planar inequality gives (5). Density removes compactness and smoothness restrictions.

For a parity test function phi, set t=log r. Circle Poincare gives

    ||phi||_(L2(C))^2 <= ||partial_theta phi||_(L2(C))^2,
    ||partial_t phi||_2^2+||partial_theta phi||_2^2
       =||grad phi||_(L2(R^2))^2.

It follows from (5) that

    ||phi||_(L4(C)) <=sqrt(12)||grad phi||_2.                 (6)

Apply(5) also to the Cartesian tensor F=r D^2g. Direct differentiation gives

    ||F||_(H1(C))^2 <=3||D^2g||_2^2+2||r D^3g||_2^2.

Consequently Holder's inequality on the cylinder gives

    ||D^2g phi||_(L2(R^2))
      =||F phi||_(L2(C))
      <=sqrt(216) (||D^2g||_2^2+||r D^3g||_2^2)^(1/2)
                     ||grad phi||_2.                       (7)

The elementary bound sqrt(216)<15 proves

    (sum_j ||grad(partial_j g phi)||_2^2)^(1/2)
         <= Z(g)||grad phi||_2.                             (8)

Products partial_j g phi have the correct velocity dual parities, so every use of Hardy and duality is legitimate.

#### Product estimate and high norm

Pair w U[h].grad g with phi. Apply vector H_minus duality, (8), and (2). This gives (3). No derivative of the weight appears here because it has already been incorporated in the weighted velocity estimate.

For the weights omega_2=<r>^(1-sigma) and omega_3=r^a <r>^(2-sigma-a), one has

    omega_2>=1,  r/omega_3<=1

when sigma<=1 and 0<a<1. Hence

    ||D^2g||_2^2+||r D^3g||_2^2 <=||g||_H^2.

By Cauchy-Schwarz, Z(g)<=sqrt(226)||g||_(H*)<16||g||_(H*), proving(4).

The space with norm H* is complete as an intersection of the original Hilbert high space and W1,infinity modulo the already controlled function representative. A bounded H* sequence converging in the low metric has a weak high-space subsequence and weak-star bounded gradients. Distributional uniqueness identifies both limits, and lower semicontinuity preserves the H* ball. This proves the required low closedness.

#### Scope

The estimate uses high regularity of the second argument and low regularity of the first. It does not assert a same-Holder quadratic bound and does not remove the derivative loss refuted earlier. It is compatible with the quasilinear frozen-velocity formulation. Uniform high solvability and an effective residual bound are still needed for existence.

### P6.9. Certificates for the weighted high principal matrices

#### Exact setting

Use the exact accepted checkpoint 131, c=4076476460239181/2251799813685248, gamma=1/c, delta=1-gamma, and sigma=1/5. For real derivative order k and radius Rk>0 put

    omega_k=(1+r^2/Rk^2)^((k-1-sigma)/2),
    M_k=(1+c+V.grad log omega_k)I-k sym(DV)+A,
    V=cX+Ubar, A=[[rho_y,-rho_x/2],[-rho_x/2,0]].

The completed certificates prove M_k>=1/2 I globally at (k,Rk)=(1,1),(2,1/2). There are 131 and 201 leaves respectively, and all leaves were reconstructed at 384-bit precision in an independent tree audit. The optional noninteger target (21/10,1/2) has not been certified. It is a principal-matrix certificate only. Full weighted energy bounds require the lower terms in the companion proof.

#### Exact compactification

Set t=r^2/(1+r^2), z=cos(2theta), w=(1-t)^(delta/2), and d_k(t)=Rk^2+(1-Rk^2)t. The exact potential representation gives

    chi_22=sum_(j=0)^3 w^(j+1) P_22,j(t,z),
    chi_04=sum_(j=0)^3 w^(j+1) P_04,j(t,z),
    chi_31=sin(2theta) sum_(j=0)^3 w^(j+1) P_31,j(t,z),
    chi_13=sin(2theta) sum_(j=0)^3 w^(j+1) P_13,j(t,z).

Every P is an exact rational polynomial, as in the independent unweighted matrix certificate. A third derivative multiplied by x or y, divided by Rk^2+r^2, has the same radial factor w^(j+1)/d_k(t). In particular

    Ubar.X/(Rk^2+r^2)=sum_(j=0)^3 w^(j+1) P_rad,j(t,z)/d_k(t).

To construct P_rad, differentiate each potential generator three times, form -x chi_xyy+y chi_xxy by the elementary products of sin(theta),cos(theta) with its angular modes, and collect the power t^(k_generator-1+l). No numerical evaluation or fitted coefficient enters these polynomials.

Write tau=k-1-sigma and b=1+(1-k)c. Multiplying M_k by the strictly positive d_k gives a polynomial matrix in t,z,w, with off-diagonal factor sin(2theta). Its common scalar part is

    b d_k(t)+tau c t.

Its remaining entries are the exact sums over j of w^(j+1) times

    upper diagonal: d_k[(k-1)P_22,j-P_04,j]+tau P_rad,j,
    lower diagonal: -k d_k P_22,j+tau P_rad,j,
    off diagonal: d_k[(1-k)P_31,j+(1+k)P_13,j]/2.

Subtracting (1/2)d_k I before certification proves the desired original matrix bound. The denominator is positive on the entire compact rectangle, including t=0 and t=1.

#### Continuum enclosure and audit

The script converts each rational polynomial to tensor Bernstein coefficients on [0,1]x[-1,1], subdivides with exact dyadic boxes, and encloses w on each box with Arb. A further degree-four Bernstein transformation retains cancellations among the four powers of w. The smallest eigenvalue is bounded below using enclosed diagonal lower bounds and the off-diagonal absolute upper bound. The polynomial scalar diagonal is included before taking the enclosure.

A successful certificate covers the full compactified quadrant, hence the plane by parity. Its JSON records the source coefficient hash, exact k,Rk,sigma,target, every leaf path and box, and every Arb lower bound. An independent Cartesian field evaluation checks the formula at rational points; a separate certificate audit reconstructs every leaf and verifies its bounds and the exact binary partition. These point checks supplement, and do not replace, the continuum Bernstein proof.

#### Auxiliary third-order growth certificate

With k=3, sigma=6/5 and Rk=1/2, the weight is again(1+4r^2)^(2/5). The same exact construction certifies M3_aux>=-5/4 I. The 282-leaf adaptive certificate and its 384-bit full-tree recomputation are in state131_high_symbol_k3_adaptive_auxiliary.json and high_symbol_certificate_audit.json. This auxiliary matrix supports interpolation with a growing third-order norm in section P7.4. It is not a dissipative third-order bound.

### P6.10. A fixed-exponent weighted H2 inverse admitting the original residual

#### Statement and current dependencies

This proof uses three numerical inputs for the exact accepted checkpoint 131: the weighted low inverse in section P6.5, the coefficient bounds below, and M_1,M_2>=1/2 I from section P6.9. Both principal-matrix certificates are complete and their full trees have passed independent 384-bit recomputation. An exact Gaussian integral test independently confirms identity(6). No nonlinear existence claim follows from this theorem alone.

Set sigma=1/5, R=2^179, and

    w=(1+r^2/R^2)^(-11/10),
    omega_0=<r>^(-6/5), omega_1=<r>^(-1/5),
    omega_2=(1+4r^2)^(2/5).

On the compact even-x, odd-y core define

    L(h)=||w h||_(Hdot^-1), P_j(h)=||omega_j D^j h||_2,
    E_1(h)^2=P_1(h)^2+2^112 L(h)^2,
    E_2(h)^2=P_2(h)^2+2^72 E_1(h)^2.                          (1)

Let the spaces be the completions of this core, and let L_fix be the generator-domain realization of (cX+Ubar).grad h-h+U[h].grad rhobar. Then L_fix is bijective onto either completed space, with

    E_1(L_fix^-1 f)<=10 E_1(f),
    E_2(L_fix^-1 f)<=20 E_2(f).                             (2)

These inverses agree with the weighted low inverse on common forcing. The original checkpoint residual belongs to both spaces, since its leading exponent 2gamma-1 is less than 1/5. The enormous coefficients in (1) make this an existence theorem for a linear inverse, not a useful nonlinear smallness result. The high space controls the density in weighted local C^alpha for every 0<alpha<1, but it does not supply the center strain trace or a bounded gradient.

#### Coefficient inputs

The required global bounds, with full Frobenius tensor norms, are

    ||grad rhobar||_infinity <=16,
    ||<r> D^2rhobar||_infinity <=2^13,
    ||<r>^2 D^3rhobar||_infinity <=2^20,
    ||<r> D^2Ubar||_infinity <=2^12.                         (3)

On r<=100 these follow from the already certified bounds 16,77,94,35, respectively. On r>=100, the exact potential expansion throughq=10 and the component tail bounds of section P3.4 give component bounds M_d+T_d, d=4,5,6. Multiplying by 2^(1+j/2) for D^j rho and 2^((j+1)/2) for D^j U, and by the appropriate powers of r, proves (3). Every exterior exponent after the displayed weight is gamma-1<0, so the maximum of this bound occurs at 100. The verification script records the Arb inequalities. No pointwise sample is used in (3).

#### Weighted Riesz bounds

The scalar-to-vector unweighted L2 norm of U is at most 1. For any real beta with |beta|<=4/5 and any R0>0,

    ||(1+r^2/R0^2)^(beta/2) U[f]||_2
        <=256 ||(1+r^2/R0^2)^(beta/2) f||_2.                  (4)

No parity is needed. To prove this, scale R0 to 1 and partition into disjoint annuli A_i={2^i<=r<2^(i+1)}, i in Z. Neighboring blocks |i-j|<=1 have norm at most 4: the weights vary by at most 4^|beta| and the full multiplier has norm 1. For |i-j|>=2 the kernel bound |K(Z)|<=1/(2pi|Z|^2), the separation distance, and the exact area 3pi 2^(2i) give an unweighted block norm at most 6*2^(-|i-j|). The weights change this to at most 12*2^(-(1-|beta|)|i-j|). Since 1-2^(-1/5)>1/8, the sum over both separated tails is below 192 and the three neighboring blocks add at most 12. The matrix Schur bound is therefore below 204<256. The identity part of U_2 is already included in neighboring blocks.

For parity f one additionally has

    P_0(U[f])<=2048 P_0(f).                                (5)

For outer source blocks, subtract K(-Y), whose integral against f restricted to the radial annulus vanishes. For inner source blocks subtract K(X), since the restricted f has zero integral. The derivative bound |DK|<=2/(pi|Z|^3) gives an unweighted block norm at most 96*2^(-2|i-j|). With beta=-6/5, outer blocks are at most 288*2^(-4(j-i)/5); inner blocks are at most 96*2^(-2(i-j)). Neighboring blocks have weight ratio at most 4^(6/5)<6. Their total row and column sums are below 18+1152+128<2048. This proves (5), including the canonical extension from the compact core.

Apply(4) with beta=-1/5 to derivatives weighted by omega_1, and with beta=4/5,R0=1/2 to derivatives weighted by omega_2. Vector and derivative tensor inputs are handled componentwise and then summed in squares, with the same operator constant.

#### Exact gradient form of the nonlocal top term

For a scalar compact smooth f, a=grad rhobar, v=omega^2 and b=v a, define

    J_v(f)=-sum_i integral b.U[partial_i f] partial_i f.

The exact identity is

    J_v(f)=integral v grad f^T A grad f
       +(1/2) integral [partial_xy b_1-partial_xx b_2] f^2
       +sum_i integral f (partial_i b).U[partial_i f].       (6)

Indeed U commutes with derivatives and Delta U[f]=(f_xy,-f_xx). Move partial_i from the second factor in J_v to b.U[partial_i f], sum i, and integrate the resulting f b_1 f_xy-f b_2 f_xx. This proves (6), including its signs. Since a is a gradient, the zero-order coefficient simplifies to

    partial_xy b_1-partial_xx b_2
      =v_xy rho_x-v_xx rho_y-v_x rho_xy+v_y rho_xx.           (7)

The third derivatives of rho cancel in (7). They must not be silently discarded in the other differentiated terms.

For either omega_1 or omega_2, direct differentiation gives

    |grad v|<=4v/<r>, |D^2v|_F<=16v/<r>^2.                    (8)

Also omega_k/omega_(k-1)<=a_k<r>, a_1=1,a_2=2. Equations(3),(7),(8) show that the f^2 error in (6) has absolute value at most

    a_k^2(8*16+2*2^13) ||omega_(k-1)f||_2^2,

and its last term is at most

    a_k(2^13+4*16)*256
      ||omega_(k-1)f||_2 ||omega_k grad f||_2.               (9)

All estimates use tensor norms and Cauchy-Schwarz, so they also apply after summing over the derivative tuples below.

#### First derivative energy and low interpolation

Differentiating transport once and adding (6) with f=h gives the exact principal matrix M_1. The remaining nonlocal term is U[h].D^2rho paired with omega_1^2 grad h. By (3),(5) it is bounded by 2^13*2048 P_0 P_1. With M_1>=1/2 I, (9) therefore yields the safely rounded bound

    -<grad L_fix h,omega_1^2 grad h>
       >=(1/2)P_1^2-2^25 P_0 P_1-2^15 P_0^2
       >=(3/8)P_1^2-2^52 P_0^2.                              (10)

The low norm controls P_0 after interpolation. Put a=omega_0^2/w. Since R>=1,

    a<=omega_1, |grad a|<=5 omega_0.

The negative-norm dual pairing gives

    P_0^2=<w h,a h><=L(P_1+5P_0),
    P_0^2<=epsilon P_1^2+(25+epsilon^-1)L^2                   (11)

for every epsilon>0. All tests have the correct parity. Taking epsilon=2^-55 in (10) gives

    -<grad L_fix h,omega_1^2 grad h>
       >=(1/4)P_1^2-2^108 L^2.                               (12)

The certified weighted low dissipation is at least (1/5)L^2. Adding 2^112 times that identity proves

    -<L_fix h,h>_(E1)>=(1/10)E_1(h)^2.                     (13)

Notice that (11) at epsilon=1 implies P_0^2<=P_1^2+26L^2<=E_1^2.

#### Second derivative energy

Group the ordered second derivatives by f=partial_j h. The top nonlocal term is sum_j J_v(partial_j h), with v=omega_2^2. Differentiating transport twice gives exactly the principal contribution M_2 and the additional D^2Ubar.grad h term. The other nonlocal terms are

    U[partial_i h].partial_j grad rho
      +U[partial_j h].partial_i grad rho
      +U[h].partial_ij grad rho.

The first two are bounded together by 4*2^13*256 P_1 P_2. The last is bounded by 2*2^20*2048 P_0 P_2. The lower transport term is bounded by 2*2^12 P_1 P_2. Combining these estimates with (9), using P_0,P_1<=E_1, and rounding upward gives

    -<D^2L_fix h,omega_2^2 D^2h>
       >=(1/2)P_2^2-2^33 E_1 P_2-2^17 E_1^2
       >=(1/4)P_2^2-2^67 E_1^2.                              (14)

Adding 2^72 times (13) proves

    -<L_fix h,h>_(E2)>=(1/20)E_2(h)^2.                     (15)

In particular every lower derivative and weight term has been accounted for. Pointwise principal positivity alone would not prove(13) or (15).

#### Realization, core and surjectivity

The complete smooth transport field V has linear growth and bounded DV. Moreover <r>D^2V is bounded by (3). Its flow Phi_t is a smooth diffeomorphism preserving parity, maps compact sets to compact sets, and for each bounded time interval satisfies <Phi_t(X)> comparable to<r>, D Phi_t bounded, and <r>D^2Phi_t bounded. The first two assertions follow from Gronwall; differentiating the flow equation twice and using <Phi_t> comparable to<r> proves the third. Consequently h -> exp(-t) h(Phi_t(X)) acts boundedly on both norms (1). It is strongly continuous by approximation with compact smooth functions and dominated convergence. The weighted low action is the same already constructed in section P6.5.

The nonlocal term B h=U[h].grad rho is bounded on either completed space: use the established low bound, (3)-(5), and the exact first and second derivative product rules displayed above. Its distributional action agrees with the canonical velocity. Thus the bounded perturbation theorem constructs consistent C0 semigroups on E_1 and E_2. Alternatively the usual convergent Duhamel series constructs them directly on bounded time intervals.

The compact parity core is invariant under the unperturbed transport semigroup. It is a graph core: approximate a resolvent integral by finite Riemann sums of transported core functions, then approximate its input by the dense core. A bounded perturbation preserves this graph-core property and does not change the generator domain. Therefore (13),(15) extend to the strong generator domains and give semigroup decay exp(-t/10), exp(-t/20).

The convergent integrals -integral_0^infinity exp(t L_fix)f dt give (2) and belong to the generator domains. The generator identity applied first to finite time integrals and then by closedness proves surjectivity. If L_fix h=0, its semigroup orbit is constant, while the decay forces h=0, proving injectivity. Agreement with the low inverse follows by the continuous injections and uniqueness there.

#### Holder control and remaining gap

On each dyadic annulus, rescale to a fixed enlarged annulus. The bounds P_0,P_1,P_2 control its H2 norm after multiplication by the common factor r^-sigma. The two-dimensional H2 Fourier difference estimate gives C^alpha control for every 0<alpha<1. On the central disk the same argument uses the inhomogeneous local H2 norm. Thus the norm

    ||h||_(C^alpha_ad)=||h||_(C^alpha(B2))
       +sup_(j>=0) 2^(-j sigma)
          [||h||_(Linfinity(A_j))+2^(j alpha)[h]_(C^alpha(A_j))]

is bounded by C_alpha E_2(h), with A_j={2^j<=r<=2^(j+1)}. Its constant can be made explicit from fixed-annulus cutoffs; no value is asserted here. This estimates h itself. It does not embed into C1, does not control c[h], and does not yet give the uniform high solvability required by the nonlinear theorem.

### P6.11. A common weighted linear inverse admitting the accepted residual

#### Statement and notation

The background is the exact accepted checkpoint 131 reconstructed in certificate file state131_exact.json. Its exponent is c=4076476460239181/2251799813685248, gamma=1/c, and a0=partial_y rhobar(0)>0. Use the canonical full-plane velocity, the even-x and odd-y density parity, and

    L_fix h=(cX+Ubar).grad h-h+U[h].grad rhobar.

The scalar homogeneous negative space is the parity Hdot^-1 completion, with its dual parity Hdot^1 realization. Write r=|X| and <r>=(1+r^2)^(1/2). Fix

    R=2^179, sigma=1/5,

    omega0=<r>^(-6/5), omega1=<r>^(-1/5),
    omega2=(1+4r^2)^(2/5).

On compact smooth parity functions define

    L(h)=||w h||_(Hdot^-1),

    E1(h)^2=P1(h)^2+2^112 L(h)^2,
    E2(h)^2=P2(h)^2+2^72 E1(h)^2,
    Q3(h)=||omega2 D^3h||_2,
    E3(h)^2=Q3(h)^2+2^195 E2(h)^2.                         (1)

All derivative tensors use ordered Cartesian indices and Euclidean tensor norms. The notation Ej also denotes the corresponding Hilbert completion. Set

    theta=1/62, alpha=1/124, X=[E2,E3]_theta,              (2)

where the bracket is complex interpolation of the compatible Hilbert spaces. Let D_X be the strong-generator domain of L_fix on X.

**Theorem.** The operator L_fix:D_X -> X is bijective, and its inverse satisfies

    ||L_fix^-1 f||_X <=40||f||_X.                          (3)

The canonical velocity is bounded from X to its vector version with norm at most 2^35. Every h in X has globally bounded, alpha-Holder first derivatives. Define

    C_ad(h)=||h||_(C^alpha(B2))
       +sup_(j>=0) 2^(-j/4)
           [||h||_(Linfinity(Aj))+2^(j alpha)[h]_(C^alpha(Aj))],

Then, for h in D_X,

    L(h)+C_ad(h)+M(h)+|c[h]|
       <=2^46 ||L_fix h||_X.                              (4)

This is one compatible estimate in one forcing space. In particular the original accepted residual F(rhobar;c) belongs to X. It is not asserted to be small in X.

The inverse restricts to a bijection

    {h in D_X:c[h]=0} -> {f in X:f_y(0)=0}.                (5)

On this domain the full normalization-dependent linearization equals L_fix. The affine class rhobar+X fixes the leading angular profile and c; it does not admit arbitrary variations of those data. No nonlinear existence statement is asserted.

#### Certified inputs and the auxiliary third-order estimate

Section P6.10 proves P0<=E1 and consistent semigroups on E1,E2 with decay rates 1/10 and 1/20. It includes every weight and nonlocal term. Section P6.9 gives the complete continuum certificate

    (1+c+V.grad log omega2)I-3 sym(DV)+A >=-5/4 I,          (6)

where V=cX+Ubar and A=[[rhobar_y,-rhobar_x/2],[-rhobar_x/2,0]]. This is the auxiliary k=3 certificate, with the same weight as the second derivative. It is not a claim of third-order coercivity.

Here are all the constants needed for the additional level:

    D=8256, Z=16512,
    ||D^2Ubar||_infinity<=35, ||D^2rhobar||_infinity<=77,

    ||<r>D^3rhobar||_infinity<=2^14,
    ||<r>^2D4rhobar||_infinity<=2^84.

The first five follow from the completed coefficient certificates and certificate file h2_constants.json; the last follows from the exact generator bound in section P7.4 and certificate file higher_coefficient_bounds.json. The weighted Riesz constants are 256 at omega1,omega2 and 2048 at omega0. These constants include the vector velocity norm.

Apply the exact gradient identity of section P6.10 to every ordered second derivative of h. Its scalar error is bounded by Z P2^2 and its first-order error by D*256 P2 Q3. The remaining differentiated transport terms are bounded by

    3*35 P2 Q3 + 2*2^14 P1 Q3.

The other differentiated nonlocal terms are bounded by

    3*77*256 P2 Q3 + 6*2^14*256 P1 Q3
       +2*2^84*2048 P0 Q3.

The factors 2 use omega2/omega1<=2<r> and omega2/omega0<=2<r>^2. The factors 3 are the exact Leibniz multiplicities. Tensor Cauchy-Schwarz accounts for the ordered derivative sums without an additional component count. The combined cross coefficient is less than 2^97. Since P0,P1,P2<=E2, (6) and Young's inequality give

    -<D^3L_fix h,omega2^2D^3h>
       >=-(3/2) Q3^2-2^195 E2^2.                            (7)

Adding 2^195 times the E2 estimate gives

    -<L_fix h,h>_E3 >=-(3/2) E3(h)^2.                      (8)

The exact rational rounding inequalities in (7)-(8) are checked in certificate file weighted_high_constants.py.

#### Generator domains, onto property and interpolation

The complete smooth field V has bounded DV, <r>D^2V and <r>D^3V. Its flow Phi_t satisfies <Phi_t(X)> comparable to<r> on every bounded time interval. Differentiating its ODE twice and three times gives the corresponding weighted derivative bounds. Thus exp(-t)h(Phi_t(X)) is a C0 semigroup on E3; the E2 construction is already established. The lower terms produced by differentiating the composition are bounded using exactly the weight ratios above.

The operator B h=U[h].grad rhobar is bounded on E3 by its product rule, the weighted Riesz bounds, and the coefficient inequalities just listed. Its lower levels are bounded by the earlier proof. The convergent bounded-perturbation Duhamel series therefore constructs a C0 semigroup S_t on E3, consistent with that on E2 and the weighted low space.

Compact smooth parity functions form a graph core. For the transport part this follows by approximating a resolvent integral by finite sums of transported core functions, and then approximating the input in the space norm. The transported functions remain compact and smooth. The bounded perturbation B preserves the generator domain and the core. Consequently (8) extends to the generator domain and yields ||S_t||_E3<=exp(3t/2).

Interpolation and the E2 decay give

    ||S_t||_(X to X)
       <=exp[-((1-theta)/20-(3/2)theta)t]=exp(-t/40).       (9)

The common compact core is dense in X, so S_t is strongly continuous there. Define T f=-integral_0^infinity S_t f dt. This integral converges in X with norm at most 40||f||_X. The generator identity for finite time integrals, followed by closedness, gives L_fix T f=f. A kernel element has a constant semigroup orbit, and (9) forces it to vanish. This proves both surjectivity and injectivity in the stated generator realization. It also proves consistency with the already established lower inverses.

#### Explicit local and annular regularity

Use the Bessel Sobolev norm with Fourier multiplier <xi>^s and Plancherel normalization (2pi)^-2. The following cutoff construction makes the interpolation embedding quantitative.

Let P(t)=35t^4-84t^5+70t^6-20t^7 on [0,1], extended by 0 on the left and 1 on the right. It is C3, with |P'|<=3, |P''|<=27 and |P'''|<=210. Put

    chi(Y)=P(4|Y|-1)[1-P(|Y|-3)],
    chi0(Y)=1-P(|Y|-3).

The first cutoff is supported in 1/4<=|Y|<=4 and equals one on 1/2<=|Y|<=3. The second is supported in B4 and equals one on B3. Their derivatives are supported away from zero. Direct differentiation gives

    ||Dchi||_infinity<=16,
    ||D^2chi||_infinity<=1024,
    ||D^3chi||_infinity<=32768,                              (10)

and the same bounds for chi0. For the third derivative, rotate the radial direction to the first coordinate: the only nonzero components are chi''' and the three copies of chi''/r-chi'/r^2. Thus the tensor estimate in (10) is valid. The coefficient sums in the H^2 and H^3 product rules are less than 2^16; these integer inequalities are independently checked in the constants script.

For any scale t>=1, let T_t h(Y)=chi(Y)h(tY). On the support of chi, change of variables gives

    ||h(t .)||_2<=6 t^sigma P0(h),
    ||D[h(t .)]||_2<=2 t^sigma P1(h),
    ||D^2[h(t .)]||_2<=2 t^sigma P2(h),
    ||D^3[h(t .)]||_2<=2 t^(sigma+1) Q3(h).                 (11)

All norms on the left of (11) are restricted to the enlarged annulus. For example (1+16t^2)^(3/5)t^-1<=6t^sigma proves the first; the other weight comparisons are just as explicit. Equations (10)-(11) imply the deliberately rounded operator bounds

    ||T_t||_(E2 to H^2)<=2^24 t^sigma,
    ||T_t||_(E3 to H^3)<=2^24 t^(sigma+1).

For multiplication by chi0 both bounds hold with t=1. Interpolating these same linear maps gives

    ||T_t h||_(H^(2+theta))<=2^24 t^(sigma+theta)||h||_X.    (12)

Fourier Cauchy-Schwarz yields

    ||grad u||_infinity
       <=[2sqrt(pi theta(1+theta))]^-1 ||u||_(H^(2+theta)),
    [grad u]_(C^alpha)
       <=2^(-alpha)/sqrt(pi)
          sqrt(Gamma(2+alpha)Gamma(theta-alpha)/Gamma(2+theta))
          ||u||_(H^(2+theta)).                             (13)

At theta=1/62, alpha=1/124 the two constants are less than 4 and 9. Also ||u||_infinity<=||u||_(H^(2+theta)). These inequalities apply first to the core and then to X by completion. In particular,

    ||grad h||_infinity<=2^26 ||h||_X,
    [grad h]_(C^alpha(R^2))<=2^30 ||h||_X,
    C_ad(h)<=2^30 ||h||_X.                                 (14)

Here is the passage from annuli to (14). Given two points with maximum radius at least 2 and distance at most a quarter of that radius, choose a dyadic t comparable to the larger radius. Both points lie where the same T_t cutoff is one. The gradient seminorm rescales by t^(sigma+theta-1-alpha), which is bounded by 1. For farther pairs use twice the gradient supremum and their separation. Pairs in B2 use chi0. The density seminorm on one annulus follows by splitting rescaled distances at 1 in the supremum and gradient bounds in (13). Finally sigma+theta=67/310<1/4, so the factor t^-1/4 in C_ad absorbs the growth in (12). All rounded constants in this argument are checked by `weighted_high_constants.py`.

The same estimates show |h(X)|=O(r^(67/310)) and |grad h(X)|=O(r^(-243/310)) at infinity. In particular the correction is sublinear and its gradient tends to zero. Compact approximation also gives the corresponding little-o estimates, although the displayed big-O bounds already suffice below.

#### Canonical velocity, strain and the moment

The weighted low velocity bound is 2^35 by section P6.8, including the induced parities of both components. On each differentiated weighted L2 level its bound is 256. Thus U maps E2 and E3 to their vector versions with norm at most 2^35. Interpolation gives the same bound on X. Equations (12)-(14), applied componentwise as tensor inequalities, imply U[h] in C^(1,alpha) locally and sublinear growth at infinity.

This extension agrees with the canonical full-plane velocity. The kernel subtraction K(X-Y)-K(-Y) converges for sublinear parity inputs, the usual local principal value converges using the proved Holder regularity, and both agree with the compact-core extension in distributions. Its stream is odd-odd and subquadratic; uniqueness follows from the harmonic Liouville argument of section P1.2.

Consequently the exact strain formula is valid:

    c[h]=-b/4+(1/pi) PV integral sin(3theta) h(X) r^-3 dX.

Using the exact y-jet cancellation and the estimate of section P6.1 gives

    |c[h]| <= |b|/4
       +4[grad h]_(C^alpha(B1))/(pi alpha(1+alpha))
       +2^((1+sigma)/2)/sqrt(2pi(1-sigma)) P0(h)
       <=2^39 ||h||_X.                                    (15)

Parity gives grad h(0)=(0,b). Taylor's first-order integral formula and (14) imply

    |h(X)-by|<=2^30 ||h||_X r^(1+alpha)/(1+alpha).

For p=256 and kappa=260 the radial integrability gap is

    p(1+alpha)+2-kappa=2/31>0.

Therefore M(h)<=2^31||h||_X. These parameters also satisfy kappa>p+lambda+1, since lambda=2c-1<3, so they lie in the transport-adapted moment range proved in section P2.3. The moment bound here follows from the common inverse and its regularity, with no unproved nonlocal absorption. Combining (3),(14),(15) and the continuous low inclusion proves (4).

#### Residual membership, normalization and scope

The accepted residual is smooth at the center. At infinity its first nonzero sector is r^(2gamma-1)E1(theta), with 2gamma-1=0.1047775...<sigma. Each additional derivative lowers this exponent by one. Its weighted low norm is finite because wF has exponent 2gamma-1-11/5<-2. The P0,P1,P2 integrals converge because their common threshold is sigma; the Q3 integral has the larger threshold sigma+1. Smooth radial truncations approximate F in all these norms. Thus F belongs to E3, and hence to X. This uses the actual density residual, not its division by y or a residual with sectors subtracted formally.

For f in X and h=L_fix^-1 f, both h and U[h] have first-order expansions at zero. Substituting those expansions in the equation gives exactly

    f_y(0)=a0 c[h].                                       (16)

Only C1 regularity is needed: V(0)=0 makes its product with the first derivative remainder o(r). Equation (16) proves (5), and the accepted residual has f_y(0)=0 by the exact background normalization. The full normalized operator has the additional column -c[h]X.grad rhobar. That column grows like r^gamma and is outside X. The natural fixed-tail realization therefore imposes c[h]=0, rather than pretending that the column is a bounded operator on X.

Since 67/310<gamma, every correction in X preserves the leading angular profile. The scaling direction Kbar, a nonzero variation r^gamma Theta, and a c-variation r^gamma log(r)Theta are excluded. The restriction fixes the scale by fixing the entire leading profile. It is not a theorem permitting free angular or exponent perturbations.

Closed X balls are closed in the weighted low metric: a bounded sequence has a weakly convergent Hilbert-space subsequence, the continuous distributional injection identifies its weak limit with a strong low limit, and weak lower semicontinuity gives the ball bound. Continuous linear constraints such as c[h]=0 are preserved in this argument.

The theorem proves all four linear controls in the requested compatible form. The forcing norm has enormous fixed coefficients and a very large low weight radius. No useful residual smallness bound in this norm has been shown. In addition, a uniform high inverse for L_fix+U[k].grad on an X ball still requires a fractional or tame argument. Differentiating three times would require derivatives of k not provided by X. Those two issues remain explicit nonlinear gaps.

### P6.12. A weighted-low transport product bound on the existing fractional high space

#### 1. Statement and dependencies

Use the canonical IPM velocity U and the density parity of section P6.11. Let

    L(h)=||(1+r^2/R^2)^(-11/10)h||_(homogeneous H^(-1)), R>0,
    E2(g)^2=||(1+4r^2)^(2/5)D^2g||_2^2+2^72 E1(g)^2,
    E3(g)^2=||(1+4r^2)^(2/5)D^3g||_2^2+2^195 E2(g)^2,
    X=[E2,E3]_(1/62),

with E1 as defined in that proof, using its fixed radius R_star=2^179. The radius R in the low norm L may be any positive number; in the application R=R_star. These are the same high Hilbert completions and complex interpolation space. In particular that proof establishes

    ||grad g||_infinity <=2^26 ||g||_X.

The low velocity estimate is supplied independently by section P15.2. Then the bilinear transport extends continuously to L times X, with

    L(U[h].grad g)
      <=(13/2)(||grad g||_infinity+5||g||_X)L(h)
      <=2^29 ||g||_X L(h).                                (1)

The low weight radius does not enter the product constant. Thus this low bilinear estimate is compatible with the already proved weighted high inverse space. No third derivative of g is assumed. This theorem does not prove the missing uniform high inverse for a rough frozen velocity and does not imply residual smallness.

#### 2. A cylinder fractional derivative bound

Write t=log r, C=R times S1, and let

    F_g(t,theta)=r D^2g(r cos theta,r sin theta),
    m(t)=sqrt(1+exp(2t)).

All Cartesian tensor components are retained. Norms on C use measure dt dtheta. For 0<theta0<4/5, put X_theta0=[E2,E3]_theta0. We claim

    ||F_g||_(H^theta0(C))
       <=K(theta0)||g||_(X_theta0),
    K(theta0)=exp(theta0(1-theta0))
               3^(theta0/2)(9/5-theta0)^theta0.            (2)

The cylinder Bessel norm uses multiplier(1+tau^2+n^2)^(theta0/2) in the real Fourier variable tau and integer angular variable n.

Consider the analytic family T_z g=m^(4/5-z) F_g. On Re z=0,

    ||T_(iu)g||_2=||m^(4/5)D^2g||_(L2(plane))<=E2(g).

On Re z=1 set a=1+(-1/5-iu) r^2/(1+r^2). Then |a|<=sqrt(1+u^2). Direct differentiation in t gives a times the weighted Hessian plus the weighted radial contraction of D^3g. Angular differentiation gives its tangential contraction. The sum of squared radial and tangential contractions is the full squared Cartesian third tensor. Since r m^(-1/5)<=m^(4/5)<=(1+4r^2)^(2/5), the Hilbert triangle inequality yields

    ||T_(1+iu)g||_H1
      <=sqrt(2+u^2) P2(g)+Q3(g)
      <=sqrt(3+u^2) E3(g).                                (3)

Here P2 and Q3 are the corresponding weighted derivative norms. The last inequality only uses E3^2>=P2^2+Q3^2, so the large coefficient 2^195 is more than sufficient.

Apply the complex interpolation theorem to exp((z-theta0)^2)T_z, with the compatible target couple(L2(C),H1(C)). It follows directly from the three-lines theorem by conjugating the family with the cylinder Bessel multiplier of order z; its imaginary powers are unitary. The boundary constants are exp(theta0^2) and sqrt(3)exp((1-theta0)^2), because sqrt(3+u^2)exp(-u^2)<=sqrt(3). Thus

    ||m^(4/5-theta0)F_g||_H^theta0
      <=exp(theta0(1-theta0))3^(theta0/2)||g||_X_theta0.

The multiplier a(t)=m^(-b), b=4/5-theta0>0, has |a|<=1 and |a'|<=b. It has L2 operator norm at most 1 and H1 operator norm at most 1+b: write (af,grad(af)) as a(f,grad f) plus (0,a'f). Interpolation gives H^theta0 multiplier norm at most (1+b)^theta0. Applying this multiplier proves (2).

The proof begins on the compact smooth parity core, including functions whose support contains the origin. There D^2g=O(r) by central oddness, so F_g=O(r^2) as t tends to minus infinity; all displayed cylinder norms are well-defined. No cutoff removing a nonzero center jet is used. The endpoint maps extend to E2 and E3 by their defining completions, and interpolation gives the claimed map on X_theta0.

#### 3. Explicit cylinder embeddings

Use the unitary Fourier transform on C,

    fhat(n,tau)=(1/(2pi)) integral_C exp(-i(t tau+n theta))f(t,theta)dt dtheta.

Plancherel has no prefactor, and the inverse L1-to-Linfinity norm is 1/(2pi). Hausdorff-Young and Holder therefore give, for q>=2 and 1/v=1/2-1/q,

    ||f||_q <=(2pi)^(-(1-2/q))
       [sum_n integral_R (1+tau^2+n^2)^(-a v/2)dtau]^(1/v)
       ||f||_H^a.                                        (4)

For beta>1, monotonicity in |n| and comparison with the integral over the plane imply

    sum_n integral_R (1+tau^2+n^2)^(-beta)dtau
      <=pi+pi/(beta-1)=pi beta/(beta-1).                   (5)

Indeed the n=0 integral is at most pi for beta>=1, and the two nonzero sums are bounded by the corresponding real integrals. This proves (5) in every case used below.

Take p=2/(1-theta0/2) in (4) with a=theta0. Then v=4/theta0 and beta=2, so

    ||F||_p <=(2pi)^(-theta0/4)||F||_H^theta0.

Take q=4/theta0 with a=1. Then beta=2/(2-theta0), giving

    ||phi||_q <=(2pi theta0)^(-(2-theta0)/4)||phi||_H1.

A centrally odd test function has zero angular mean. Circle Poincare and conformal invariance of the plane Dirichlet integral give

    ||phi||_H1(C)<=sqrt(2)||grad phi||_(L2(plane)).

Since 1/p+1/q=1/2, Holder and (2) yield

    ||D^2g phi||_(L2(plane))=||F_g phi||_(L2(C))
      <= D(theta0)||g||_X_theta0 ||grad phi||_2,
    D(theta0)=K(theta0)/(sqrt(pi) theta0^((2-theta0)/4)).     (6)

The same embeddings hold for Cartesian tensors: Hausdorff-Young extends to Hilbert-valued transforms by interpolation between the L1-to-Linfinity and Plancherel bounds, and Holder is applied to the pointwise Euclidean norm. At theta0=1/62, the inequality D(theta0)<5 can be checked without numerical transcendental evaluation. Since log(3)<2, log(9/5)<1 and exp(x)<=1/(1-x) for 0<=x<1, K(theta0)<exp(3/62)<=62/59. Also theta0^(-(2-theta0)/4)<sqrt(62) and pi>3. Hence D(theta0)^2<(62/59)^2(62/3)=238328/10443<25. Independent 512-bit interval evaluation gives D(theta0) in [4.52050853418831069838,4.52050853418831069840]. No uncomputed embedding constant occurs in (6).

#### 4. Dual product and completion

For a smooth parity test phi,

    (sum_j ||grad(partial_j g phi)||_2^2)^(1/2)
      <=||grad g||_infinity||grad phi||_2+||D^2g phi||_2
      <=(||grad g||_infinity+5||g||_X)||grad phi||_2.

Each partial_j g phi has the dual parity of the corresponding velocity component. Pair w U[h] with this vector of products. The sharp regularized-weight velocity bound L(U[h])<=(13/2)L(h) proves the first inequality in (1). The established gradient embedding and the exact inequality (13/2)(2^26+5)<2^29 prove the second.

Density and this uniform estimate define the product on L times X; the limit is independent of approximation. On smooth inputs, or when both inputs belong to X, it agrees with the ordinary distributional transport product. Closed X balls are already closed in the low metric by section P6.11. Thus (1) supplies the low Lipschitz estimate needed in a two-norm iteration on precisely that X ball. It leaves the separate high solvability hypothesis open.

### P6.13. A radial-resolvent bound for the weighted negative-order commutator

#### 1. Statement, spaces and scope

Let H be the homogeneous H^(-1) completion of complex centrally odd compact smooth functions on R^2. Fix R>0, 0<delta<=1 and 0<=s<3-delta. Set

    w=(1+r^2/R^2)^(-s/2),
    B=(partial_x-i partial_y)^2(-Delta)^(-1),
    M_delta=sup_(z>0) z^(2-delta)/(1+z^2)
           =(delta/2)((2-delta)/delta)^(1-delta/2).

All transforms use the canonical full-plane realization of section P15.2. Then

    ||r^(-delta)(w B w^(-1)-B)g||_H
      <=[4s M_delta/(3-s-delta)] R^(-delta)||g||_H.       (1)

Let rho have the project's real density parity, a=grad rho, and

    C_rho=sup_(r>0) r^delta(|a|+r|Da|)<infinity,
    T h=U[h].a, U=(-R1 R2,R1^2).

Then on the real density subspace

    ||w T w^(-1)-T||_(H->H)
      <=[4s M_delta/(3-s-delta)] C_rho R^(-delta).         (2)

In particular, for delta=2/5 and 0<=s<=11/5, the bracket is less than 14. This replaces the factor 2^53 in the earlier commutator estimate. The result is an upper bound, not a sharp-norm claim. It changes neither the background matrix assumptions nor the realization of the linear operator.

#### 2. Resolvent difference on the logarithmic cylinder

Put t=log r, D=partial_t and

    alpha(t)=-D log w=s e^(2t)/(R^2+e^(2t)).

Write a source mode as g=r^(-2)F(t)e^(in theta), n odd. Its negative norm squared is

    2pi ||Q_n^(-1/2)F||_2^2, Q_n=n^2-D^2.

For n>=3, the weighted Beurling transform maps this mode to n-2, with cylinder source

    -F+2(n-1)(n-D-alpha)^(-1)F.

For n=-k, k>=1 odd, the corresponding source in mode-k-2 is

    -F+2(k+1)(D+k+alpha)^(-1)F.

The positive inverses are future Volterra integrals and the negative inverses are past Volterra integrals. These are the canonical radial Poisson formulas proved in the regularized-weight theorem. The mode n=1 maps exactly to-F in mode-1 for every radial weight, so its commutator is zero.

Subtract the formulas at alpha=0. The resolvent identity gives

    E_n=2(n-1)(n-D-alpha)^(-1) alpha (n-D)^(-1)F, n>=3,
    E_(-k)=-2(k+1)(D+k+alpha)^(-1) alpha (D+k)^(-1)F.

Multiplication by r^(-delta)=exp(-delta t) shifts the two outer inverses:

    r^(-delta)(n-D-alpha)^(-1)
       =(n-delta-D-alpha)^(-1)r^(-delta),
    r^(-delta)(D+k+alpha)^(-1)
       =(D+k+delta+alpha)^(-1)r^(-delta).                   (3)

These identities first follow by substitution in the Volterra formulas. Their convergence is ensured by n-delta-s>0 and k+delta>0. Thus no boundary solution or harmonic term is introduced by the conjugation.

#### 3. Mode bounds

The Fourier multiplier identities give

    ||(n-D)^(-1)F||_2=||Q_n^(-1/2)F||_2,
    ||(D+k)^(-1)F||_2=||Q_k^(-1/2)F||_2.

The shifted Volterra kernels are bounded by exponential convolution kernels. Hence their L2 norms are at most 1/(n-delta-s) and 1/(k+delta), respectively. Also

    ||r^(-delta)alpha||_infinity=s M_delta R^(-delta).

Applying Q_(n-2)^(-1/2) or Q_(k+2)^(-1/2) after these L2 estimates gives the respective block bounds

    2(n-1)s M_delta/[(n-2)(n-delta-s)] R^(-delta),
    2(k+1)s M_delta/[(k+2)(k+delta)] R^(-delta).             (4)

The first expression decreases with n>=3, because both 1+1/(n-2) and 1/(n-delta-s) decrease. Its maximum is the bracket in (1). The second decreases with k>=1: differentiating its logarithm gives 1/[(k+1)(k+2)]-1/(k+delta)<0 for 0<delta<=1. At k=1 it is 4s M_delta/[3(1+delta)], no larger than the first maximum, since 3-s-delta<=3(1+delta).

Angular orthogonality now proves (1) on finite angular sums with compact annular radial support. This core is dense in H. The bound defines the extension of the weighted commutator, including its r^(-delta) factor. Its distributional action agrees with the original commutator on smooth compact inputs by the radial formulas and local convergence. Possible growth of r^(-delta) at the origin is handled by the proved bounded map; no bounded-multiplier assertion about r^(-delta) alone is made.

#### 4. Restore the density-gradient coefficient

For real scalar inputs, U2+i U1=(B-I)/2. The local identity cancels from the commutator. Thus (1) gives the vector negative-norm bound with half its constant.

Put b=r^delta a. Then

    |b|<=C_rho,
    r|Db|<=delta r^delta|a|+r^(delta+1)|Da|<=C_rho.

The last inequality uses delta<=1 and the definition of C_rho. For a smooth parity test phi, the vector product b phi satisfies

    ||D(b phi)||_2
       <=C_rho||Dphi||_2+C_rho||phi/r||_2
       <=2 C_rho||Dphi||_2.

The final inequality is the angular parity Hardy inequality. Each component has exactly the dual parity of the corresponding velocity component. By duality, multiplication by b from vector H to scalar H has norm at most 2C_rho. Compose it with the half-constant vector estimate to obtain(2).

The fractional power r^delta makes b only locally weakly differentiable at zero. The displayed Hardy estimate still defines its bounded multiplier action. Approximation away from zero and completion justify the dual calculation without assuming a bounded ordinary gradient at the origin.

At delta=2/5, M_delta=4^(4/5)/5. The bracket is increasing in s and equals 22 M_delta at s=11/5. The elementary integer inequality

    4^4 * 11^5 < 35^5

implies M_delta<7/11, hence 22 M_delta<14. The sharper bracket is about 13.3383. No numerical approximation is needed for the bound 14.

#### 5. Consequence for the already established low inverse

In section P6.5, replace the commutator factor 2^53 by 14. Every other term and its sign is unchanged. With the coefficient bounds C_rho,C_U,C_DU,C_D2U from that theorem, set

    C_new(s)=C_DU+C_rho
              +s(9C_U+2C_DU+C_D2U/sqrt(2))+14C_rho.

If m_s-C_new(s)R^(-2/5)>0, the same graph-core energy argument and semigroup integral give a bijective generator realization, with inverse norm at most the reciprocal of that difference. This proves injectivity and surjectivity in the same completion. A change of R changes equivalent norms, and therefore requires rechecking any constants that were tied to a particular norm. No nonlinear conclusion follows from the commutator improvement alone.

#### 5. Realization, inverse and scope

The transport flow is complete, smooth, parity preserving, with bounded finite-time derivatives and the weighted second-derivative bounds established in section P6.10. It acts on these new spaces by exactly the same product and weight-ratio estimates. The background coupling U[h].D rhobar is bounded on E1 and E2 by the displayed coefficient and Riesz bounds, and on the low space by check 67 and the parity multiplier estimate. The resulting bounded-perturbation Duhamel series is consistent with the low semigroup.

Compact smooth parity functions form a common graph core: approximate the transport resolvent integral by finite sums of transported compact functions, then use bounded perturbation. The energy inequalities(9),(12) pass to the generator domains. Exponential decay gives the inverse as minus the integral of the semigroup over nonnegative time. The generator identity for finite integrals and closedness prove surjectivity; a constant orbit and strict decay prove injectivity. These arguments apply to the same low realization and prove consistency, not only separate coercive inequalities.

The accepted density residual belongs to both spaces since its leading exponent 2/c-1 is below 1/5, and its derivative asymptotics have the same weighted threshold. Smooth truncations converge at infinity and the center is regular. This membership is unchanged by the finite positive coefficients or the choiceR=2^35. Those stronger claims require a compatible fractional construction.

### P6.15. Stronger radial weights on the higher background derivatives

#### Statement

For the exact recovered state 131 and its canonical full-plane velocity,

    sup_X <r>^2 |D^4 rho(X)|_F <512,
    sup_X <r> |D^3 U(X)|_F <16,

where <r>=(1+|X|^2)^(1/2) and the Frobenius norms count every ordered Cartesian derivative. These are continuum inequalities for this reference, not assumptions on a new reference or bounds from a grid.

#### Exact algebraic formulas

Use the source, polynomial derivation and parity conventions of section P7.3. Put t=r^2/(1+r^2), z=cos(2theta), delta=1-1/c, q=(1-t)^(delta/2). The exact sixth- and seventh-order polar recurrence, with all negative powers cancelling as rational identities, gives

    D^3 U=(1-t) sum_(j=0)^3 q^(j+1) P_(3,j)(t,z) A_3(theta),
    D^4 rho=sqrt(t)(1-t)^(3/2) sum_(j=0)^3 q^(j+1) P_(4,j)(t,z) A_4(theta).

Each tensor component has its own rational polynomial and angular factor. The factors A_3 are 1 or sin(2theta); A_4 are sin(theta) or cos(theta). The identities follow from U=(-chi_xyy,chi_xxy), rho=-chi_xxy-chi_yyy. Consequently the radial factors for the displayed theorem are exactly

    sqrt(1-t),                     for <r>D^3 U,
    sqrt(t)*sqrt(1-t),              for <r>^2 D^4 rho.

No asymptotic truncation is used. The formulas extend continuously to the compactified endpoints. Quadrant parity extends the bounds to the whole plane.

#### Interval verification and source binding

The script certificate file r2_extra_audit.py reconstructs all rational polynomials directly from the recovered original state. It compares them exactly with extra_coefficient_polynomials.json and verifies the source hash against the earlier independently audited certificate. That earlier audit includes all 13 distinct components at seven rational points against seventh-order Cartesian potential jets, and rejects non-finite values. The exact polynomial equality makes those checks apply to the current polynomials as well.

The script traverses the entire 315-leaf binary partition of extra_coefficient_certificate.json. On each rectangle it takes the Bernstein hull of the polynomial in t,z and the degree-four polynomial in q. The angular factors are bounded on that same rectangle. It then multiplies by the nonnegative radial bounds above and sums the squared tensor-component bounds with binomial multiplicities. Thus different component maxima are allowed at different points, as required for an upper bound.

The largest recomputed enclosures are below 324.712695 and 8.091291, respectively. Every leaf is strictly below 512 and 16. The complete enclosures, input hashes and source hash are in certificate file r2_extra_audit.json. A final audit checks all leaf bounds and binds the proof and script hashes. The smooth complete transport field has bounded DV, <r>D2V and <r>D3V, by the same coefficient bounds.
