This holds for every 0<s<=2^-12 and anyR>=1 in the defined weighted space, includingR2^31 by the uniform-radius audit. The sufficienteta2^-35 therefore fails by more than 2^34. All eight points agree in all seven fields between the Cartesian-jet and polar-polynomial methods. This does not refute a smaller global positive matrix bound, later candidate iterates, or actual existence.

## P21. Real angular pairing: a smaller velocity constant, the weight radius 2^31 and the residual gap there

### P21.1. Real angular pairing improves the weighted velocity and low radius

Status: CONFIRMED check 95 after complete independent analytical and 512-bit arithmetic audit. 

#### Statement

Let H be the homogeneous H^-1 completion of real centrally odd compact smooth functions on the plane, and define H_(sigma,R)(h)=||w_R h||_H, with w_R=(1+r^2/R^2)^(-sigma/2), R>0 and 0<=sigma<=11/5. The velocity is the canonical full-plane U=(-R1R2,R1^2), with a Hilbert sum of its two components. Then

    H_(sigma,R)(U[h]) <= (13/3) H_(sigma,R)(h).             (1)

No sharpness is asserted. The proof uses only real central oddness, so it applies to the project's narrower density parity. The earlier 13/2 bound is replaced by 13/3.

For sigma=11/5 and d=4/9, the real weighted coupling commutator satisfies

    ||w_R (U[w_R^-1 g].D rho)-U[g].D rho||_H
       <=(21/2) C_rho R^-d ||g||_H,                       (2)
    C_rho=sup r^d(|D rho|+r|D2 rho|).

Consequently, a reference satisfying all the current low-energy hypotheses and

    (C_rho,C_U,C_DU,C_D2U)<=(186,22,22,56)                 (3)

has low margin greater than 1/5 already at R=2^31. Here C_U=sup r^(d-1)|U|, C_DU=sup r^d|DU| and C_D2U=sup r^(1+d)|D2U|. The original exact state 131 satisfies (3), as checked below. The compatible fractional theorem of part P19 then holds in this new norm with the same s=3*2^-31, r0=5*2^-32, eta=2^-35, high inverse 40 and low inverse 6. No actual residual smallness at the new radius is asserted.

#### 1. Real pairing of angular modes

All norms and inner products in this section are in the weighted space H_(sigma,R), or equivalently in H after conjugation by w_R. Put B=(partial_x-i partial_y)^2(-Delta)^-1 and t=log r. For each odd integern write w_R h=r^-2 F_n(t)e^(in theta), Q_n=n^2-partial_t^2. The scalar negative norm is the sum of 2pi||Q_n^-1/2 F_n||2^2. Since h is real, F_-n=conjugate(F_n), so the two input norms are equal.

The exact Volterra formulas and their proof in section P15.2 give, for n>=3, the positive block B:n->n-2 with norm at most

    A_n=n(n-2+sigma)/((n-2)(n-sigma)),

and for n>=1 the negative block B:-n->-n-2 with norm at most

    D_n=1+sigma/(n+2).

The positive n=1 block is exactly minus the identity into angular mode-1. Both A_n and D_n decrease in n over their indicated ranges and increase in sigma. Their values at sigma=11/5 may therefore be used throughout. Normalize a_n>=0, n positive odd, so that a_n^2 is the sum of the positive and negative input energies at n, including 2pi. Thus ||h||^2=sum a_n^2.

Orthogonality of output angular modes gives

    ||Bh||^2 <= (1+D_1^2)a_1^2/2
                   +sum_(n>=3)(A_n^2+D_n^2)a_n^2/2.      (4)

Only modes separated by two can contribute to <Bh,h>, except for the n=1 reflection. The latter contribution is bounded below by-a_1^2/2. For each n>=3 the two links between the pair n and n-2 are bounded below by

    -(A_n+D_(n-2))a_n a_(n-2)/2.

This follows from the block norms and Cauchy-Schwarz; it does not assume that the positive and negative blocks are adjoints or have the same sign. For the project's sine parity the n=1 self term is actually positive, but that improvement is not needed.

Since U2+iU1=(B-I)h/2, equations(4) and the cross bounds give

    ||Uh||^2 <= sum J_nn a_n^2+2sum J_(n,n-2)a_n a_(n-2),

where

    J_11=5/8+D_1^2/8,
    J_nn=1/4+(A_n^2+D_n^2)/8, n>=3,
    J_(n,n-2)=(A_n+D_(n-2))/8, n>=3.                     (5)

All coefficients in this comparison matrix are nonnegative. The complex norm of U2+iU1 is exactly the Hilbert sum of the real component norms, because the radial negative-order inner product is real on real functions.

#### 2. Explicit weighted row bound

Choose positive weights v_1=1/10, v_3=1, v_n=1/20 for n>=5. The elementary inequality 2xy<=a x^2+a^-1 y^2 on each edge proves that the quadratic form of J is bounded by

    sup_n (sum_m J_nm v_m)/v_n * sum_n a_n^2.             (6)

This argument works first for finite sequences. Its constant extends by density; no unproved infinite-matrix spectral theorem is needed.

At sigma=11/5 the exact constants are

    A_3=12, A_5=65/21, A_7=21/10,
    D_1=26/15, D_3=36/25, D_5=46/35.

For row 1, (6) is J_11+10J_13<19. For row 3 it is

    J_33+J_31/10+J_35/20 <75/4.

The sharper common target 75/4 also holds for row 1 by direct rational comparison. Row 5 is J_55+20J_53+J_57<14. For n>=7, monotonicity gives J_nn<2 and each adjacent off-diagonal entry<1, hence row sum<4. All these are exact rational inequalities checked in the adjacent script. Therefore ||Uh||^2<=(75/4)||h||^2. Finally 75/4<169/9 because 675<676. This proves (1). Finite angular sums and compact annular radial sources are dense in the stated space; the canonical completion is the same as in the Volterra theorem.

#### 3. Real commutator estimate

The radial-resolvent proof in section P6.13 applies to

    r^-d(w_R B w_R^-1-B).

For positive n>=3 its block norm is bounded by

    P=4 sigma M_d/(3-sigma-d),
    M_d=(d/2)((2-d)/d)^(1-d/2).

For negative n=-k it is bounded by

    D=4 sigma M_d/[3(1+d)],

using the maximum at k=1. The positive n=1 block is zero. Real pairing and angular orthogonality therefore improve the full complex-source bound P to

    C_real=sqrt((P^2+D^2)/2).                             (7)

Indeed each positive/negative input pair has equal norm, while its two outputs remain orthogonal. The real velocity commutator has half this norm, since the local identity cancels.

At sigma=11/5,d=4/9, P=(99/4)M_d and D=(132/65)M_d. Moreover M_d^9=4*7^7/9^9, so the integer inequality 4*7^7*100^9<59^9*9^9 gives M_d<59/100. Substitution in (7) proves C_real<21/2 by a rational squared comparison.

To restore the coefficient put b=r^d D rho. Then |b|<=C_rho and r|Db|<=C_rho because d<=1. Angular parity Hardy and the product rule give ||D(b phi)||2<=2C_rho||Dphi||2 for a centrally odd scalar test phi. This multiplier bound cancels the factor 1/2 of the velocity commutator and proves (2). Weak differentiability at the origin, completion and the canonical realization are justified by exactly the same cutoff argument as in the existing radial-resolvent proof. No independent bound on multiplication by r^-d is assumed.

#### 4. Radius 2^31 and compatibility

The original-state certificate in certificate file decay_radius.json already encloses the local coefficient quantities below 185.824,21.680,21.680,23.228 and the exterior quantities below 151.032,1.979,7.375,55.064. The new script checks these balls against (3), including their exact source hash, and reconstructs the original coefficient vector again for input identity. Thus (3) requires no new continuum enclosure method.

The exact low-energy proof now yields the margin

    2/5-R^-d [22+(1+21/2)186
                    +(11/5)(9*22+2*22+56/sqrt(2))].       (8)

At R=2^31, R^d=2^(124/9)>14000, as verified by the integer inequality 14000^9<2^124. Also 1/sqrt(2)<5/7. Hence (8) is strictly greater than

    2/5-[22+(23/2)186+(11/5)*282]/14000
       =14093/70000 >1/5.                                (9)

The generator, its graph core and the inverse integral depend on the positive margin and the same canonical weighted coupling, not on the old sufficient radius. They therefore give a bijective low realization with inverse at most 5 and the same perturbed bound 6 used in part P19. All derivative weights and their coefficient bounds are unchanged. Part P18 section 3 proves that the Bessel, interpolation, localization, common-domain and low/high consistency estimates are uniform for every R>=1. Thus the complete part P19 theorem transfers to R=2^31 with unchanged parameters and hypotheses, replacing only its explicit low coefficient contract by (3),(8).

The improved velocity bound also makes the low bilinear constant in part P19 equal to at most 280*(13/3)=3640/3<1280, rather than 1820. Keeping the old rounded 2048 is valid, so no unproved optimization of the nonlinear parameters is involved in the transfer. A residual norm at R=2^31 must be checked in that norm; old-radius numerical lower or upper bounds are not silently substituted.

#### Dependencies and scope

The real pairing argument is analytical. The only source-specific input is (3) and the unchanged reference contract from part P17, including global matrices and derivative bounds. The script binds all imported proof and certificate files and performs exact rational inequalities plus 512-bit arithmetic. This is a sufficient improvement, not a sharp velocity constant or a minimal radius. Original-profile nonlinear existence remains unproved.

### P21.2. Annular lower bound for the accepted weighted residual

Status: CONFIRMED check 96 after analytical audit and 768-bit original-source recomputation. The proof preceded its arithmetic run.

#### Statement and spaces

Use the exact accepted state 131 reconstructed from the read-only original in certificate file state131_exact.json, and its canonical velocity. Put c=c_l, gamma=1/c, delta=1-gamma, q=2gamma-1, R=2^31, w=(1+r^2/R^2)^(-11/10). For a parity density f, let L(f)=||wf||_{dot H^{-1}} and N_s^w(f)=E_w(J^s f), with E_w^2=P2^2+2^22 P1^2+2^53 L^2 as in this part's section P21.1. The bounded inverse Bessel estimate in section P17.4 gives

    N_s^w(f) >= 2^(53/2) L(f)/6,  0<s<=2^-12.

The present proof will give a lower bound for f=F(rho_131). It uses only an explicit compactly supported homogeneous H1 test, exact rational Fourier algebra, and rigorously bounded omitted binomial terms.

#### The test function

Fix an odd positive integer m and let chi(t)=(t-1)^2(2-t)^2 on 1<=t<=2, zero elsewhere. Let phi(r,theta)=sign(e_m) chi(r/R) sin(m theta), where e_m is the leading coefficient of F. This test is C1, compactly supported, and has the required even-x, odd-y parity. Direct polynomial integration gives

    integral chi(t) dt=1/30,
    integral chi(t)^2 dt=1/630,
    integral t chi'(t)^2 dt=1/35.

Consequently ||Dphi||_2^2=pi integral [t chi'^2+m^2 chi^2/t]dt <=pi(1/35+m^2/630). Suppose for every r>=R the sin(m theta) coefficient of F has sign e_m and absolute value at least b r^q. Since q+1>0 and w>=5^(-11/10) on the test annulus,

    |<wF,phi>| >= pi b R^(q+2) 5^(-11/10)/30,
    L(F) >= sqrt(pi) b R^(q+2) 5^(-11/10)
                    /(30 sqrt(1/35+m^2/630)).                 (1)

The inequalities below verify a positive b without numerical quadrature.

#### Exact finite sectors and uniform tail error

Each canonical potential summand is v r^(2k)(1+r^2)^(p_j-k) cos(2m theta), with p_j=(3+gamma-j delta)/2, 0<=j<=3 and |p_j-k|<26. Retain binomial orders 0<=a<=Q. Their density powers are gamma-j delta-2a. Differentiate the angular monomials exactly to obtain the truncated density rho_t, velocity u_t and residual F_t. The residual powers are gamma-j delta-2a, with linear and quadratic coefficients combined exactly. The leading gamma term vanishes because c gamma=1. All remaining powers are <=q.

Write A_j=sum_{branch j}|v| and a0=Q+1. For d=3,4 define

    M_d=sum_(j,a<=Q) B_(d,j,a) R^(-j delta-2a),
    tau_d=((a0+26)/(a0+1))
                    *((2a0+34)/(2a0+32))^d/R^2,
    T_d=binom(a0+25,a0)(2a0+32)^d R^(-2a0)
                    sum_j A_j R^(-j delta)/(1-tau_d).

Here B_(d,j,a) is the maximum, over Cartesian components of the d-th derivative of its potential sector, of the sum of absolute angular coefficients. These are exact rational numbers. The ratio test is valid because the binomial coefficient majorant is binom(a+25,a), and every Cartesian derivative multiplies the angular coefficient norm by at most 2a+32 for d<=4. Indeed |gamma+3-j delta-2a|+2m+2(d-1)<2a+32 for the archived indices. The displayed ratio decreases in a. Thus, for r>=R, each potential derivative component satisfies

    |D^d chi_t| <= M_d r^(gamma+3-d),
    |D^d(chi-chi_t)| <= T_d (R/r)^(2a0) r^(gamma+3-d).

The density is a sum of two third derivatives and each velocity component is one third derivative. Hence the tensor bounds give

    |rho-rho_t| <=2T3 r^gamma (R/r)^(2a0),
    |u-u_t| <=sqrt(2)T3 r^gamma (R/r)^(2a0),
    |D(rho-rho_t)| <=2sqrt(2)T4 r^(gamma-1)(R/r)^(2a0),
    |u_t| <=sqrt(2)M3 r^gamma,
    |D rho_t| <=2sqrt(2)M4 r^(gamma-1).

Since 2a0>delta, the full pointwise residual difference obeys, uniformly for r>=R,

    |F-F_t|/r^q <= Ctail,
    Ctail=(2sqrt(2)c T4+2T3) R^delta
                      +4(T3 M4+M3 T4+T3 T4).                  (2)

The normalized sin(m theta) coefficient of an error bounded by Ctail is at most (4/pi)Ctail<2Ctail. Let

    B_m=sum_(p<q)|coefficient_(p,m)(F_t)| R^(p-q).

Then b=|e_m|-B_m-2Ctail is a valid lower bound for the signed normalized coefficient at every r>=R. The certificate encloses (1), (2), B_m and b using Arb from exact rational inputs. The source hash, precision, exact sector coefficients, derivative component bounds and all final lower bounds are recorded. A float is never used to prove a bound.

#### Combining angular tests

The single-mode tests are orthogonal in the gradient inner product. To obtain one explicit improved test, put d_m=1/35+m^2/630 and use

    phi=chi(r/R) sum_m (e_m/d_m) sin(m theta).

All coefficients of this angular polynomial are exact rationals. If b_m>0 are the bounds proved above, its squared gradient norm is at most pi sum_m e_m^2/d_m, and its pairing is at least pi R^(q+2)5^(-11/10) sum_m |e_m|b_m/d_m /30. Dividing gives the combined lower bound recorded by the certificate. This is one test function, not a sum of incompatible estimates.

#### Domain of the inverse Bessel comparison

The actual residual is smooth, centrally odd and a symbol of degree q=2/c-1<1/5. Its derivatives satisfy |D^jF|<=C_j<r>^(q-j) for every fixedj. The polynomially moderate Bessel kernel preserves this symbol class: local Taylor subtraction handles its singularity, and the exponentially decaying kernel handles the far region. In particular J^sF has the same leading degreeq. The weighted low and top derivative components converge because q<1/5, as proved in section P17.3. Thus g=J^sF belongs toE andL. The bounded J^-s inequality extends to the entire L completion by density, not only compact or bounded inputs. Its canonical distributional action satisfies J^-s g=F. This justifies the displayed norm comparison for the growing residual and any 0<s<=2^-12. It also answers the C8 domain question.

#### Certified conclusion

The adjacent program independently reconstructs all 860 coefficients from the read-only original and retains eight potential sectors(Q=1). All twenty odd modes 1 through 39 have positive signed normalized coefficient bounds. The combined test proves

    L_(2^31)(F131)>130848043650562055,
    N_(s,2^31)(F131)>2069716531185650706596364>2^80, 0<s<=2^-12.

The sufficient eta=2^-35 from part P19, transferred by this part's section P21.1, is therefore violated by more than 2^115. Three independently evaluated complete Cartesian jets agree with the exact sector expansion within the proved omitted-binomial bound. No value from an older radius was inserted into this norm. The actual norm can be larger than this one-test lower bound.

#### Scope

This is a lower bound on the weighted norm of one exact reference residual, not an obstruction to all nearby exact solutions or a lower bound over an optimized family. The same test argument applies to a repaired residual only after its actual annular coefficient and error are separately checked. In particular the P14 repairs cancel all residual powers >=-2, so their original growing sector cannot be inserted in (1).

## P22. Optimality of the frozen heat-norm inverse, including the trace constraints

### P22.1. Optimality of the frozen heat-norm inverse, including trace constraints

Status: CONFIRMED check 98 by independent analytical derivation and proof audit. Lead  No numerical evidence is needed for this theorem.

#### Exact statement

Fix lambda>1, a>0, sigma=a/(lambda-1)>4 and 0<alpha<1. Let X be the completion of real Schwartz functions with compact Fourier support away from zero, even in x and odd in y, in the norm

    N(h)=sup_(t>0) t^((sigma-alpha)/2)
                         ||exp(t Delta) Lambda^sigma h||_infinity.

Use the canonical full-plane Riesz transform R1^2 with Fourier multiplier -xi_x^2/|xi|^2. Let L0 be the generator realization on X of

    lambda x partial_x+y partial_y-1+a R1^2,

with the strongly continuous semigroup S_t and inverse constructed in section P5.1. Then the sufficient bounds in that proof are optimal in this exact norm:

    ||S_t||_(X->X)=exp(-(1-alpha)t), t>=0,
    ||L0^-1||_(X->X)=1/(1-alpha).                         (1)

More precisely, there are real Schwartz densities h_n in the generator domain such that

    N(h_n)=1,
    ||(L0+(1-alpha))h_n||_X ->0,
    partial_y h_n(0)=0, c[h_n]=0.                        (2)

Here c[h]=partial_y R1^2h(0) uses the canonical strain with its contact term. The forcing L0h_n is smooth and has zero y derivative at the origin. Thus even on this regular trace-compatible test class, no smaller uniform inverse constant can replace 1/(1-alpha). This does not assert that the strain or origin-derivative constraints define closed subspaces of X. They do not supply a new Banach realization by themselves.

The result concerns the complete coupled frozen operator. It does not prove a sharp inverse constant for the variable-coefficient IPM operator or change the nonlinear residual thresholds.

#### 1. Two elementary preparation facts

Write [.]_alpha for the global homogeneous alpha-Holder seminorm. The previous heat proof gives finite constants A,B>0 such that

    N(h)<=A[h]_alpha, [h]_alpha<=B N(h).                  (3)

These hold on the stated core and its completion. Only finiteness is needed here.

First, if b is a bounded C1 function on R with bounded derivative, the function

    g(y)=sign(y)|y|^alpha b(log|y|), g(0)=0

satisfies

    [g]_alpha <=4(||b||_infinity+||b'||_infinity).         (4)

To prove this, take two positive arguments with maximum M, minimum m and difference d. If d>=M/2, bound the two values by 2||b||M^alpha<=2^(1+alpha)||b||d^alpha. If d<M/2 then d<m; the derivative is bounded on [m,M] by m^(alpha-1)(alpha||b||+||b'||), and d m^(alpha-1)<=d^alpha. Negative arguments give the same estimate. For opposite signs, concavity gives |y|^alpha+|z|^alpha<=2^(1-alpha)(|y|+|z|)^alpha. These cases prove(4).

Second, every real Schwartz density h belongs to the generator domain and L0 acts by the displayed distributional formula. Here is a graph approximation argument, rather than an assumption about the domain. Put

    Omega_alpha(v)=int_R2 |xi|^alpha |vhat(xi)| dxi.

The Fourier difference inequality gives [v]_alpha<=2^(1-alpha)(2pi)^(-2)Omega_alpha(v), and hence (3) bounds its X norm. Let P_n be smooth radial Fourier cutoffs to expanding compact annuli, equal to one on every fixed nonzero frequency for sufficiently large n, with |xi| |DP_n| uniformly bounded. For a Schwartz h, both Omega_alpha(h) and Omega_alpha(L0h) are finite: the transport Fourier derivatives are Schwartz and the Riesz multiplier is bounded. Thus P_nh->h and P_nL0h->L0h in X by dominated convergence. In Fourier variables the commutator is exactly

    (L0P_n-P_nL0)h hat
       =-(lambda xi_x partial_xi_x+xi_y partial_xi_y)P_n * hhat.

Its Omega_alpha norm tends to zero by the same domination, since the derivative supports leave every fixed nonzero frequency. Each P_nh is in the generator core. Closedness of the generator proves the assertion, including the canonical meaning of L0h. This argument also applies to every finite sum of the Schwartz functions used below.

#### 2. A vertical approximate eigenfunction with slow cutoffs

Choose eta in C_c^infinity(R) with 0<=eta<=1, eta=1 on [-1,1], and eta=0 outside [-2,2]. For an integer L>=1 define

    g_L(y)=sign(y)|y|^alpha eta(log|y|/L), g_L(0)=0.

It is odd, smooth, compactly supported and zero on a neighborhood of zero; g_L(1)=1. Its defect under the one-dimensional dilation is

    r_L=(y partial_y-alpha)g_L
        =L^-1 sign(y)|y|^alpha eta'(log|y|/L).

Equation(4) proves

    [g_L]_alpha<=C_alpha,
    [r_L]_alpha<=C_alpha/L,                              (5)

with constants depending on the fixed cutoff and alpha, not on L. The suprema of g_L and r_L can grow with L; they will be controlled by the independent horizontal scale below.

Choose a smooth theta:R->[0,1] equal to one on (-infinity,1] and zero on [2,infinity). Set

    chi_L(x)=theta(log(1+x^2)/(2L)),
    p_L(x)=x chi_L'(x).

These are even smooth compactly supported functions, chi_L(0)=1, and

    p_L(x)=x^2/[L(1+x^2)] theta'(log(1+x^2)/(2L)),
    ||p_L||_infinity<=||theta'||_infinity/L.              (6)

For 0<epsilon<=1 define f_(L,epsilon)(x,y)=chi_L(epsilon x)g_L(y). It is a smooth compactly supported density with the required parity, zero origin y derivative and f_(L,epsilon)(0,1)=1. Put mu=alpha-1. Direct differentiation gives

    (L0-mu)f_(L,epsilon)
       =lambda p_L(epsilon x)g_L(y)
          +chi_L(epsilon x)r_L(y)+a R1^2 f_(L,epsilon).  (7)

For separate-variable products the exact elementary estimate is

    [u(x)v(y)]_alpha
       <=||u||_infinity[v]_alpha+[u]_alpha||v||_infinity.

It follows from (5)-(6) and scaling of the seminorm that, for fixed L,

    limsup_(epsilon->0)
      [lambda p_L(epsilon x)g_L+chi_L(epsilon x)r_L]_alpha
           <=C/L.                                      (8)

The terms discarded in this limit are precisely epsilon^alpha times the finite quantities lambda[p_L]_alpha||g_L||_infinity and [chi_L]_alpha||r_L||_infinity. Also [f_(L,epsilon)]_alpha stays uniformly bounded if epsilon is chosen sufficiently small for each L. Its lower bound is one, using the two points(0,0),(0,1).

#### 3. The entire Riesz coupling and the strain disappear at large horizontal scale

For fixed L, let u and v denote the horizontal and vertical Fourier variables after the horizontal change of scale. Then

    Omega_alpha(R1^2 f_(L,epsilon))
       =int_R2 ((epsilon u)^2+v^2)^(alpha/2)
          epsilon^2 u^2/((epsilon u)^2+v^2)
          |chi_L hat(u)||g_L hat(v)| du dv.              (9)

The integrand tends to zero for every v!=0. It is dominated, for epsilon<=1, by

    (|u|+|v|)^alpha |chi_L hat(u)||g_L hat(v)|,

which is integrable because both factors are Schwartz. Dominated convergence and the Fourier estimate in section 1 therefore give

    [R1^2 f_(L,epsilon)]_alpha ->0.                      (10)

This treats the order-zero coupling itself. No product of separate first-order Riesz norms is used.

The strain has the absolutely convergent Fourier expression

    c[f]=(2pi)^(-2) int i xi_y (-xi_x^2/|xi|^2)
                                         fhat(xi) dxi.

For f_(L,epsilon), its absolute integrand after scaling is bounded by |v||chi_L hat(u)||g_L hat(v)|. It tends to zero almost everywhere by the same multiplier factor. Hence

    c[f_(L,epsilon)] ->0                                (11)

for every fixed L. This statement concerns these smooth test functions and does not claim continuity of c on X.

#### 4. Exact removal of both traces

Use the fixed Schwartz density

    q(x,y)=8 x^2 y exp(-x^2-y^2).

It satisfies q_y(0)=0, q(0,y)=0 and c[q]=1. To verify the last normalization directly, the strain kernel has no contact contribution because q_y(0)=0. In polar coordinates x^2y=r^3(sin theta+sin3theta)/4, so angular orthogonality and the radial Gaussian integral give

    c[x^2 y exp(-r^2)]
       =(1/pi)*(pi/4)*int_0^infinity r exp(-r^2) dr=1/8.

All integrals converge absolutely. This uses the already independently proved canonical kernel, not a normalization convention.

Set

    h_(L,epsilon)=f_(L,epsilon)-c[f_(L,epsilon)] q.        (12)

It is Schwartz, is in the generator domain by section 1, and has exactly zero strain and exactly zero origin y derivative. Because q(0,y)=0, its values at (0,0),(0,1) remain 0 and 1. Thus N(h_(L,epsilon))>=1/B by (3).

The fixed function (L0-mu)q has finite Holder seminorm, by the Fourier estimate already used for the domain. Equations(8),(10),(11),(12) imply that for each integer L one can choose an epsilon_L>0 so small that

    [(L0-mu)h_(L,epsilon_L)]_alpha<=C'/L.

The constant C' is independent of L. This choice is legitimate even though the support and suprema of g_L grow: L is fixed first, and every horizontal-scale term tends to zero before L is increased. Dividing h_(L,epsilon_L) by its X norm gives the unit vectors in (2), with defect at most ABC'/L.

For these smooth functions the exact origin identity is (L0h)_y(0)=a c[h]: the y derivative of y h_y-h cancels, the x term vanishes at x=0, and the Riesz term supplies the strain. Therefore the forcing of every constructed normalized vector has zero y derivative at the origin.

#### 5. Sharp semigroup and inverse bounds

The previous heat proof gives ||S_t||<=exp(mu t) and ||L0^-1||<=-1/mu. For a unit vector h in the generator domain, the semigroup differentiation formula yields

    S_t h-exp(mu t)h
       =int_0^t exp(mu(t-s)) S_s (L0-mu)h ds.

Using the upper bound, its norm is at most t exp(mu t)||(L0-mu)h||. Apply this to the sequence(2) and let n tend to infinity. It follows that ||S_t||>=exp(mu t), proving the first equality in (1).

Also ||L0 h_n||<=|mu|+||(L0-mu)h_n||, while L0^-1 L0h_n=h_n. Hence

    ||L0^-1||>=limsup_n 1/||L0 h_n||>=1/|mu|.

This proves the second equality. The same sequence already has the two exact traces, so its forcing witnesses the lower bound on the stated regular trace-compatible test class as well.

#### Dependencies and scope

The only functional-analytic input is the fully proved heat-norm semigroup, its core and the two norm comparisons in section P5.1. The strain normalization uses section P2.1. The construction, graph-domain approximation, coupling limit and normalization are proved here. No accepted-state coefficient or numerical experiment enters the argument. For alpha=1/2 the constant 2 in the heat norm is optimal; this does not assert that the converted ordinary Holder constant 486 is optimal.

## P23. Vertical-axis consequences of the matrix condition and the distance of the projected refits from it

### P23.1. What the low matrix condition forces on the vertical axis

Status: CONFIRMED check 99 (analytical restrictions) and check 100 (independent candidate certificates). Lead  No numerical scan is a continuum certificate.

#### Exact assumptions and notation

Let c be real, and let rho be a smooth real density on the full plane, even in x and odd in y. Its smooth canonical IPM velocity is

    u=(-R1 R2 rho,R1^2 rho), div u=0.

The full-plane convention and the strain c[rho]=partial_y u2(0) are those of part P1.2 and part P2, including the contact term. Assume exact center normalization c+c[rho]=1 and a0=rho_y(0)>0. Set

    q(y)=rho(0,y), v(y)=u2(0,y), V(y)=c y+v(y),
    f(y)=F(rho;c)(0,y), F=(cX+u).D rho-rho,
    M=(2c+1)I+sym Du+[[rho_y,-rho_x/2],[-rho_x/2,0]].

For a specified matrix floor kappa define

    epsilon=c+2-kappa, a=1-epsilon=kappa-c-1.

The statements below concern the actual matrix M and actual unnormalized residual. A condition only on the density, with no relation to its velocity or residual, cannot replace this matrix condition.

#### 1. Exact axial reduction and its integrated consequence

Parity gives rho_x(0,y)=u1(0,y)=u1_y(0,y)=u2_x(0,y)=0. Incompressibility gives u1_x(0,y)=-v'(y). Therefore at every point of the vertical axis

    M(0,y)=diag(2c+1-v'(y)+q'(y), 2c+1+v'(y)),           (1)
    f(y)=V(y)q'(y)-q(y).                                (2)

Consequently M(0,y)>=kappa I is exactly equivalent to the pair

    v'(y)>=kappa-2c-1,
    v'(y)<=2c+1-kappa+q'(y).                            (3)

The lower inequality can be written

    V'(y)>=a, or v'(y)>=v'(0)-epsilon.                  (4)

If (3) holds for 0<=t<=y, integration, q(0)=v(0)=0, and y>0 give

    a y<=V(y)<= (3c+1-kappa)y+q(y).                     (5)

These are necessary conditions for a global matrix floor. They are not sufficient conditions away from the axis, nor do the integrated inequalities alone imply the pointwise inequalities.

At the origin the diagonal entries are 3c+a0 and c+2. Hence every normalized reference, irrespective of its tail, has the universal ceiling

    inf_X lambda_min M(X)<=c+2.                         (6)

For the accepted c and kappa=19/5, epsilon=c-9/5 is a small positive rational number. Thus the imposed floor allows the axial velocity derivative to become more negative than its origin value by at most epsilon. This concerns local compression of the vertical velocity, rather than an assumption that a prescribed far-field angular function determines the interior.

If q'(y)>=0, (2),(5) also imply the residual condition

    f(y)>=a y q'(y)-q(y).                               (7)

It is only necessary; no residual upper bound follows from it alone.

#### 2. Shape constraint for an exact profile

Assume now F=0, a>0 and M>=kappa I on the entire vertical axis. Equation(5) gives V(y)>=a y>0 for y>0. Since q(y)=a0 y+O(y^3) near zero with a0>0, the linear equation q'=q/V shows that q stays strictly positive for every y>0. For any fixed small y0>0 its exact representation is

    q(y)=q(y0) exp(int_(y0)^y 1/V(t) dt).

On compact subintervals of (0,infinity), V has a positive lower bound, so this formula propagates positivity without an assumption about the sign of q at infinity. In particular q'(y)>0 and V=q/q'. Differentiating gives

    V'=1-K, K=q q''/(q')^2.

Substitution into (1) gives the equivalent exact-profile matrix conditions

    kappa-3c-q'<=K<=epsilon.                            (8)

If additionally epsilon<1, then a=1-epsilon>0 and

    (q^a)''=a q^(a-2)(q q''-epsilon(q')^2)<=0.           (9)

Thus q^a is concave on the positive vertical axis. This is a necessary consequence of the low matrix condition for an exact profile. In the critical case kappa=c+2, it says that q itself is concave. For the current kappa=19/5 and c=4076476460239181/2251799813685248, the exponent is a=14/5-c, about 0.98968.

Concavity is consistent with the sublinear asymptotic q(y)~Theta0(pi/2)y^(1/c) when the leading axial coefficient is positive, because 0<a/c<1 for the present parameters. The argument proves neither an obstruction from the prescribed far-field profile nor the existence of an exact profile satisfying it. It does identify a local shape restriction absent from mere tail admissibility.

For an approximate reference with q' nonzero, the exact replacement for K is

    K_f=(q+f)q''/(q')^2-f'/q'.                          (10)

Indeed differentiation of V=(q+f)/q' gives V'=1-K_f. Equations(1),(8) hold with K_f in place of K. A curvature test on an approximate q that omits f or f' is invalid. If q>0 as well, the upper matrix inequality is equivalently

    (q^a)''<=a q^(a-2)(f'q'-f q'').                     (11)

No small-residual assumption is needed for this identity and inequality. It follows by multiplying K_f<=epsilon by (q')^2, rearranging, and using the exact derivative of q^a.

#### 3. Exact center Taylor restriction

Write q=a0 y+b y^3+O(y^5) and v=(1-c)y+d y^3+O(y^5). Then V=y+d y^3+O(y^5), and direct multiplication in (2) gives

    f=(2b+a0 d)y^3+O(y^5).                              (12)

For an exact profile, d=-2b/a0. At the critical floor kappa=c+2, (4) gives v'(y)>=v'(0); expanding v' at zero shows d>=0. Thus b<=0. At a strictly smaller floor, the sign of b alone does not disprove the matrix inequality: the positive slack epsilon and the higher Taylor terms must be retained. Formula (12) explains why forcing only the center normalization is much weaker than controlling the cubic profile defect.

#### 4. Quantitative distance from the sufficient matrix class

Fix c and use the precise compatible weighted space N=N_(s,R) of part P19, with 0<s<=2^-12 andR>=1. Its reference-independent Fourier embedding gives

    ||Dh||_infinity<=4 N(h)/sqrt(s),
    ||DU[h]||_infinity<=4 N(h)/sqrt(s),                  (13)

where tensors have their Euclidean norm and the canonical velocity is used. These estimates extend to the completion, so both derivatives have continuous representatives.

Suppose a smooth reference rho has

    2c+1+partial_y u2(0,y0)<=kappa-delta0

for some y0 and delta0>0. If a correction h inN makes M_(rho+h)>=kappa I globally, then its lower axial diagonal entry must increase by at least delta0. That entry depends only on partial_y U2[h], not on the local density-gradient matrix. Consequently(13) implies the necessary distance bound

    N(h)>=delta0 sqrt(s)/4.                             (14)

This is stronger than the general off-axis estimate delta0 sqrt(s)/8 obtained from Weyl's inequality and ||sym DU[h]+A(Dh)||<=8N(h)/sqrt(s). The same conclusion holds if h is also required to have zero strain, positive corrected center slope or fixed leading tail, since these extra conditions only restrict the class of available corrections.

The assertion is about distance to this sufficient coercivity class. It does not exclude exact solutions that do not satisfy this particular matrix floor, and it is not a nonlinear nonexistence theorem. The nearby original reference or a later numerical iterate must be evaluated separately.

#### Independent numerical method and scope

The adjacent program reconstructs the accepted state from the strictly read-only original checkpoint, using its exact rational elimination formula. It also reads the already independently reconstructed exact canonical A2 and A3 potentials, tied to their supplied files by hashes. It does not call the producer's evaluation code. Cartesian Taylor jets and a separately differentiated polar polynomial representation check all previously certified fields, including the lower eigenvalue. The new axial derivative is calculated both by Cartesian jets and by differentiating an independently assembled one-dimensional axis series term by term.

Only a few rational points and the exact center jets are needed. This is a small independent computation, not a refit or a numerical global search. Numerical statements will be appended with rigorous intervals, exact inputs and actual times after this check succeeds.

#### Dependencies

Section P1.2 proves parity, the origin normalization and operator conventions. Section P19.1 proves (13) with the Euclidean velocity multiplier. Every identity(1)-(12) and the distance consequence(14) is derived here. No unverified external claim is imported.


#### Certified original and candidate consequences

The independent 768-bit computation passes all axial/Cartesian comparisons at y=1/10,1,2 for state 131, nb_stableA2_exact and nb_stableA3_exact. It reconstructs state 131 from the read-only original and binds the exact N-B source and canonical hashes. The current slack and exponent satisfy

    0.01031921019999808<epsilon<0.01031921019999809,
    0.98968078980000191<a<0.98968078980000192.

At y=1, the lower axial diagonal entries satisfy

    state 131: 4.12001312000831<M22<4.12001312000832,
    A2:       2.22252637111320<M22<2.22252637111321,

The entire required matrix is diagonal there. These individual values do not certify the original matrix globally; that separate global certificate already exists in part P4. They do refute the required floor for both N-B references.

At s=3*2^-31, equation(14) and outward comparisons show that every correction bringing A2 into the matrix class satisfies N(h)>1.4740e-5, more than 12000 times the theorem ball radius 5*2^-32. For A3 the corresponding bound is N(h)>6.2115e-6, more than 5000 times that radius. These lower bounds hold for anyR>=1 and for any additional trace or tail constraints on h. The integrated necessary condition V(1)>=a also fails: A2 has -0.065468<V(1)<-0.065467, while A3 has 0.424903<V(1)<0.424904. The original has 1.135398<V(1)<1.135399. Finally A3 at y=1 provides a concrete counterexample to omitting the residual terms in (10): its density-only ratio satisfies 0.0000777<K<0.0000778<epsilon, while 0.675079<K_f<0.675080 and M22<19/5. ## P24. A weaker low matrix hypothesis for Theorem D_w

### P24.1. A weaker low matrix hypothesis for the same weighted existence theorem

Status: independently proved below. This changes a sufficient hypothesis, not the theorem's norm or constants. It does not certify a new reference.

#### Statement

Use the exact spaces, canonical velocity, maximal distributional domains, reference conditions, and parameters of parts P19 and P21. In particular

    M=(2c+1)I+sym Du+[[rho_y,-rho_x/2],[-rho_x/2,0]]
                           >=(5/2)I on r<=R.             (1)

Then every weighted inverse, nonlinear closure, normalization, and fixed-tail conclusion of part P19 remains valid in the R=2^31 norm, with exactly the same constants. In particular, the low reference semigroup decays at rate at least 1/5; the rough high rate is

    1/20-2^23 s-400 N_(s,R)(k)/sqrt(s),

and at s=3*2^-31, r0=5*2^-32, eta=2^-35 the inverse bounds are 40 and 6, with low contraction factor less than 2/5. Existence still requires the actual residual bound N_(s,R)(F)<=eta.

#### 1. The only use of the old floor

Let g=w_Rh, phi=(-Delta)^-1g and q=Dphi. The exact weighted low energy identity is

The derivation includes every weight term and is unchanged by a different bound on M. On r<=R, t<=1/2 and Delta b0<=0. Consequently the contribution of M+b0I and Delta b0 on this region is bounded below by

       >(5/2-407/200) int_(r<=R)|q|^2
       =(93/200) int_(r<=R)|q|^2
       >(2/5) int_(r<=R)|q|^2.                          (2)

Thus the old floor 19/5 was stronger than required for the baseline 2/5. Neither a change of weight nor an altered matrix energy is involved.

#### 2. Exterior and commutator terms

For r>=R the coefficient bounds already imply

    M >= [2c+1-(C_DU+C_rho)R^-d] I.

The radial circle Poincare inequality

    int a(r) phi^2 <= int r^2 a(r)|Dphi|^2, a>=0,

applies to the positive part of Delta b0 on this region. The same exact cubic maximum as in LOW_INVERSE_PROOF gives

    t+2t(1-t)(2t-1)<=21/20, 1/2<=t<=1.

The exterior baseline is therefore

    2c+1-(21/20)sigma c
       =1-31c/100 >853/2000>2/5.                        (3)

The loss from C_DU+C_rho is included in the global error below. The velocity-weight terms and the real radial coupling commutator are independent of the floor in (1). parts P6 and P7 and P21 bound their total, together with that exterior coefficient loss, by

    R^-d [C_DU+(1+21/2)C_rho
                   +sigma(9C_U+2C_DU+C_D2U/sqrt(2))].    (4)

At the stated tuple and radius, the already certified rational estimate is

    2/5-(4) >14093/70000>1/5.

Combining(2)-(4) proves the identical low coercivity. The weak-circle treatment of the radial term and ordinary parity Hardy bound for b1 are precisely the previous ones; there are no omitted interface fluxes, because the proof restricts the original integrals and applies a circle inequality rather than integrating by parts across r=R.

#### 3. Generator, high inverse, and nonlinear closure

The low generator construction uses the smooth complete transport flow and the bounded canonical weighted coupling. Its domain construction needs the structure and coefficient regularity, not a particular numerical matrix floor. The positive energy margin supplies both the semigroup decay and the convergent inverse integral. Thus injectivity and surjectivity persist.

The weighted first and second derivative estimates of SHARP_WEIGHTED_H2_PROOF use the low margin 1/5, W2, W3 and universal Riesz bounds. Their displayed energy identities have no further use of the number 19/5. They still yield the E_R semigroup rate 1/20. Their constants are unchanged.

The trace identity, complete high ball in the low metric, bilinear difference estimate and fixed leading profile likewise use only the already retained hypotheses. Thus the entire conditional theorem transfers, without treating a mere energy inequality as a proof of surjectivity.

#### 4. Interpretation and limits

The axial shape restrictions in part P23 were proved for a specified floor kappa. They remain correct at kappa=19/5, including the certified A2/A3 distances to that stronger matrix class. They do not say that this stronger class is necessary for a weighted existence theorem. At kappa=5/2 the parameter kappa-c-1 is negative, so the positive-power concavity conclusion from that part cannot be invoked.

In particular, failure of M>=19I/5 alone no longer disproves applicability of the conditional theorem with this weaker hypothesis. One must check(1), both W2 matrices, every W3 derivative bound, decay coefficients, normalization, membership and actual smallness for the particular reference. No A2,A3 or later candidate is declared admissible for the full theorem by this result.

## P25. An annular lower bound for the residuals of two exactly admissible projected refits

### P25.1. A far-field residual lower bound for the exactly admissible N-B references

Status: analytical proof and numerical lower bounds CONFIRMED by the independent check (check 103); independently reviewed CORRECT by the draft (check 110). Scope: the two named candidates only.

#### Statement, spaces and exact input class

Let rho be the density of an exact finite canonical potential

    chi=sum a_(j,m,k) r^(2k)(1+r^2)^(p_j-k) cos(2m theta),
    p_j=(3+gamma-j delta)/2, gamma=1/c, delta=1-gamma,
    rho=-partial_y Delta chi,
    u=(-partial_x partial_y^2 chi,partial_x^2 partial_y chi).

Here c is the accepted state 131 exponent,0<=j<=5,0<=m<=59,m<=k<=75. Coefficients are exact rationals. The canonical velocity convention is the one proved in part P1.2. Assume that the residual F=(cX+u).D rho-rho has no nonzero sector with radial exponent larger than

    p_star=gamma-6delta=-8696260065638350/4076476460239181,

and that its p_star angular polynomial is E_star(theta)=sum e_m sin(m theta), not identically zero. These finite exact conditions must be checked for the particular input. They hold for the independently audited A2 and A3 references, whose six leading potential branches coincide with the stationary tail determined by the original leading profile. This proof does not impose an unproved uniform bound on all possible free coefficients in the enlarged family.

For R>=1 set w_R=(1+r^2/R^2)^(-11/10), L_R(F)=||w_R F||_(dot H^-1), and N_(s,R)=E_R(J^s F), with the weights, Euclidean derivative norms and completion of part P19. For 0<s<=2^-12, the already proved inverse Bessel comparison gives

    N_(s,R)(F)>=2^(53/2)L_R(F)/6.                        (1)

These inputs are smooth symbols of degree p_star<-2 and their derivatives have the corresponding decay. Hence the required spaces and the canonical Bessel comparison apply, by the same completed-space argument as in section P21.2. Membership is checked before using (1).

#### 1. One combined angular test, allowing signed subleading sectors

Choose T>=1 and set chi0(t)=(t-1)^2(2-t)^2 on [1,2], zero elsewhere. Put

    d_m=1/35+m^2/630,
    phi(r,theta)=chi0(r/T) sum_m(e_m/d_m)sin(m theta),
    S=sum_m e_m^2/d_m, A=sum_m |e_m|/d_m.

This is a compact C1 test in homogeneous H1, with the density parity. Exact polynomial integration gives integral chi0=1/30, integral chi0^2=1/630 and integral t(chi0')^2=1/35. Angular orthogonality and 1/t<=1 on [1,2] give

    ||D phi||_2^2<=pi S.                                (2)

Suppose a finite exact sector residual F_t=sum_(h,q) r^p E_(h,q)(theta) has the same leading sector E_star, and every other nonzero sector has p<p_star. Write

    C_(h,q)=sum_m e_m E_(h,q,m)/d_m,
    B=sum_(p<p_star) max(0,-C_(h,q)) T^(p-p_star).

If |F-F_t|<=Ctail r^p_star for every r>=T, then each normalized sine coefficient of the error is bounded by (4/pi)Ctail<2Ctail. Consequently the signed angular pairing coefficient obeys

    sum_m(e_m/d_m) F_m(r)/r^p_star
         >= S-B-2 Ctail A=:b, r>=T.                     (3)

Positive subleading cross coefficients are discarded; negative ones are bounded using their decreasing powers. This avoids the unnecessary requirement that every individual leading mode dominate its remainder. Assume b>0.

On T<=r<=2T, w_R>=W=(1+4T^2/R^2)^(-11/10). Since p_star+1<0, the radial factor satisfies t^(p_star+1)>=2^(p_star+1). The power has the opposite sign from the growing-residual test in part P21 and must be retained. Equations(2)-(3) give

    L_R(F)>=sqrt(pi) b T^(p_star+2) W 2^(p_star+1)
                                               /(30 sqrt(S)).    (4)

Every factor is positive. The exact test uses all nonzero leading modes and is a single duality witness, rather than a sum of unrelated norm lower bounds.

#### 2. Complete uniform binomial remainder

Retain potential binomial orders 0<=q<=Q, where Q=3 and q0=4. For each branch j and order q, form the exact angular potential polynomial by summing a_(j,m,k) binom(p_j-k,q) cos(2m theta). Cartesian differentiation gives the density, velocity, and every derivative through order 4. Form F_t by exact polynomial products. All cancellations are performed before taking absolute values.

For d=3,4 let B_(d,j,q) be the maximum component sum of absolute complex Fourier coefficients of that differentiated potential sector. Define

    M_d=sum_(j,q<=Q) B_(d,j,q) T^(-j delta-2q),
    A_j=sum_(m,k)|a_(j,m,k)|,
    tau_d=((q0+76)/(q0+1))
                      *((2q0+130)/(2q0+128))^d/T^2,
    T_d=binom(q0+75,q0)(2q0+128)^d T^(-2q0)
                  sum_j A_j T^(-j delta)/(1-tau_d).      (5)

The actual exact index bounds imply |p_j-k|<76 and

    |3+gamma-j delta|+2m+2(d-1)<128, d<=4.

Thus |binom(p_j-k,q)|<=binom(q+75,q). Each Cartesian derivative multiplies the Fourier coefficient sum by at most 2q+128. The omitted-term majorant ratio is at most tau_d, and both rational factors in that ratio decrease with q. Whenever tau_d<1, the geometric sum proves, for r>=T,

    |D^d chi_t|_(each component)<=M_d r^(gamma+3-d),
    |D^d(chi-chi_t)|_(each component)
          <=T_d(T/r)^(2q0) r^(gamma+3-d).               (6)

Density is a sum of two third derivatives and velocity has two individual third derivatives. Therefore the same Euclidean product calculation as in part P21 gives

    |F-F_t|/r^p_star<=Ctail,
    Ctail=(2sqrt(2)c T4+2T3) T^(gamma-p_star)
          +4(T3M4+M3T4+T3T4) T^(2gamma-1-p_star).       (7)

To take the sup at r=T, one uses 2q0>gamma-p_star=6delta and 2q0>2gamma-1-p_star=5delta. Both strict inequalities hold for the exact exponent. For the product of two omitted tails, discarding one factor (T/r)^(2q0)<=1 is permissible. No uniform coefficient bound other than the finite actual sums A_j is assumed.

Equations(5)-(7) are a full pointwise estimate, not an asymptotic numerical fit. The retained exact residual sectors and actual majorant quantities are stored with the certificate. Independent Cartesian evaluation at large rational-direction points checks their signs and phases; that check supports the implementation but does not replace the uniform proof.

#### 3. Independent source reconstruction and verification

The program expands every supplied monomial or Legendre generator using exact integer binomial coefficients and reconstructs the canonical rational vector afresh. It compares the exact source and canonical hashes against the earlier independent admissibility audit. The original leading potential and exponent are independently recovered from the strictly read-only original checkpoint. No evaluator or sector code of the numerical work is imported.

The program represents each angular polynomial by Laurent coefficients with explicit powers of i for Cartesian y derivatives, and multiplies them with exact rational polynomial convolution. It verifies the vanishing of every residual sector above p_star, the original leading profile, and the exact equality of the A2/A3 leading residual sectors. It checks all numerical claims with 768-bit Arb. The large-point Cartesian evaluation uses a distinct full-potential Taylor expansion, without the exterior series.

#### Scope

A lower bound from (4) concerns the specified exact reference and norm. It does not certify a norm upper bound, a uniform obstruction for arbitrarily large coefficients, or nonexistence of an exact solution. Cancellation of the eight sectors above -2 proves membership but does not, by itself, imply quantitative smallness. The purpose of this test is to measure that remaining gap for the supplied admissible references.

## P26. Necessary point tests of the full reference contract for the projected refits

### P26.1. Necessary point tests for the full reference contract

#### Statement and scope

Use the weighted fractional norm N_(s,R) of parts P19 and P21, with R>=1 and 0<s<=2^-12. The sufficient reference contract in section P17.6 requires the global Euclidean tensor bound |D^2 rho|<=3, even after the low matrix hypothesis is weakened in part P24. At every point, |rho_yy|<=|D^2 rho|. Thus a rigorously enclosed value |rho_yy|>3 at one point refutes that particular contract for the supplied reference. No conclusion about the existence of an exact profile, a theorem with larger derivative constants, or other references follows.

The same norm has the reference-independent point evaluation bound

    |f(X)| <= 16 max(1,|X|^(1/5)) N_(s,R)(f)

on its density parity completion. This is part P19's embedding, proved through the Bessel kernel and weighted interpolation; it needs no reference matrix certificate. Therefore every rigorously evaluated nonzero residual at a fixed point supplies a norm lower bound. This remains valid for the admissible candidate residuals, whose smooth tail has degree gamma-6delta<-2 and hence belongs to the completed forcing space.

#### Independent evaluation

The exact candidate coefficient vector is reconstructed in part P20. For A2 and A3, the part P23 certificate differentiates the full Cartesian potential through order seven and independently differentiates its one-dimensional restriction to the vertical axis. Writing Phi(y)=chi(0,y) and A_x(y)=chi_xx(0,y), the two methods compare

    q''(y)=rho_yy(0,y)=-chi_xxyyy(0,y)-chi_yyyyy(0,y)
                        =-A_x'''(y)-Phi'''''(y).

Both methods use 768-bit Arb. The new check binds those records to their exact source and dependency hashes, compares the saved enclosures, and tests the strict endpoint inequalities. The complete two-method identity is established in section P23.1; using it here does not introduce a fresh unverified derivative formula.

For the A4 residual point bound, use X=(3,4), so |X|=5. Part P20's independent Cartesian and polar evaluations give the same Arb enclosure of F(3,4). Dividing its absolute lower bound by 16*5^(1/5) gives a strict lower bound for N_(s,R)(F). The present check performs this division with directed interval arithmetic. It does not estimate a norm upper bound or certify any global coefficient inequality.

#### Findings

The completed check records strict values and verdicts. A2 and A3 violate |D^2 rho|<=3 at (0,1/10), separately from their violations of the older 19/5 matrix floor. The weaker matrix theorem consequently does not by itself make them valid references for the complete current contract. A4 has a certified positive residual lower bound even if its coefficient hypotheses were all to pass. Later references require their own checks.

## P27. A uniform unweighted residual bound for the fitting family

### P27.1. A uniform residual obstruction for the fixed finite N-B family

Status: CONFIRMED check 106 by independent algebra and arithmetic, and by a second independent review of the argument. This is a lower bound for the unweighted Route U norm. No uniform weighted obstruction is asserted.

#### 1. Exact statement, family and dependencies

Put c=4076476460239181/2251799813685248, gamma=1/c and delta=1-gamma. Consider any real potential

    chi=sum_(0<=j<=5, 0<=m<=59, m<=k<=75) a_(j,m,k)
             r^(2k)(1+r^2)^((3+gamma-j delta)/2-k)cos(2m theta).

Set rho=-partial_y Delta chi, U=(-chi_xyy,chi_xxy) and F=(cX+U).D rho-rho. The function is smooth on the plane and has the density parity. Its subquadratic stream function is the canonical one by the uniqueness statement of part P1.2. Impose these exact affine constraints on the potential coefficients:

1. For each j=0,...,5, the leading cosine polynomial sum_(m,k) a_(j,m,k)cos(2m theta) is C_(j+1), the six stationary homogeneous potential profiles uniquely determined by the full leading angular profile of original state 131. parts P3 and P10.2 construct these profiles. Their exact rational coefficients are in certificate file state131_splice.json.
2. For j=0,1, the first descendant cosine polynomial sum_(m,k) a_(j,m,k)((3+gamma-j delta)/2-k)cos(2m theta) vanishes.

The center normalization may also be imposed but is not needed for this lower bound. Coefficients may be arbitrarily large. The exact A2, A3, A4, A5 and Mpen references satisfy these constraints whenever their separate canonical audits pass. The larger displayed index set is intentional and contains their supports.

Write e(theta)=sum_m e_m sin(m theta) for the residual coefficient at degree p_star=gamma-6delta=1-7delta. It is fixed by the six leading branches and is independent of every remaining coefficient. Only odd m=1,...,139 occur, and its full-circle L2 norm is greater than 3081.27. Define

    a0=7delta/2-2,
    A={ell delta/2+k-2 : 1<=ell<=12, 0<=k<=154,
                                  ell delta/2+k-2>=a0}.

List the 1852 distinct elements increasingly as a0,a1,...,a1851. Define

    D=(2a0+1)^(-1/2) product_(j=1)^1851 (a_j-a0)/(a_j+a0+1),
    C_D^2=sum_j a_j^2+sum_(i<j)(2a_i+1)(2a_j+1).

Then every potential in the family satisfies

    ||F||_(dot H^-1)^2 >= (pi/2) D^2
                      sum_m e_m^2/[m^2+(1+2C_D)^2].                 (1)

The 384-bit evaluation and independent 512-bit audit gives the right-hand square root greater than 2.67750e-7. For the Route U norm N_s=E2(J^s .), s=2^-18, the established reverse comparison N_s(F)>=(1-34s)E2(F) and the negative component of E2 give

    N_s(F)>=(1-34s)sqrt((20/21)2^18)||F||_(dot H^-1)
           >0.00013376.                                          (2)

This exceeds 210 times eta_U=1/1572864. Thus no member of this particular finite family can satisfy the existing Route U sufficient residual threshold, even with arbitrary real coefficients. This is neither a nonexistence theorem for IPM nor a lower bound for arbitrary reference families. Adding a branch, changing the leading profile or exponent, or increasing the degree changes the argument and its constants.

Numerical inequalities in this statement become certified only after the accompanying verification program and audit record pass. The norm definition and reverse comparison are in parts P8 and P14; no background matrix or coefficient assumption is used to compare norms.

#### 2. Exact finite power representation

Put u=(1+r^2)^(-1), t=1-u. Part P12 derives, by repeated Cartesian differentiation expressed in polar variables,

    F_m(r)=sqrt(1-u)u^(-1/2) H_m(u),
    H_m(u)=sum_(ell=1)^12 u^(ell delta/2) P_(ell,m)(1-u).           (3)

Here every P is a real polynomial of degree at most 153. To check this degree rather than assume it, a d-th derivative of one potential generator has, after its common radial factor is removed, powers t^(k-2+l), 0<=l<=d. At d=3 the degree is at most k+1<=76; at d=4 it is at most k+2<=77. Negative powers cancel for each generator separately because k>=m makes that generator smooth. Each generator has one fixed radial exponent, so its angular polynomial after differentiation is divisible by the power of t needed for origin regularity. This assertion is applied before summing distinct radial exponent classes. The nonlinear term multiplies a third derivative and a fourth derivative and therefore has degree at most 153. The linear terms have degree at most 77. The branch number of a single derivative is ell=j+1, while a nonlinear product adds two such branch numbers. Thus 1<=ell<=12 contains every residual term. This reasoning allows zero polynomials and does not assume that all possible powers are actually attained.

The exact rational delta makes every ell delta/2+k in the displayed finite ranges distinct. The leading stationary conditions cancel the sectors with j=0,...,5 and q=0; the two descendant conditions cancel the sectors(j,q)=(0,1),(1,1). The relation between the exterior expansion and (3) is triangular within each fractional power class. These are exactly the eight exponents below lambda_star=7delta/2 in (3). Hence they vanish there too. The next exponent is lambda_star and its coefficient is e_m. Since no potential branch j=6 is present, that residual coefficient consists solely of the quadratic interactions of branches i+j=5, so it is fixed. Multiplication by 1-u does not change it.

Set

    w_m(u)=(1-u)u^(-2)H_m(u).

This belongs to the real power space V=span{u^a:a in A} and its u^a0 coefficient is e_m. The additional factor 1-u accounts for the degree 154 in A. Since a0>-1/2, all powers in V are square integrable. No assertion that an arbitrary element of V is a nonlinear residual is required: using the larger linear space weakens a valid lower bound.

#### 3. Distance of one power from a finite span

Let -1/2<a0<a1<...<an. In L2(0,1), the distance of u^a0 from span{u^a1,...,u^an} is

    D=(2a0+1)^(-1/2) product_(j=1)^n (a_j-a0)/(a_j+a0+1).          (4)

Distinct powers are linearly independent: setting u=exp(t) gives distinct exponentials, whose derivatives have a nonzero Vandermonde determinant at any interior t. Their Gram matrix is therefore positive definite. Let q be the orthogonal residual of u^a0. Its Mellin transform Q(z)=int_0^1 q(u)u^z du is rational, with simple poles at-a_j-1, zeros at a1,...,an, and residue 1 at-a0-1. Its numerator has degree at most n, so these conditions give

    Q(z)=C product_(j=1)^n(z-a_j)/product_(j=0)^n(z+a_j+1),
    C=product_(j=1)^n(a0-a_j)/(a0+a_j+1).

The residue condition fixes this constant, including its sign. Orthogonality gives ||q||2^2=<q,u^a0>=Q(a0), which is the square of (4). Consequently every element of V whose u^a0 coefficient is e has norm at least|e|D. The minimizing orthogonal projection exists in this finite-dimensional space, so this is an exact distance formula.

#### 4. A norm bound for dilation

The operator B=u partial_u preserves V. For f,g in V, integration by parts gives

    <Bf,g>+<f,Bg>=f(1)g(1)-<f,g>.                               (5)

The endpoint at zero vanishes because every exponent in u f g is positive. Gram-Schmidt in increasing exponent order gives orthonormal polynomials p_j in the powers, each in span{u^a0,...,u^aj}. Thus B has a triangular matrix with diagonal a_j. Taking f=g=p_j in (5) yields p_j(1)^2=2a_j+1. For i<j, Bp_i belongs to the earlier span and is orthogonal to p_j. Taking f=p_i,g=p_j in (5) therefore shows that the other triangular entry has square(2a_i+1)(2a_j+1). The Frobenius norm bounds the operator norm, proving

    ||Bw||2<=C_D||w||2.                                          (6)

This is not a spectral-radius estimate and does not assume that B is self-adjoint.

#### 5. The actual homogeneous negative norm

For one sine mode m>=1, let s=log r and g_m(s)=r^2F_m(r). Writing the potential of -Delta in these variables gives

    ||F_m(r)sin(m theta)||_(dot H^-1)^2
        =pi <g_m,(-partial_s^2+m^2)^(-1)g_m>_L2(ds).              (7)

Indeed the radial Poisson equation becomes -phi_ss+m^2 phi=g_m and its Dirichlet energy is pi int(phi_s^2+m^2 phi^2)ds. The positive cylinder operator has inverse kernel exp(-m|s-t|)/(2m). For g_m in L2, this is the unique H1 cylinder solution, and hence realizes the homogeneous inverse in this angular sector. Approximation by smooth compactly supported cylinder functions justifies the pairing and identifies it with the completion of the full-plane Dirichlet space. There is no zero angular mode.

In the present finite family g_m belongs to H1(R). At r=0 the smooth odd residual is O(r), so g_m and its s derivative decay at least like r^3. At infinity F has a differentiable expansion beginning at p_star<-2, so g_m and its derivative decay exponentially in s. The same conclusion also follows directly from the formulas below and (6).

For a positive operator A=-partial_s^2+m^2, Cauchy-Schwarz gives

    <g,A^-1g> >= ||g||2^4/(||g'||2^2+m^2||g||2^2).               (8)

Using r^2=(1-u)/u and |ds|=du/[2u(1-u)], direct substitution gives

    ||g_m||2^2=(1/2)||w_m||2^2,
    ||g_m'||2^2=(1/2)||(-1+2u)w_m-2u(1-u)w_m'||2^2.             (9)

Since |2u-1|<=1 and |1-u|<=1, equations(4),(6),(9) imply

    ||g_m||2>=|e_m|D/sqrt(2),
    ||g_m'||2<=(1+2C_D)||g_m||2.

Equations(7)-(8) now prove(1) for each mode. Distinct sine modes are orthogonal in the Dirichlet energy, so their squared bounds add. This proves the stated full norm inequality.

#### 6. Scope of the obstruction

This argument controls the actual unweighted negative norm, rather than merely the proxy ||rF||2. The factor C_D is essential for that passage. The degree bound and all eight cancellations are also essential.

The weighted norm L_R(F)=||(1+r^2/R^2)^(-11/10)F||_(dot H^-1) is not bounded below by a fixed multiple of the unweighted norm on arbitrary functions. Its multiplier changes the finite power space. Therefore (1)-(2) do not establish a coefficient-independent weighted gap. The previously certified weighted annular gaps remain statements about their particular exact candidates. A separate argument is required for a uniform weighted bound.

## P28. Point tests of the reference contract for four later projected refits

### P28.1. Point tests for the later exact N-B candidates and axis corrections

Status: analytical identities and individual point certificates CONFIRMED (check 107-check 109). The stated global W3 requirements are REFUTED for A4, A5 and Mpen. This is not a global positivity certificate.

#### 1. Exact inputs and tested quantities

Each candidate is the real finite potential reconstructed independently in part P20 from its own exact N-B JSON file. The source and canonical hashes identify the function. Its density is rho=-chi_xxy-chi_yyy and its canonical velocity is u=(-chi_xyy,chi_xxy). The previously proved compactification and canonical uniqueness apply. Center normalization and the stationary branch constraints are checked separately by exact rational arithmetic.

For every multi-index I=(i,j), the exact derivative identities are

    partial^I rho=-chi_(i+2,j+1)-chi_(i,j+3),
    partial^I u=(-chi_(i+1,j+2),chi_(i+2,j+1)).

An ordered tensor norm of order k is the square root of the sum over i=0,...,k with multiplicity binom(k,i). For the velocity, both vector components are included. This convention is the one used in W3. Squaring intervals is performed by integer powers, so no negative square root is introduced by treating a value as two independent intervals.

At a point X define A=[[rho_y,-rho_x/2],[-rho_x/2,0]], V=cX+u and

    M=(2c+1)I+sym Du+A,
    M_k=(1+c+V.D log omega_k)I-k sym(cI+Du)+A,
    omega1=(1+r^2)^(-1/10), omega2=(1+4r^2)^(2/5).

Here V.D log omega1=-(V.X)/(5(1+r^2)) and V.D log omega2=16(V.X)/(5(1+4r^2)). The factor 16 in the latter formula includes differentiation of 4r^2. Each symmetric 2 by 2 least eigenvalue is obtained from the trace-minus-discriminant formula.

The W3 tests are |Du|<=14/5, |D rho|<=16, <r>|D2u|<=3, <r>|D3u|<=16, |D2rho|<=3, <r>|D2rho|<=8, <r>^2|D3rho|<=32 and <r>^2|D4rho|<=512. W2 requires both M_k>=I/2. A certified violation at one point disproves the corresponding global requirement. Passing every selected point leaves that global requirement open.

Every point is evaluated both by Cartesian Taylor jets through order 7 and by a separately differentiated polar polynomial recurrence. Both use the exact canonical coefficients, without importing the numerical producer's evaluator. The two enclosures must overlap and be finite before a result is recorded.

#### 2. Residual point lower bounds

For the weighted space of parts P17, P19 and P21, the reference-independent inequality

    |g(X)|<=16 max(1,r)^(1/5) N_(s,R)(g)

holds for 0<s<=2^-12 and R>=1. Therefore every certified nonzero value of the actual residual gives

    N_(s,R)(F)>=|F(X)|/[16 max(1,r)^(1/5)].

This is a lower bound on the complete norm. It gives no upper bound and does not imply nonexistence. The threshold compared below is eta=2^-35.

#### 3. Correct axis identities

Write q(y)=rho(0,y), v(y)=u2(0,y). Parity and incompressibility give

    M(0,y)=diag(2c+1-v'(y)+q'(y),2c+1+v'(y)).

Consequently the second diagonal entry is the least eigenvalue if and only if q'(y)>=2v'(y). Diagonality by itself does not imply this ordering. The correct velocity derivative is

    psi_xy(0,y)=partial_y u2(0,y)=-partial_x u1(0,y).

In contrast, -partial_y u1=psi_yy, which vanishes on x=0 by oddness of psi in x. These correct the general statement made in the numerical work. They do not dispute its individually evaluated second diagonal entries.

The missing ordering cannot be supplied from S1 parity and center normalization alone. To see this, start with the normalized original potential and add t times

    chi_b=(x^2/4)[(y-1)^2 zeta(x^2+(y-1)^2)
                      +(y+1)^2 zeta(x^2+(y+1)^2)],

where zeta is smooth, equals 1 near 0 and vanishes for arguments>=1/4. This is even in both coordinates, vanishes near the origin, and is compactly supported. Its density and stream are therefore canonical perturbations preserving the center and the entire far field. At (0,1), chi_b,xxyy=1 and chi_b,yyyy=0. Thus q'-2v' changes by -3t. For large positive t the first matrix entry is smaller. This is a counterexample to the claimed implication within smooth, normalized, sublinear S1 references.

Finally let

    rho=a0 y+b y^3+d x^2y+O(r^5),
    psi=(1-c)xy+Bxy^3+Cx^3y+O(r^6), lambda=2c-1.

Direct multiplication in F=(cX+u).D rho-rho gives

    F_3=(2b+a0B)y^3+(2lambda d+3a0C)x^2y.

This confirms the cubic identity in the numerical work. Cubic stationarity implies B=-2b/a0. Locally the second matrix entry is c+2+3By^2+O(y^4), and it is the smaller one near 0 because the first origin value exceeds it when a0>=1 and c>9/5. A positive cubic density coefficient b is compatible with a strictly lower floor kappa<c+2 on a sufficiently small neighborhood. A sign conclusion b<=0 from this expansion requires the zero-margin floor kappa=c+2, or an additional quantitative neighborhood condition. Part P23 supplies the complete residual-aware axis inequalities.

## P29. The fixed tail sector alone does not force a weighted residual gap

### P29.1. Limits of a tail-invariant argument in the weighted norm

Status: CONFIRMED check 111 by independent recurrence and arithmetic checks, and by a second independent review of the argument. The constructed functions are residual-shaped functions in a linear relaxation. They are not asserted to be residuals of any IPM potential.

#### 1. Statement and purpose

Use the exact c, delta, a0=7delta/2-2, leading sine coefficients e_m and degree bound 154 of part P27. Put mu=11/10, R=2^31, w_R=(1+r^2/R^2)^(-mu), and define

    P1(f)=||<r>^(-1/5) Df||2,
    P2(f)=||(1+4r^2)^(2/5) D2f||2,
    L_R(f)=||w_R f||_(dot H^-1),
    E_R(f)^2=P2(f)^2+2^22 P1(f)^2+2^53 L_R(f)^2,
    N_(s,R)(f)=E_R((1-Delta)^(s/2)f), 0<s<=1/2.

All tensor norms are ordered Cartesian Frobenius norms. The spaces are the compact parity completions used in parts P17 and P19. We construct a smooth even-x, odd-y function f with f_y(0)=0, leading tail r^(1-7delta)e(theta), all eight preceding sectors zero, and exactly the finite power representation allowed for residuals in part P27. An explicit bound for its complete N_(s,R) norm is given below. The certified value below 2^-35 shows that the fixed leading tail and the finite power representation alone do not exclude the weighted sufficient residual threshold. Such a result does not imply the existence of an IPM reference with small residual.

#### 2. An explicit finite-dimensional construction

For each odd m with e_m nonzero, put

    M_m=(m+1)/2+4, K_m=154-M_m,
    A_m={ell delta/2+k-2 : 1<=ell<=12, 0<=k<=K_m,
                             ell delta/2+k-2>=a0}.

Let q_m be the unique element of span{u^a:a in A_m} whose u^a0 coefficient is 1 and whose norm ||u^mu q_m||_L2(0,1) is minimal. Existence and uniqueness follow from the positive definite Gram matrix. The orthogonal projection formula of part P27 makes this an exact definition using rational arithmetic. In particular

    D_m:=||u^mu q_m||2
       =(2(a0+mu)+1)^(-1/2)
          product_(a in A_m, a>a0) (a-a0)/(a+a0+2mu+1).

Set u=(1+r^2)^(-1), t=1-u, and

    f_m(r,theta)=e_m u^(3/2) t^(M_m-1/2) q_m(u) sin(m theta),
    f=sum_m f_m.

At infinity the u^a0 coefficient is 1, so the leading tail is the required one. There are no smaller exponents. The compactified quantity w_m=t u^-2 H_m equals t^M_m q_m and has degree at most 154 in the integer power variable; H_m=u^2 t^(M_m-1)q_m has degree at most 153. Thus it has precisely the larger finite power representation of part P27. No claim is made that its coefficients satisfy the nonlinear identities of an actual residual.

At the origin, t^(M_m-1/2)sin(m theta) is r^(m+8) times a smooth radial analytic factor and sin(m theta). Since m is odd, r^m sin(m theta) is a homogeneous polynomial of the correct parity. All other factors are smooth functions of r^2 there. Hence f is smooth and its low center jets vanish. At infinity it and each derivative have the differentiated power decay of r^(1-7delta). Smooth radial cutoffs approximate it in all the weighted norms below.

#### 3. Dilation and derivative bounds

Write g_m=u^mu q_m. This belongs to the power space with exponents a+mu for a in A_m. The exact dilation estimate of part P27 gives

    ||(u partial_u)^j g_m||2<=C_m^j D_m,
    C_m^2=sum_(a in A_m)(a+mu)^2
              +sum_(a<b)(2(a+mu)+1)(2(b+mu)+1).

Define A_(m,0)=1 and, for 1<=k<=4,

    A_(m,k)=product_(j=0)^(k-1)(4C_m+2m+48/5+6j).

For each Cartesian derivative of order k, the complex polar derivative formulas produce a sum of angular modes with radial factor

    u^(alpha+k/2)t^(beta-k/2),
    alpha=2/5, beta=m/2+4,

times a polynomial in u applied to (u partial_u)^j g_m, j<=k. The sum of coefficient norms, with C_m^j as weights, is at most A_(m,k). Here coefficient norm means the sum of the absolute monomial coefficients. To verify the recurrence, use

    partial_x +/- i partial_y
       =exp(+/- i theta) r^-1(r partial_r +/- i partial_theta),
    r partial_r=-2ut partial_u.

After k steps the polynomial degree is at most k and the current angular order has absolute value at most m+k. The derivative of a coefficient polynomial costs at most 4k in coefficient norm; the derivative of g costs at most 4C_m; the radial prefactor and angular term together cost at most 2m+48/5+2k. Their sum proves the stated factor with 6k. The factors beta-k/2 remain positive for k<=4. Expressing each Cartesian derivative as an average of the complex derivatives does not increase this bound.

There are 2^k ordered Cartesian components. Bounding each angular function by its coefficient sum and using the angular measure2pi and radial measure du/(2u^2) therefore gives

    ||omega1 D^k f_m||2
       <=2^(k/2)sqrt(pi)|e_m| A_(m,k) D_m,        k>=1,
    ||omega2 D^k f_m||2
       <=4^(2/5)2^(k/2)sqrt(pi)|e_m| A_(m,k) D_m, k>=2,
    ||r w_R D^k f_m||2
       <=R^(2mu)2^(k/2)sqrt(pi)|e_m| A_(m,k) D_m, k>=0,

for k<=4. For example the squared u powers after the measure are k-1 for the first estimate and k-2 for the second, hence nonnegative. For the last estimate use w_R<=R^(2mu)u^mu; its squared u power is k. All remaining t powers are nonnegative. Also omega2<=4^(2/5)u^(-2/5). These facts justify dropping the remaining factors by 1, including at the endpoints.

Every f_m is centrally odd. The parity Hardy inequality gives L_R(h)<=||r w_R h||2 for it and for Delta f_m. Taking a trace costs at mostsqrt(2), so

    E_R(f_m-Delta f_m)
      <=sqrt(pi)|e_m|D_m [
          4^(2/5)(2A_(m,2)+4sqrt(2)A_(m,4))
          +2^11(sqrt(2)A_(m,1)+4A_(m,3))
          +2^(53/2)R^(2mu)(1+2sqrt(2)A_(m,2)) ].       (1)

The use of a sum of the three components, rather than their Euclidean combination, only enlarges the bound.

#### 4. Bessel regularization and the complete norm

For 0<tau<=2, the positive Bessel kernel of J^-tau=(1-Delta)^(-tau/2) is the heat mixture with gamma time parameter tau/2. Each radial moment of order 0 through 4 is at most the corresponding moment of J^-2. This follows either by the gamma convolution identity, with a nonnegative independent gamma time of parameter 1-tau/2 added, or directly by integrating the beta identity. Thus

    integral (1+|z|)^4 b_tau(z) dz <=89+20pi<152.

The weight ratios for omega1, omega2, w_R and <r>w_R are all bounded by (1+|z|)^4. The weighted L2 norm of J^-tau is therefore at most 152 for these weights. The exact divergence decomposition in section P17.4, section 4, then gives

    L_R(J^-tau h)<=(1+4mu)152 L_R(h)<821 L_R(h).

The derivatives commute with this convolution, so E_R(J^-tau h)<=821 E_R(h). This is a bounded operator on the same compact parity completion; it does not use translation invariance of the weighted negative norm.

Taking tau=2-s yields J^s f=J^-(2-s)(f-Delta f). Consequently, for every 0<s<=1/2,

    N_(s,R)(f)<=821 sum_m E_R(f_m-Delta f_m),             (2)

with each summand bounded by (1). All terms are explicit algebraic expressions in the exact exponent and leading coefficients, except positive square roots and fixed positive powers, which can be enclosed by ball arithmetic.

#### 5. Scope

The functions just constructed retain smooth parity, center compatibility, the fixed leading residual coefficient, all earlier cancellations, and the finite degree/power restrictions used in the uniform Route U obstruction. Their coefficients have not been shown to arise from (cX+U[rho]).D rho-rho. The nonlinear realizability constraint is therefore essential to any stronger weighted exclusion. Neither a low residual IPM reference nor an exact IPM solution follows from this construction.

## P30. Necessary residual scales for the weighted theorem

### P30.1. Necessary residual scales for the present weighted theorem

Status: proved by the two already verified general embeddings below. These are necessary consequences of the sufficient smallness condition, not sufficient tests for the full norm.

#### Exact statement

Let R>=1 and 0<s<=2^-12. Use the compact parity completion N_(s,R) of parts P17 and P19, with

    w_R=(1+r^2/R^2)^(-11/10), L_R(f)=||w_R f||_(dot H^-1),
    E_R(f)^2=||(1+4r^2)^(2/5)D2f||2^2
                +2^22||<r>^(-1/5)Df||2^2+2^53 L_R(f)^2,
    N_(s,R)(f)=E_R(J^s f), J=(1-Delta)^(1/2).

All derivatives are ordered Cartesian tensors, and f denotes the continuous representative supplied by the embedding. If N_(s,R)(f)<=2^-35, then

    L_R(f)<=6*2^(-123/2)<2^-58,
    |f(X)|<=2^-31 max(1,|X|^(1/5)) for every X.

These conclusions apply in particular to the actual unnormalized reference residual F in the current conditional nonlinear theorem, where R=2^31 and s=3*2^-31, if that theorem's sufficient residual hypothesis is met. Neither conclusion implies this sufficient hypothesis conversely. No sampled or normalized residual can replace F here.

#### Proof

Put H=J^s f. The negative component of E_R gives L_R(H)<=2^(-53/2)N_(s,R)(f). The Bessel bound of section P17.4, retained in part P19, gives L_R(J^-s H)<=6L_R(H). It is an inequality on the same canonical completion, so it applies to f=J^-s H. Consequently

    L_R(f)<=6*2^(-53/2)N_(s,R)(f)<=6*2^(-123/2).

The last number is less than 2^-58 because 6<2^(7/2), equivalently 36<128.

The point embedding in part P19, equation(7), states

    |f(X)|<=16max(1,|X|)^(1/5)N_(s,R)(f).

Since max(1,|X|)^(1/5)=max(1,|X|^(1/5)) and 16*2^-35=2^-31, the second conclusion follows for every point of the continuous representative. The strict bound on s in the current theorem lies in the stated interval. This proves the assertion.

#### Dependencies and scope

Section P19.1, equations(6)-(7) and section 5, supplies the point embedding and its compatible low inclusion. Section P17.4 supplies the Bessel bound. Section P21.1 verifies transfer of the same theorem toR=2^31. The current matrix weakening in part P24 changes neither embedding.

The verification script checks the exact inequalities and parameters, and binds these dependencies. No numerical profile is asserted to meet either target. Passing them is weaker than bounding the whole fractional residual norm.

## P31. The uniform unweighted residual bound for every radial degree up to 779

### P31.1. Radial degree needed to escape the present unweighted residual obstruction

Status: CONFIRMED by the proof below, independent exact compression tests and 384/512-bit arithmetic. A second independent review of the argument found it correct, and a separate interval computation of its constants agrees. This concerns the same six stationary branches as part P27. Adding a seventh branch changes the fixed-sector problem and is outside this statement.

#### 1. Exact family and conclusion

Set c=4076476460239181/2251799813685248, gamma=1/c, delta=1-gamma and a_star=7delta/2-2. For an integer K>=59 consider every real potential

    chi=sum_(0<=j<=5,0<=m<=59,m<=k<=K) a_(j,m,k)
          r^(2k)(1+r^2)^((3+gamma-jdelta)/2-k)cos(2m theta).

Put rho=-partial_y Delta chi, U=(-chi_xyy,chi_xxy), F=(cX+U).D rho-rho. Impose the six stationary leading potential branches and the two vanishing first descendants exactly as in part P27. The center normalization may be imposed but is not needed here. The potential coefficients have no size restriction. The canonical realization, parity and exact original leading profile are those in that part.

Let e_m, positive odd m<=139, be the fixed sine coefficients of F at radial degree 1-7delta. Define

    A_K={ell delta/2+k-2:1<=ell<=12,0<=k<=2K+4,
                                   ell delta/2+k-2>=a_star},
    S_K=sum_(a in A_K)(2a+1),
    C_K=sqrt(4 S_K^2/pi^2+1/4),
    D_K=(2a_star+1)^(-1/2)
                 product_(a in A_K,a>a_star)(a-a_star)/(a+a_star+1),
    B_K=(1-34*2^-18)*512sqrt(20/21)*D_K
              *sqrt((pi/2)sum_m e_m^2/[m^2+(1+2C_K)^2]).

Then

    ||F||_(dot H^-1)>=D_K
              *sqrt((pi/2)sum_m e_m^2/[m^2+(1+2C_K)^2]),
    N_U(F)>=B_K,

where N_U is precisely the Route U norm E2(J^(2^-18).) of parts P8 and P12. In particular, any integer K with B_K>eta_U=1/1572864 excludes the current sufficient Route U residual threshold for this whole family. If a subsequent K has B_K<eta_U, the displayed sufficient obstruction has ceased to decide the issue there. It does not establish feasibility or existence at that K.

The numbers B_K strictly decrease with K. Thus one pair of certified adjacent comparisons determines the last integer excluded by this formula. Independent 384-bit direct products and 512-bit gamma-ratio calculations give B_349/eta_U>1.0019782 and B_350/eta_U<0.9917770. Hence every 59<=K<=349 is excluded by this formula. The formula does not decideK=350. At the existing supportK=75 its ratio is greater than 233.
