The K=349 family contains 115380 coefficient slots before affine constraints; the conclusion allows all their real values.

#### 2. A dilation bound from compression of an integral operator

We first prove a statement for any finite strictly increasing real exponents a_0,...,a_(n-1)>-1/2. Let P be their power span in L2(0,1;du), and let B=u partial_u act on P. Put S=sum_i(2a_i+1). Then

    ||B||_(P->P)<=sqrt(4S^2/pi^2+1/4).                    (1)

Apply increasing-order Gram-Schmidt to the powers u^a_i. Choose its orthonormal basis p_i so that p_i(1)>0. The exact endpoint formula from part P27 gives p_i(1)^2=2a_i+1. Dilation preserves each preceding power span. Integration by parts, whose u=0 boundary term vanishes since all exponents exceed -1/2, gives

    <Bp_i,p_j>+<p_i,Bp_j>=p_i(1)p_j(1)-delta_ij.

The triangular matrix of B therefore has diagonal a_i and upper entries sqrt((2a_i+1)(2a_j+1)) for i<j, with all lower entries zero.

Partition the interval(0,S) into consecutive intervals I_i of lengths l_i=2a_i+1. Let P_step denote the orthogonal projection onto functions constant on these intervals, with orthonormal basis1_(I_i)/sqrt(l_i). Define

    (Tf)(x)=int_x^S f(y)dy.

Its compressed matrix P_step T P_step has diagonal l_i/2 and upper entries sqrt(l_i l_j). Hence the matrix of B is exactly that of P_step T P_step-I/2. For every function f in this step space,

    ||Bf||2^2=||P_step Tf||2^2-Re<Tf,f>+(1/4)||f||2^2.

Fubini gives Re<Tf,f>=(1/2)|int_0^S f|^2>=0, also for complex f. Moreover

    ||Tf||2<=(2S/pi)||f||2.                              (2)

For completeness, g=Tf satisfies g(S)=0 and g'=-f. Reflect g evenly across 0 to (-S,S). The reflected function belongs to H1_0(-S,S), so its elementary first Dirichlet sine-mode inequality is ||g||2<=(2S/pi)||g'||2. The two reflected squared norms each acquire a factor 2, which cancels. This proves (2). Orthogonal projection decreases norm. Substituting (2) into the preceding identity proves (1).

This proof is independent of a numerical singular value calculation. Compared with the Frobenius bound of part P27, its leading coefficient in S is 2/pi instead of 1/sqrt(2). We use (1) directly; no assertion about optimality on the finite power span is needed.

#### 3. Compactified residual and the fixed coefficient

Set u=(1+r^2)^-1 and t=1-u. For each generator separately, the Cartesian derivative recurrence and its origin regularity give degree bounds K+1 after three derivatives and K+2 after four derivatives, after removing the same radial factor as in part P27. The nonlinear product therefore has degree at most 2K+3. The linear terms have degree at most K+2. For every sine mode one can write

    F_m(r)=sqrt(t)u^(-1/2)H_m(u),
    H_m=sum_(ell=1)^12 u^(ell delta/2)P_(ell,m)(t),
    deg P_(ell,m)<=2K+3.

Put w_m=t u^-2 H_m. Its integer degree bound is 2K+4, so it is a sum of powers in A_K once the eight required sectors are removed. Exactly the same eight exponents precede a_star for every K>=59. Their triangular relation with the exterior expansion makes their coefficients zero. The coefficient of u^a_star is exactly e_m. Distinct exponent classes cannot resonate: their ell difference has magnitude at most 11, smaller than the denominator needed for an integer relation with the exact delta.

The coefficient e_m only involves the six prescribed leading stationary branches. There is no branch j=6 supplying a linear term at degree 1-7delta. Increasing the radial degree introduces descendants but no new leading branch, so it cannot change e_m.

The exact power-space distance of part P27 now gives

    ||w_m||_(L2(du))>=|e_m|D_K.                          (3)

The canonical fields are smooth at the origin and decay sufficiently at infinity after the eight cancellations. In particular g_m(s)=r^2F_m(r), s=log r, belongs to H1(R;ds). Its exact norm conversion is

    ||g_m||2^2=(1/2)||w_m||2^2,
    ||partial_s g_m||2<=(1+2||B||)||g_m||2.              (4)

To verify the second identity, g_m=sqrt(u(1-u))w_m and partial_s=-2u(1-u)partial_u. Differentiate the prefactor and use |2u-1|<=1 and 1-u<=1. The same measure du/[2u(1-u)] as in part P27 removes the prefactor. Applying (1) to the space A_K proves (4) with C_K.

#### 4. The actual negative norm and the threshold

For m>=1, the planar Poisson equation reduces in the log-radius coordinate to (-partial_s^2+m^2)phi_m=g_m. Its Dirichlet energy is pi times the corresponding cylinder energy. Positive self-adjoint spectral calculus and Cauchy-Schwarz give

    <g_m,(-partial_s^2+m^2)^-1g_m>
       >=||g_m||2^4/(||partial_s g_m||2^2+m^2||g_m||2^2).

Substitute(3)-(4), multiply bypi, and sum the orthogonal sine energies. Every omitted angular mode has nonnegative energy. This proves the first claimed bound. The established comparison

    N_U(F)>=(1-34*2^-18)E2(F),
    E2(F)>=512sqrt(20/21)||F||_(dot H^-1)

proves the bound B_K in the exact Route U norm. No weighted-to-unweighted replacement is made.

Finally A_K is strictly nested as K increases. Every new factor in D_K lies strictly between 0 and 1 because a_star>-1/2, while every summand2a+1 in S_K is positive. Thus D_K decreases strictly and C_K increases strictly. The vector e is fixed and nonzero. It follows that B_K strictly decreases. This proves the adjacent-comparison procedure.

#### Dependencies and scope

Section P27.1 supplies the exact stationary affine constraints, original e_m, monomial-distance identity, endpoint formula and cylinder realization. Its two independent programs recover the original source and verify those constants. Parts P8 and P12 provide the Route U reverse norm comparison. The present proof supplies the new dilation bound, general degree count and monotonicity.

This is a quantitative obstruction to one current sufficient unweighted threshold over six fixed stationary branches and bounded radial degree. It is neither a weighted obstruction nor nonexistence of full-plane profiles. It allows arbitrarily large coefficients within the specified finite support. A seventh stationary branch is not in the family and requires a separate audit.

### P31.2. Keeping the radial factor in the cylinder derivative

Status: analytical proof and two independent arithmetic implementations are complete. Exact rational basis, trace and cylinder identities have also been checked. A second independent review of the argument found it correct, and a separate interval computation of its constants agrees. The result concerns the unweighted Route U norm and six fixed stationary branches.

#### 1. Exact statement

For every n-dimensional span E of n distinct exponentials exp(-b_j tau), b_j>0, in L2(0,infinity;d tau),

    ||tau partial_tau f||2^2<=n(n^2+2)||f||2^2/6,
                                            f in E.       (1)

No separation or upper bound on the b_j is needed. This is an explicit sufficient constant; no optimal operator-norm claim is made.

Let a_1,...,a_n>-1/2 be distinct, w(u) in their power span on (0,1), u=(1+r^2)^-1, and s=log r. Put

    g(s)=sqrt(u(1-u))w(u).

Then

    ||partial_s g||2^2<=Q_n||g||2^2,
    Q_n=[2n(n^2+2)+1]/3.                                (2)

Both norms in (2) use ds. This improves the preceding sufficient bound by retaining 1-u in the cylinder derivative.

Apply this to the exact potential family

    chi=sum_(0<=j<=5,0<=m<=59,m<=k<=K) a_(j,m,k)
         r^(2k)(1+r^2)^((3+gamma-jdelta)/2-k)cos(2m theta),

for K>=59, c=4076476460239181/2251799813685248, gamma=1/c, delta=1-gamma. Set rho=-partial_y Delta chi, U=(-chi_xyy,chi_xxy), F=(cX+U).D rho-rho. Impose the six fixed stationary leading potential branches determined by original state 131, and the vanishing first descendants of branches j=0,1, exactly as in parts P27 and P31.1. All coefficients are real and unrestricted in magnitude; the center normalization is optional here. Put a_star=7delta/2-2,

    A_K={ell delta/2+k-2:1<=ell<=12,0<=k<=2K+4,
                                   ell delta/2+k-2>=a_star},
    n_K=12(2K+5)-8,
    D_K=(2a_star+1)^(-1/2)
                product_(a in A_K,a>a_star)(a-a_star)/(a+a_star+1).

Let e_m be the fixed coefficient of sin(m theta) in the residual sector r^(1-7delta), with positive odd m<=139. Then the actual homogeneous negative norm satisfies

    ||F||_(dot H^-1)>=D_K sqrt((pi/2)
                                   sum_m e_m^2/(m^2+Q_(n_K))).        (3)

The exact Route U norm N_U=E2(J^(2^-18).) consequently satisfies

    N_U(F)>=Bnew_K,
    Bnew_K=(1-34*2^-18)*512sqrt(20/21)
                  D_K sqrt((pi/2)sum_m e_m^2/(m^2+Q_(n_K))).          (4)

Bnew_K strictly decreases with K. A certified comparison Bnew_K>eta_U=1/1572864 excludes the current sufficient Route U residual threshold for the entire stated family. A value below eta_U makes this formula inconclusive there. It is not an existence or feasibility conclusion. Adding branch j=6 changes the problem and is not covered.

#### 2. An orthonormal basis for the exponential span

Use the Laplace transform F(z)=int_0^infinity exp(-z tau)f(tau)d tau, with boundary norm

    ||f||2^2=(1/(2pi))int_R |F(i omega)|^2 d omega.

For each j=0,...,n-1 define

    Phi_j(z)=sqrt(2b_j)/(z+b_j)
                    product_(i<j)(z-b_i)/(z+b_i).        (5)

The simple poles show that Phi_j is the Laplace transform of a function phi_j in the span of exp(-b_i tau), i<=j. Its coefficient at the newly introduced pole-b_j is nonzero, since the b_i are distinct. Each boundary factor (z-b_i)/(z+b_i) has modulus 1 at z=i omega, so

    |Phi_j(i omega)|^2=2b_j/(omega^2+b_j^2),
    ||phi_j||2=1.

For i<j, Phi_j(z)Phi_i(-z) has only left-half-plane poles and decays quadratically at infinity: all right-half-plane poles cancel with the factors in Phi_j. Closing the imaginary-axis contour in the right half-plane gives zero integral. Equivalently one may integrate its partial fractions directly. Thus <phi_j,phi_i>=0. The n triangularly independent vectors form an orthonormal basis of E. This argument establishes the basis used below, rather than assuming a named rational-function theorem.

#### 3. The norm of tau partial_tau on each basis vector

Integration by parts and differentiation of the Laplace integral give

    Laplace(tau f')=-F-zF'.                              (6)

The constant boundary term f(0) in Laplace(f') disappears under z differentiation. The finite exponential functions justify every operation absolutely in the right half-plane and by L2 limits on its boundary.

At z=i omega set

    A_i(omega)=2b_i omega/(omega^2+b_i^2),
    P_b(omega)=b/[pi(omega^2+b^2)].

P_b is a probability density. Logarithmic differentiation of (5) shows that the multiplier in (6) is

    -b_j/(b_j+i omega)+i sum_(i<j) A_i(omega).

Its squared modulus is

    b_j^2/(b_j^2+omega^2)
       +A_j sum_(i<j)A_i+(sum_(i<j)A_i)^2.              (7)

All quantities in (7) are real. The imaginary part of-b_j/(b_j+i omega) is A_j/2, which accounts for the middle term.

Direct integration against P_(b_j) gives

    E[b_j^2/(b_j^2+omega^2)]=1/2,
    E[A_i^2]=2b_i b_j/(b_i+b_j)^2<=1/2.                 (8)

For example, E[1/(omega^2+a^2)]=1/[a(a+b_j)]. Differentiating this identity in a and subtracting gives E[omega^2/(omega^2+a^2)^2]=b_j/[2a(a+b_j)^2], proving the second formula. All poles lie off the real axis and all differentiated integrals are absolutely convergent. Cauchy-Schwarz now gives |E[A_i A_k]|<=1/2. Integrating(7), with exactly j preceding terms, yields

    ||tau phi_j'||2^2<=(j^2+j+1)/2.                     (9)

For f=sum c_j phi_j, Cauchy-Schwarz in the finite vector index gives

    ||tau f'||2^2<=(sum_j |c_j|^2)
                              sum_j ||tau phi_j'||2^2.

The last sum is at most n(n^2+2)/6. Orthogonality gives sum|c_j|^2=||f||2^2. This proves (1). It is a Hilbert-Schmidt estimate, which suffices here even though it need not give the smallest operator norm.

There is an independent exact formula for the sum before this bound:

    sum_j ||tau phi_j'||2^2
      =n/2+4sum_(i<j) b_i b_j/(b_i+b_j)^2
             +8sum_(i<j<k)
                 b_i b_j b_k/[(b_i+b_j)(b_i+b_k)(b_j+b_k)].          (10)

Indeed E_(b_j)[A_i A_k]=4b_i b_k b_j/[(b_i+b_k)(b_i+b_j)(b_k+b_j)]. Substitute this into (7) and group pairs and triples. Each normalized pair and triple summand in (10) is at most 1 by arithmetic-geometric mean. This independently recovers the same upper bound. The formula is used only for small exact audit cases; evaluating its large triple sum is unnecessary.

#### 4. Exact transformation to the radial cylinder

Set tau=-log u, t=1-u=1-exp(-tau), and

    f(tau)=exp(-tau/2)w(exp(-tau)).

Its exponents are b_j=a_j+1/2>0. This transformation is unitary from L2(0,1;du) to L2(0,infinity;d tau). Moreover

    g(s)=sqrt(t)f(tau), ds=d tau/(2t),
    ||g||2^2=(1/2)||f||2^2,
    ||partial_s g||2^2
       =(1/2)||exp(-tau)f+2(1-exp(-tau))f'||2^2.         (11)

These identities follow by differentiating r^2=exp(tau)-1. They include the derivative of the prefactor, which is essential.

Write u=exp(-tau). Expand the last square and integrate its mixed term by parts. The boundary term u(1-u)|f|^2 vanishes at both 0 and infinity, since f is a finite sum of decaying exponentials. The exact result is

    ||u f+2(1-u)f'||2^2
       =4||(1-u)f'||2^2+int(2u-3u^2)|f|^2 d tau.       (12)

Since 0<=1-exp(-tau)<=tau and 2u-3u^2<=1/3 for 0<=u<=1, equations(1),(11),(12) prove(2). This is the step that retains the radial cancellation lost when u partial_u is bounded first.

#### 5. Full-plane consequence

Part P31.1 gives the exact residual representation with compactified degree 2K+4. Its eight cancellations remove all exponents below a_star, and its u^a_star coefficient is the fixed e_m. Its exact monomial-distance identity gives ||w_m||2>=|e_m|D_K. The residual lies in the actual homogeneous negative space; its mode cylinder functions belong to H1 by the endpoint exponents and origin regularity.

For each m>=1 the Poisson inverse is (-partial_s^2+m^2)^-1 and

    <g_m,(-partial_s^2+m^2)^-1g_m>
      >=||g_m||2^4/(||partial_sg_m||2^2+m^2||g_m||2^2).

Apply(2), the measure factor 1/2 in (11), and the monomial-distance bound. Multiplication bypi and summation over orthogonal sine modes prove(3). The previously verified Route U comparison gives (4). The vector e is fixed and nonzero, D_K decreases strictly and n_K increases strictly, proving the claimed monotonicity.

#### Dependencies and scope

The standalone family, exact source data, radial degree count, eight cancellations, fixed sine vector and Route U comparison are specified in section P27.1 and section P31.1. The present proof independently supplies the exponential derivative estimate, its exact trace formula, and the complete cylinder transformation. Its numerical constants were checked from the same source-bound exact sine vector using separate gamma-product and direct-product implementations at 384 and 512 bits. Every one of 21 rows agrees. Four unrelated rational exponential sets independently verify all basis orthogonality, exact trace and complete cylinder identities.

The certified comparisons are Bnew_75/eta_U>1308, Bnew_779/eta_U>1.0035179 and Bnew_780/eta_U<0.9995471. Consequently every 59<=K<=779 fails the present Route U sufficient residual threshold. The K779 family has 270180 coefficient slots before constraints. The K780 result only makes this formula inconclusive. Numerical evidence is in certificate files constant_bound.py, constant_bound.json and constant_bound.log and certificate files audit_derivative.py, audit_derivative.json and audit_derivative.log.

No weighted norm lower bound, successful improved reference, or exact IPM profile is asserted. All positive conclusions are stated for the exact spaces and finite support above. The result gives a necessary change to the sufficient Route U program while keeping the six stationary branches fixed.

## P32. The seventh stationary order and the next fixed residual sector

### P32.1. The seventh stationary tail and the next fixed residual sector

Status: the formal argument and two independent exact original-source reconstructions are complete. Every seventh-order coefficient agrees with the record of the numerical work. A second independent review of the argument found it correct. This is a finite formal expansion, not a convergence or existence theorem.

#### 1. Setting and statement

Fix the exact original state 131 exponent

    c = 4076476460239181/2251799813685248,
    gamma = 1/c, delta = 1-gamma,
    p_n = 1-n delta.

The equation and velocity convention are

    F(rho) = (c X + U[rho]).grad rho-rho,
    U = (-psi_y,psi_x), -Delta psi = rho_x.

Let C_1(theta) be the leading even cosine potential of original state 131, independently recovered from its 860 canonical rational coefficients. Its largest angular frequency is 18. Define Theta_1 and Psi_1 by differentiating r^(p_1+3) C_1:

    rho_1 = -partial_y Delta(r^(p_1+3) C_1),
    psi_1 = partial_x partial_y(r^(p_1+3) C_1).

There is a unique sequence of finite odd sine density polynomials Theta_n, 1<=n<=8, and even sine stream polynomials Psi_n, solving the homogeneous angular Poisson equations and cancelling the formal stationary coefficients through order 8. Their density and stream degrees are at most 20n-1 and 20n respectively. The definitions and uniqueness are in sections 2-3.

For a potential with branches j=0,...,6, whose first seven leading homogeneous potentials equal these stationary orders, the residual sector indexed(h,q)=(7,0) is the fixed sine polynomial

    E_7 = sum_(i+j=8,1<=i,j<=7)
              [(p_i+1) Psi_i Theta_j' - p_j Psi_i' Theta_j]
        = 7(c-1) Theta_8.                              (1)

It has radial power p_8=1-8delta. No coefficient in the radial descendants of those seven branches can alter E_7. Adding branch j=7 with the eighth stationary leading density cancels it.

This does not assert that E_7 is the leading nonzero residual of an arbitrary seven-branch candidate. If only sectors(0..6,0),(0,1),(1,1) are set to zero, the unconstrained sector(2,1) has power gamma-2delta-2, which is strictly larger than p_8. An approximate penalty on its coefficients does not remove it from the asymptotic expansion.

#### 2. Angular inverse and nonresonance

For a homogeneous density r^p Theta(theta), write its stream as r^(p+1) Psi(theta). The angular Poisson equation is

    [-partial_theta^2-(p+1)^2] Psi
          = p cos(theta) Theta - sin(theta) Theta'.   (2)

If Theta=sum_(k odd positive) a_k sin(k theta), the right side contributes

    (p-k)a_k/2 to sin((k+1)theta),
    (p+k)a_k/2 to sin((k-1)theta),

with sin(0 theta)=0 and negative frequencies reduced by sin(-m theta)=-sin(m theta). Divide each even sine coefficient by m^2-(p+1)^2 to obtain Psi.

For the exact c above and 1<=n<=8, p_n+1=2-n delta is not an integer. Indeed delta=A/B with A=1824676646553933, B=4076476460239181 and gcd(A,B)=1. An integer value would imply B divides n, impossible since 0<n<=8<B. Thus no Fourier denominator in (2) vanishes. This uniquely determines Psi within the finite even sine class. The same noninteger condition excludes additional homogeneous harmonic terms at this radial power.

#### 3. The formal recurrence

In polar coordinates the advection of r^(p_j)Theta_j by the stream r^(p_i+1)Psi_i is

    r^(p_i+p_j-1)
        [(p_i+1)Psi_i Theta_j' - p_j Psi_i' Theta_j].  (3)

The exponents satisfy p_i+p_j-1=p_(i+j). The linear coefficient on the n-th density is

    c p_n-1=-(n-1)(c-1).

Thus the leading n=1 equation vanishes identically, and for n>=2 define

    S_n=sum_(i+j=n) [(p_i+1)Psi_i Theta_j'
                                      -p_j Psi_i' Theta_j],
    Theta_n=S_n/[(n-1)(c-1)].                          (4)

The denominator is nonzero because c>1. Equations(2) and (4) give existence and uniqueness recursively. For each finite order they are exact rational operations on finite trigonometric polynomials. The order n coefficient of F is zero by substitution; this is a formal algebraic assertion, with no interchange of an infinite sum.

Inductively Theta_n has odd frequencies at most 20n-1 and Psi_n even frequencies at most 20n. In (3) the product of degrees20i and 20j-1 has degree at most 20n-1. Equation(2) increases the degree by at most 1. This proves the bounds.

An even cosine potential C_n of degree at most 20n-2 can also be recovered uniquely. Apply -partial_y Delta to r^(p_n+3) cos(m theta). Its highest sine frequency is m+1 and has nonzero coefficient for every nonnegative even m: p_n is noninteger, so none of the factors p_n+3-m, p_n+3+m, p_n+1-m vanishes. At m=0 the two signed frequency contributions coincide and must both be retained. Solve from the highest odd density frequency down to 1. This triangular procedure gives C_n and reproduces Theta_n exactly. Differentiating it by partial_x partial_y gives the same Psi_n by (2) and nonresonance.

#### 4. Invariance and the descendant qualification

A smooth finite radial branch admits a binomial expansion at infinity, with its descendants indexed by an integer q>=0 and powers

    alpha(h,q)=gamma-h delta-2q.

The linear term can contribute to (7,0) only from branch j=7, which is absent. Quadratic interactions contribute to this sector only when i+j=6 in zero-based branch indices and both descendant indices are zero. These are precisely the leading interactions in (1), all fixed by the seven leading moments.

There is no collision with another sector in the finite seven-branch residual. Equality of two radial powers would give (h-h')delta=2(q'-q). Coprimality implies B divides h-h'. Here 0<=h,h'<=13 and B>13, so h=h' and then q=q'. In particular radial descendants cannot absorb the fixed coefficient E_7.

The exponent difference between (2,1) and (7,0) is 5delta-2, which is positive for this exact delta. Therefore (2,1) precedes E_7 unless it is zero exactly. If (2,1) is also removed, then E_7 precedes(3,1) because 2-4delta>0, and it precedes the first q=2 sector because 4-7delta>0. These are strict rational comparisons. Subsequent invariant statements are always conditional on the specified earlier sectors vanishing exactly.

#### 5. Independent verification and numerical result

The verification recovers state 131 directly from the read-only original JSON and NPZ, checks its canonical digest, and extracts its leading cosine polynomial. A real sine recurrence and an independent complex Fourier differentiation/convolution agree on every density, stream and potential order through 8. The existing six-order record and the exact seventh-order coefficients of the numerical work are comparison inputs, not premises of the recurrence. Every compared input and implementation is hashed.

The new seven-branch invariant has full-circle norm in (9679.9655,9679.9656), approximately 9679.96558019927435194. Its first-quadrant norm is 4839.98279009963717597. The old six-branch residual at the same exponent has full-circle norm 4331.15745649082938888 and first-quadrant norm 2165.57872824541469444. The latter is not the invariant after adding the seventh stationary branch: it omits the interactions (1,7) and (7,1) in one-based stationary-order notation.

The seventh potential has maximum coefficient magnitude 138.26904068945842515. Its density has 70 odd sine coefficients through frequency 139; the first three are -21.90824839824379453,78.22820506075036798,-118.97814871736291410. These decimals summarize the exact rational files.

The full-circle angular norm is sqrt(pi sum_m E_m^2). The first-quadrant norm is one half of that value for these integer sine polynomials. Both normalizations must be reported explicitly. Bounds on norms use rational coefficient squares and Arb enclosures of pi and square root. The result says nothing about convergence of the stationary series, global smoothness of a resulting formal profile, a small finite-radius residual, or nonlinear closure.

## P33. A recursive dilation constant: the uniform unweighted residual bound for every radial degree up to 3675

### P33.1. A recursive dilation estimate for exponential sums

Status: analytical proof, independent exact algebraic tests and two independent arithmetic evaluations are complete. Lead This improves the unweighted family obstruction; no weighted existence claim is made.

#### 1. Statement and spaces

Let b_1,...,b_J be distinct positive real numbers, with positive integer multiplicities d_1,...,d_J and total n=sum_j d_j. Let E_n be the span of tau^k exp(-b_j tau), 0<=k<d_j, in L2(0,infinity;d tau). Coefficients may be complex. The ordinary exponential span is the special case d_j=1. Define

    c_n = n - 1/2 + (1/8) log(2n-1),
    q_1 = 1/2, q_n = sqrt((q_(n-1)+1)^2+1/4).

Then, for every f in E_n,

    ||(tau partial_tau+1/2)f||2 <= q_n ||f||2 <= c_n ||f||2,
    ||tau f'||2^2 <= (c_n^2+1/4)||f||2^2.             (1)

No separation, lower bound, or upper bound on the positive rates is needed. The constants are sufficient bounds, not claimed sharp. A simpler rational squared bound is

    ||tau f'||2^2 <= (5n^2+1)||f||2^2/4.              (2)

For distinct a_j>-1/2 with the same multiplicities and total n, w(u) in the span of u^a_j(log u)^k, 0<=k<d_j, on (0,1), and

    u=(1+r^2)^-1, s=log r, g(s)=sqrt(u(1-u))w(u),

one consequently has

    ||partial_s g||2^2 <= Q_n ||g||2^2,
    Q_n=4c_n^2+4/3,                                  (3)

where both norms in (3) use ds.

#### 2. One-step orthogonal decomposition

Use the Laplace transform F(z)=int_0^infinity exp(-z tau)f(tau)d tau and its boundary norm

    ||F||^2=(1/(2pi))int_R |F(i omega)|^2 d omega=||f||2^2.

All transforms here are proper rational functions with poles at -b_j of orders at most d_j, because the transform of tau^k exp(-b_j tau) is k!/(z+b_j)^(k+1). Fix one rate b with positive multiplicity, and set

    k_b(z)=sqrt(2b)/(z+b), B_b(z)=(z-b)/(z+b).

The reproducing identity is <F,k_b>=sqrt(2b)F(b), with the inner product linear in its first argument. It follows directly by pairing f(tau) with sqrt(2b)exp(-b tau). Write d=<F,k_b> and

    F=d k_b+B_b G, G=(F-d k_b)/B_b.                   (4)

The numerator vanishes at z=b. Division by B_b lowers the allowed pole order at z=-b by one and leaves the other allowed orders unchanged. Thus G belongs to the Laplace image of the remaining dimension n-1 exponential-polynomial space. If the original pole order at -b was one, that pole disappears. Since |B_b(i omega)|=1,

    ||F||^2=|d|^2+||G||^2.                           (5)

Indeed B_b G vanishes at b and is orthogonal to k_b. This proves the decomposition and norm identity without invoking an abstract model-space theorem.

#### 3. The recursive estimate

The time operator A=tau partial_tau+1/2 becomes

    Ahat F=-F/2-z F'.

Integration by parts justifies this identity on finite exponential sums. Direct differentiation gives

    Ahat k_b=(1/2)B_b k_b,
    Ahat(B_b G)=B_b Ahat G-z B_b' G.                  (6)

The first term has norm 1/2. For the multiplier in the second formula,

    |(i omega) B_b'(i omega)|
          =2b|omega|/(b^2+omega^2)<=1.               (7)

Its squared inequality is exactly (omega^2-b^2)^2>=0. Assuming the bound q_(n-1) on the remaining span, equations(4)-(7), the triangle inequality, and Cauchy-Schwarz in the two components imply

    ||Ahat F|| <= |d|/2+(q_(n-1)+1)||G||
               <= sqrt(1/4+(q_(n-1)+1)^2)||F||.

For n=1, G=0 and equality in the first formula of (6) gives q_1=1/2. This proves the recursion for every n and every set of rates.

The lower bound q_n>=n-1/2 follows from q_n>=q_(n-1)+1. For n>=2,

    q_n-q_(n-1)-1
       = (1/4)/(sqrt((q_(n-1)+1)^2+1/4)+q_(n-1)+1)
       <=1/[8(n-1/2)].

Since the positive function(t-1/2)^-1 decreases,

    sum_(k=2)^n 1/(k-1/2)
         <=int_1^n dt/(t-1/2)=log(2n-1).

This proves q_n<=c_n. Alternatively induction proves q_n<=sqrt(5)n/2: for a=sqrt(5)/2 the difference

    a^2 n^2 - (a(n-1)+1)^2 - 1/4
       =2an(a-1)-(a-1)^2-1/4

is increasing in n and equals zero at n=1. The initial q_1 is smaller than a. This gives (2).

The time operator A has purely imaginary quadratic form: integration by parts gives Re<A f,f>=0, with boundary tau|f|^2 vanishing at 0 and infinity. Therefore

    ||tau f'||2^2=||A f-f/2||2^2
                =||A f||2^2+||f||2^2/4.

This proves (1) completely, including the conversion from the centered dilation to the derivative used below.

#### 4. Cylinder transformation

Set tau=-log u, t=1-u and f(tau)=exp(-tau/2)w(exp(-tau)). Its rates are b_j=a_j+1/2>0. As in part P31.2, direct differentiation and integration by parts give

    ||g||2^2=||f||2^2/2,
    ||partial_s g||2^2=||u f+2(1-u)f'||2^2/2,
    ||u f+2(1-u)f'||2^2
       =4||(1-u)f'||2^2+int(2u-3u^2)|f|^2 d tau.

All boundary terms vanish for the finite exponential sum. Since 1-exp(-tau)<=tau and 2u-3u^2<=1/3, equation(1) implies (3).

#### 5. Consequence for the fixed six-branch IPM family

Use exactly the family, source state and constraints in part P31.2: c=4076476460239181/2251799813685248, gamma=1/c, delta=1-gamma, branches 0<=j<=5, angular indices 0<=m<=59, radial indices m<=k<=K, K>=59, six fixed stationary leading moments, and zero first descendants of branches 0,1. Set

    a_star=7delta/2-2,
    A_K={ell delta/2+k-2:1<=ell<=12,0<=k<=2K+4,
                                    ell delta/2+k-2>=a_star},
    n_K=12(2K+5)-8,
    D_K=(2a_star+1)^(-1/2)
           product_(a in A_K,a>a_star)(a-a_star)/(a+a_star+1).

Let e_m be the fixed nonzero sine vector at residual power 1-7delta, as recovered and checked in parts P25, P27 and P31.2. The exact compactified residual representation, monomial-distance identity, angular orthogonality and cylinder resolvent inequality proved there give

    ||F||_(dot H^-1)>=D_K sqrt((pi/2)
                       sum_m e_m^2/(m^2+Q_(n_K))),
    N_U(F)>=(1-34*2^-18)512sqrt(20/21)
                  D_K sqrt((pi/2)sum_m e_m^2/(m^2+Q_(n_K))).        (8)

Here N_U=E2(J^(2^-18).) is precisely the Route U norm of the prior theorems, and its sufficient residual threshold is eta_U=1/1572864. The right side of (8) strictly decreases with K: D_K decreases, c_n strictly increases, and e is nonzero. A certified comparison above eta_U excludes that sufficient threshold for the entire stated finite family, independently of coefficient size. A comparison below eta_U only makes this formula inconclusive. Adding the seventh branch is outside the claim.

#### Dependencies and limits

The new independent argument is sections 2-3. Section 4 includes the full cylinder conversion to make its constant unambiguous. Part P27 supplies the actual residual representation and invariant; part P31.2 restates the exact family, low-space membership and resolvent consequence. The repeated-pole form also proves (3) for finitely many logarithmic power coordinates u^a(log u)^k. It does not by itself establish a varying-exponent inverse or accommodate an arbitrary changing leading angular function. No weighted lower bound, convergence of an asymptotic series, or existence conclusion is drawn. Numerical application and independent verification will be recorded alongside this proof.

#### Certified application

The two arithmetic implementations agree on all 23 evaluated radial caps. The gamma-product computation uses 384-bit balls; the second independently multiplies each individual monomial-distance factor at 512 bits. The strict comparisons are

    B_75/eta_U > 22986,
    B_3675/eta_U > 1.0004726,
    B_3676/eta_U < 0.9997658.

Together with monotonicity, this excludes every 59<=K<=3675 from the sufficient Route U residual threshold in the family stated in section 5. The K3675 family has 1312740 coefficient slots before constraints. The formula is inconclusive at K3676. There is no claim that this cap is a true feasibility transition.

Six exact rational Gram-matrix tests include distinct, nearly coincident, widely separated, repeated and mixed repeated rates. They verify the centered skew quadratic form, a strict rational comparison smaller than c_n, the simpler squared bound 5n^2/4, and every cylinder identity. Two separate exact partial-fraction tests verify the orthogonal factorization. The elementary recursive upper bounds are additionally enclosed through n=10000; these finite checks supplement the induction proof and do not replace it. All inputs, code and proofs are hashed. See certificate files constant_bound.py, constant_bound.json and constant_bound.log and certificate files audit_recursive.py, audit_recursive.json and audit_recursive.log,AUDIT.md.

## P34. Scope of the annular obstruction: residuals in the negative-order space have square-summable annular pairings

### P34.1. Scope of the annular affine obstruction

Status: a logical audit of the report and a complete supporting observation. This does not prove existence or nonexistence in any repaired affine class.

#### Statement and notation

Let H be the homogeneous H^-1 completion of smooth compactly supported functions on R^2 with the density parity (even in x and odd in y). Its norm is ||f||_H=||D(-Delta)^-1 f||_2. Fix R0>0 and a real smooth test phi supported in 1<|X|<2. Put R_j=3^j R0 and phi_j(X)=phi(X/R_j).

For every f in H,

    sum_(j>=0) |<f,phi_j>|^2 <= ||D phi||_2^2 ||f||_H^2.       (1)

Consequently an H residual already satisfies every square-summability condition of this form. The annular affine-obstruction theorem cannot exclude a repaired affine class merely by showing that the residual lies in H. It excludes a reference only when its actual residual violates a necessary annular condition, for example by a nonzero leading sector r^q E(theta) with q>=-2.

For the exact S1 finite potentials, the cancellation of the eight forbidden sectors (h,q)=(0,0),...,(5,0),(0,1),(1,1) implies F in N_s, and hence F in H, for 0<s<=1/2. The initial accepted states and early refits m4, m5, m10, m12 and m14 have a verified forbidden sector and are excluded from their unweighted N_s affine correction classes. The later repaired references A2, A3, A4, A5, Mpen, A6dpen and Mpen2 cancel all eight forbidden sectors exactly. The annular argument does not exclude their affine classes at their recorded exponent. Weighted correction spaces are also outside the original theorem's H hypothesis.

#### Proof of (1)

For finitely supported scalar coefficients a_j, the annuli supporting D phi_j are disjoint. Scaling in two dimensions gives ||D phi_j||_2=||D phi||_2. Thus

    ||D sum_j a_j phi_j||_2^2
       = ||D phi||_2^2 sum_j |a_j|^2.

Homogeneous H^-1/H^1 duality implies

    |sum_j a_j <f,phi_j>| <= ||f||_H ||D phi||_2
                                      (sum_j |a_j|^2)^(1/2).

Duality with finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces gives (1) for each finite partial sum. Monotone convergence proves it for the infinite sequence. No stationarity assumption enters this argument.

#### Application and the distinction between statements

Part P13 proves that a stationary correction h in H with bounded gradient forces square-summable annular residual moments. It also proves that a nonzero r^q E term, q>=-2, violates this condition. Its finite-ladder membership theorem gives the exact eight-sector criterion and smooth derivative decay for the repaired references. Part P20 independently verifies the eight cancellations as exact rational identities for all seven later references named above.

Therefore the report may state nonexistence of a correction of any size for the initial states and the specified early refits in the unweighted classes. It may also state that the repaired references fail a current sufficient smallness threshold or another coefficient hypothesis, as individually certified. These are different conclusions: failure of a sufficient criterion does not prove nonexistence of a correction.

The exponent-rigidity part of part P13 remains valid for repaired references: a different exponent creates a nonzero r^gamma sector, so an exact correction in the same unweighted class would have to keep the recorded exponent. This does not exclude a correction at that exponent. Nor does the finite-potential nonexistence theorem exclude a corrected profile that lies outside that finite potential family.

#### Dependencies and audit conclusion

Dependencies are section P13.2 and the exact rational candidate records in 19_nb_candidates/verification. The report snapshot and their hashes are stored alongside this proof.

The wording "for every exact refit audited so far" is refuted as a statement of what the annular theorem proves. Actual nonexistence in the later repaired classes remains OPEN. Replace that phrase by the explicit initial-state and early-refit list, and explicitly restrict the conclusion to unweighted corrections in H with bounded gradient. A count of potential coefficient slots before imposed affine constraints is not a count of free coefficients after those constraints.

## P35. The uniform bound for the seven-branch fitting family is inconclusive

### P35.1. What the finite-dimensional residual bound gives after adding a seventh branch

Status: analytical derivation, independent exact distance tests and two arithmetic implementations are complete. A second independent review of the argument found it correct. No smallness or existence claim is made.

#### 1. Exact family and spaces

Let c=4076476460239181/2251799813685248, gamma=1/c and delta=1-gamma. Fix an integer K>=69. Consider all real potentials

    chi = sum_(0<=j<=6, 0<=m<=69, m<=k<=K)
              a_(j,m,k) r^(2k) (1+r^2)^((3+gamma-j delta)/2-k)
                         cos(2m theta).

Set rho=-partial_y Delta chi, U=(-chi_xyy,chi_xxy), and F=(cX+U).D rho-rho, with the canonical parity realization. Fix the seven leading potential branches to the exact stationary orders 1 through 7 reconstructed in part P32 from the original state 131. Impose zero first descendants of branches 0 and 1. Let epsilon=1 if the first descendant of branch 2 is also required to vanish, and epsilon=0 otherwise. These are exact linear coefficient constraints. The center normalization may be imposed but is not used here.

Use the Route U norm N_U=E2(J^(2^-18).) and its sufficient residual threshold eta_U=1/1572864. Let e_m be the exact sine coefficients of the new seven-branch residual at degree 1-8 delta, computed in part P32. This vector is nonzero and its full-circle angular norm is between 9679.9655 and 9679.9656.

Put M=2K+4, a_star=4 delta-2, and define a set by index pairs:

    A_(K,epsilon) = {ell delta/2+k-2 : 1<=ell<=14, 0<=k<=M}
                    minus {(ell,0):1<=ell<=7}
                    minus {(1,1),(2,1)}
                    minus {(3,1)} if epsilon=1.

The subtractions mean removal of the corresponding indexed exponents. All remaining exponents exceed -1/2, are distinct, and a_star belongs to this set. Its dimension is n=14(2K+5)-9-epsilon. Define

    D_(K,epsilon) = (2a_star+1)^(-1/2)
          product_(a in A_(K,epsilon), a != a_star)
                       |a-a_star|/(a+a_star+1),
    c_n = n-1/2+log(2n-1)/8,
    Q_n = 4c_n^2+4/3.

Then the following finite-family lower bound holds:

    N_U(F) >= B_(K,epsilon)
      = (1-34*2^-18) 512 sqrt(20/21) D_(K,epsilon)
              sqrt((pi/2) sum_m e_m^2/(m^2+Q_n)).       (1)

For each fixed epsilon, B_(K,epsilon) strictly decreases as K increases. This theorem supplies a sufficient obstruction if B exceeds eta_U; a value below eta_U is only inconclusive.

#### 2. Exact residual powers and the preceding descendant

The Cartesian derivative recurrence of part P27 applies separately to each generator. Three derivatives leave, after the common radial factor is extracted, a polynomial of degree at most K+1, and four leave degree at most K+2. The product in the residual therefore has degree at most 2K+3. With u=(1+r^2)^-1, t=1-u, each sine coefficient satisfies

    F_m = sqrt(t) u^(-1/2) H_m(u),
    H_m = sum_(ell=1)^14 u^(ell delta/2) P_(ell,m)(t),
    deg P_(ell,m) <= 2K+3.

Consequently w_m=t u^-2 H_m has integer degree at most M in each exponent branch. Seven stationary leading orders remove the exponents (ell,0), 1<=ell<=7. The imposed first descendants remove (1,1) and (2,1), and optionally (3,1). The correspondence between exterior and compactified coefficients is triangular in each fixed ell branch. Removing the preceding coefficient makes the next zero condition equivalent in either coordinate.

There are exactly nine removed exponents before the optional condition. The possible preceding exponent (3,1) is

    a_low=3 delta/2-1 > -1/2,
    a_star-a_low=5 delta/2-1 > 0.

It corresponds to the actual residual sector (h,q)=(2,1), of radial degree gamma-2 delta-2=1-3 delta-2, which is larger than 1-8 delta. The next invariant is therefore not necessarily the first nonzero residual sector. A soft penalty does not remove this exponent.

The exact rational delta has reduced denominator 4076476460239181. Thus two indexed exponents with ell difference at most 13 cannot coincide unless both indices coincide. For the same reason a descendant of another exponent branch cannot contribute to the coefficient of u^a_star. No potential branch j=7 is present, so this coefficient is the fixed quadratic interaction e_m among the seven leading stationary orders. Part P32 proves and independently recomputes that vector including the two new endpoint interactions.

#### 3. Distance from an arbitrary exponent to the remaining power span

The monomial distance formula of part P27 applies to any distinguished exponent a_star>-1/2, not only the smallest exponent. The Gram matrix entries are 1/(a_i+a_j+1). Its Cauchy determinant and the Schur complement give

    dist(u^a_star, span{u^a:a in A, a != a_star})^2
       = (2a_star+1)^(-1)
           product_(a != a_star) (a-a_star)^2/(a+a_star+1)^2.

Every denominator is positive since both exponents exceed -1/2. Hence the absolute product in section 1 is the correct distance even when a_low<a_star. The fixed coefficient in w_m gives ||w_m||_L2(du)>=|e_m|D_(K,epsilon).

The general recursive dilation theorem of part P33 applies to this n-dimensional span, regardless of exponent order or separation. For g_m=r^2 F_m on s=log r, it gives ||g_m'||_2^2<=Q_n||g_m||_2^2 and ||g_m||_2^2=||w_m||_2^2/2. Positive inverse duality for -partial_s^2+m^2 and angular orthogonality give

    ||F||_(Hdot^-1)^2 >= (pi/2) D_(K,epsilon)^2
                                      sum_m e_m^2/(m^2+Q_n).

All actual residuals in this family belong to the low space because their first possible residual degree is 1-3 delta-2<-2, or later. Smoothness and differentiated decay give membership in N_U as in part P13. Combining the negative-norm bound with the proved Route U norm comparison gives (1).

#### 4. Monotonicity and limits

Increasing K adds only exponents greater than a_star. For such an exponent, 0<(a-a_star)/(a+a_star+1)<1 since 2a_star+1>0. Thus D strictly decreases, while n and Q_n strictly increase. The fixed nonzero vector e then makes B strictly decrease.

The theorem concerns one finite set of potential branches and a fixed leading profile. It neither estimates weighted smallness nor allows arbitrary variation of the exponent. The difference between epsilon=0 and epsilon=1 is an exact descendant cancellation, not a numerical tolerance. Failure of (1) to exceed the threshold is not evidence that a suitable reference exists.

#### Dependencies

Part P13 supplies the finite-ladder membership argument. Part P27 supplies the generator degree recurrence and monomial-distance identity. Part P32 supplies the exact seventh stationary order and its next residual vector. Part P33 supplies the recursive dilation and cylinder derivative bounds. Arithmetic records and independent exact tests are to be kept in verification alongside this proof.

#### Certified application

The gamma-product calculation at 384 bits and independent direct squared products at 512 bits agree on all eight rows. At K=69,

    B_(69,0)/eta_U < 7e-13,
    B_(69,1)/eta_U < 3e-12.

Both are strictly positive and below one. Monotonicity therefore makes this particular bound inconclusive for every K>=69 in both classes. At the current enlarged support cap K=92 the ratios are approximately 5.12490e-14 and 1.98936e-13 respectively. These are values of a proved lower-bound formula, not measurements of any actual residual norm.

Fifteen exact rational Schur-complement tests, including nonminimal distinguished exponents and a power close to -1/2, reproduce the squared distance product. The independent arithmetic also checks every retained and removed exponent, the dimension and the earlier descendant, and reconstructs the invariant vector from the independently verified eighth density order. See certificate files constant_bound.py, constant_bound.json and constant_bound.log and audit_bound.py,json,log. A second independent review of the argument found it correct.

## P36. An exactly admissible seven-branch refit and its failure of the coefficient and smallness conditions

### P36.1. Exact seven-branch candidates and their necessary point tests

Status: analytical checking identities established. Candidate-specific computation is pending. A point certificate does not prove a global coefficient condition or existence.

#### 1. Function, normalization and exact coordinates

Let c=4076476460239181/2251799813685248, gamma=1/c and delta=1-gamma. An input coefficient file specifies the real potential

    chi=sum a_(j,m,k) H_m(x,y) (x^2+y^2)^(k-m)
                         (1+x^2+y^2)^((3+gamma-j delta)/2-k),
    H_m=Re(x+iy)^(2m), 0<=j<=6, 0<=m<=k.

Each finite term is smooth on the whole plane. This is the polar expression r^(2k)(1+r^2)^(p_j-k) cos(2m theta), where p_j=(3+gamma-j delta)/2. Set rho=-chi_xxy-chi_yyy and u=(-chi_xyy,chi_xxy). The stream chi_xy satisfies -Delta(chi_xy)=rho_x. The parity is the prescribed S1 parity. These derivatives have sublinear growth; the canonical uniqueness convention and harmonic exclusion proved in parts P1.2 and P3 identify this u with U[rho]. No independent harmonic velocity is added.

A monomial generator t^h, t=r^2/(1+r^2), maps to k=m+h. A shifted Legendre generator t^w P_n(2t-1) maps exactly using

    P_n(2t-1)=sum_(h=0)^n (-1)^(n-h) binom(n,h) binom(n+h,h) t^h.

The input rationals, not their floating approximations, determine the function. Define its canonical hash by lexicographically ordered (j,m,k):coefficient lines.

The normalization is c+chi_xxyy(0)=1. If the Taylor coefficients of chi are b_(a,b), then

    chi_xxyy(0)=4 b_(2,2),
    rho_y(0)=-4 b_(2,2)-24 b_(0,4).

These follow by ordinary monomial differentiation. Expand each factor (1+r^2)^(p_j-k) to degree six to compute the center and cubic jets by exact binomial arithmetic. This gives a second exact derivation independent of the previously established per-generator center formulas. It also yields

    [y^3]rho=-8 b_(2,4)-120 b_(0,6),
    [xy^3]psi=8 b_(2,4).

The slope is free in the candidate family. It is not fixed by leading-tail or strain normalization and is not a scaling phase.

#### 2. Exterior moments and residual sectors

The q-th exterior potential moment is

    C_(j,q,m)=sum_k binom(p_j-k,q) a_(j,m,k).

Indeed each generator equals r^(3+gamma-j delta) cos(2m theta) times (1+r^-2)^(p_j-k). For q=0,1 this is respectively sum a and sum (p_j-k)a. Seven leading moments must equal the stationary potential orders 1,...,7 independently reconstructed from the read-only original in part P32. First descendants j=0,1 must be exactly zero. Additional descendants are recorded explicitly.

For a homogeneous complex Fourier term r^s exp(i m theta), x differentiation shifts m to m-1 and m+1 with coefficients (s+m)/2 and (s-m)/2. After extracting a factor i for each y differentiation, y differentiation has the same first coefficient and the negative of the second. Keeping these factors gives the exact density, stream, velocity, gradient and quadratic residual by finite convolution. Thus the sector of radial degree

    p_(h,q)=gamma-h delta-2q

is (c p_(h,q)-1) times its density coefficient, plus every velocity-density-gradient interaction with branch indices i+j=h-1 and descendant indices u+v=q. All present pairs must be included, including branches 0 and 6 in the (7,0) sector. This proves an exact rational algorithm for every reported sector, independent of the producer's evaluator.

The nine required zero sectors are (h,0), h=0,...,6, and (0,1),(1,1). The next possible sector is (2,1), of degree 1-3 delta-2<-2. If it is nonzero it is the leading residual; if it vanishes the next fixed invariant is (7,0), of degree 1-8 delta. Part P32 supplies the latter exact vector. Exterior coefficients with these different powers cannot mix because the reduced denominator of delta is 4076476460239181 and the branch-index differences are smaller. The full-circle L2 norm of a real sine vector e_m is (pi sum_m e_m^2)^(1/2), twice its first-quadrant norm.

Nine exact cancellations imply smooth differentiated decay F=O(r^(1-3 delta-2)). This establishes F in unweighted Hdot^-1: F is integrable with zero integral by odd parity, and has a finite beta moment for any 0<beta<3 delta-1. The Fourier estimate |Fhat(xi)|<=C |xi|^beta gives integrability of |Fhat|^2/|xi|^2 near zero in two dimensions; L2 controls large frequencies. All derivatives decay faster by their order. The weighted derivative components and Bessel fractional components of the Route U and weighted N norms are finite by the cutoff and convolution argument of parts P13 and P20. This is membership, with no smallness conclusion.

#### 3. Independent point evaluations and their scope

For a multi-index I=(i,j),

    partial^I rho=-chi_(i+2,j+1)-chi_(i,j+3),
    partial^I u=(-chi_(i+1,j+2),chi_(i+2,j+1)).

One computation expands the Cartesian Taylor jet at the point to degree seven. A second differentiates the polar radial-polynomial representation. Tensor norms use multiplicity binom(k,i) at derivative order k and sum both velocity components.

With V=cX+u and A=[[rho_y,-rho_x/2],[-rho_x/2,0]], set

The logarithmic derivatives are -(V.X)/(5(1+r^2)) and 16(V.X)/(5(1+4r^2)). The least eigenvalue follows from the exact symmetric two by two characteristic formula. The tested W2 bounds are M_k>=I/2. The eight W3 bounds are those in part P28, namely Du<=14/5, D rho<=16, <r>D2u<=3, <r>D3u<=16, D2rho<=3, <r>D2rho<=8, <r>^2D3rho<=32 and <r>^2D4rho<=512, in ordered tensor norm. The reference-independent embedding of part P19 gives, for 0<s<=2^-12 and R>=1,

    N_(s,R)(F)>=|F(X)|/[16 max(1,r)^(1/5)].

Consequently point evaluation gives a rigorous necessary residual lower bound, to compare with eta=2^-35. It is neither a residual upper bound nor a nonexistence theorem. The uniform six-branch exclusion does not apply to this seven-branch family.

parts P1.2 and P3 fix the canonical inverse and source convention. parts P13 and P20 prove residual-space membership from the exact exterior ladder. ## P37. The canonical strain as a bounded velocity-gradient trace and the output constant of Theorem D_w

### P37.1. The canonical strain as a bounded velocity-gradient trace

Status: analytical derivation complete; independent constant audit and draft review pending. This strengthens output constants in the existing weighted inverse. It changes neither its reference hypotheses nor its sufficient residual threshold.

#### 1. Spaces and statement

Fix R>=1 and 0<s<=2^-12. Let N=N_(s,R) be the compact smooth S1 parity completion defined in part P19:

    N(h)=E_R(J^s h), J=(1-Delta)^(1/2),
    E_R(g)^2=||(1+4r^2)^(2/5)D2g||2^2
             +2^22||<r>^(-1/5)Dg||2^2
             +2^53||w_R g||_(Hdot^-1)^2,
    w_R=(1+r^2/R^2)^(-11/10).

Use its canonical sublinear velocity U=(-R1R2,R1^2) and continuous C1 representative. The singular strain is the already defined canonical functional

    c[h]=partial_y U2[h](0)
        =-h_y(0)/4+(1/pi)PV int sin(3theta) h(X)/r^3 dX.

Then

    |c[h]|<=s^(-1/2) N(h).                              (1)

Let alpha=s/2, p=8/s, kappa=p+4, and define exactly as in part P19

    C_ad(h)=||h||_(C^alpha(B2))
      +sup_(j>=0) 2^(-j/4)
          (||h||_(Linf(Aj))+2^(j alpha)[h]_(C^alpha(Aj))),
    Aj={2^j<=r<=2^(j+1)},
    M(h)=(int_(r<1) r^(-kappa)|h-h_y(0)y|^p dX)^(1/p),
    L_R(h)=||w_R h||_(Hdot^-1).

The compatible four-output bound improves to

    L_R(h)+C_ad(h)+M(h)+|c[h]|<146 s^(-1/2) N(h)          (2)

for nonzero h, with a non-strict inequality also valid for h=0. If the same-space linear inverse A_k has norm at most 1/beta, beta>0, then its four-output constant is at most 146/(beta sqrt(s)). In particular, at s=3*2^-31 and under every unchanged reference and perturbation hypothesis of the audited weighted theorem, the inverse bound 40 gives

    L_R(h)+C_ad(h)+M(h)+|c[h]|<=2^28 N(A_k h).             (3)

This replaces the previously stated sufficient constant 2^58. It is not an optimality claim. The nonlinear radius 5*2^-32, forcing threshold 2^-35 and contraction factor remain those of the original theorem.

#### 2. Trace proof and completion

For a compact smooth parity density h, the canonical stream satisfies U2=psi_x, hence c[h]=psi_xy(0)=partial_y U2(0). This is an equality of the full distributional operator. In particular the contact term -h_y(0)/4 in the displayed kernel representation is already included; it must not be dropped or added a second time.

Part P19, equation(5), proves

    ||Dh||infinity<=4N(h)/sqrt(s),
    ||DU[h]||infinity<=4N(h)/sqrt(s).

The second estimate follows from the same absolute Fourier integral as the first, since the vector velocity multiplier has Euclidean magnitude |xi_1|/|xi|<=1. The ordered tensor norm of DU bounds every component, including partial_y U2(0). This first proves the weaker bound 4 N(h)/sqrt(s) on the compact core.

Let h_n converge to h in N. The same estimates show uniform convergence of Dh_n and DU[h_n] on the entire plane. Parity gives U[h_n](0)=0, so the velocities converge locally uniformly as well. The established distributional realization identifies this limit with the canonical U[h]; there is no undetermined affine or harmonic velocity. Uniform convergence of first derivatives proves convergence of their origin traces. Thus the trace identity and its weaker bound extend to the completed space.

For completeness, this trace agrees with the existing singular-integral definition on the completion. The C^(s/2) estimate for Dh_n-h and the zero linear-jet subtraction give an integrable near-origin bound of order r^(1+s/2) in the kernel integral. The weighted P0 bound controls its far part, exactly as in part P19 section 6. The contact terms converge by the uniform derivative estimate. Hence both definitions are continuous in N, agree on the compact core, and agree on its completion. This argument uses no higher-order Holder norm beyond the already proved fractional-space embedding.

#### 3. The strain multiplier gives the sharper constant

The same Fourier calculation in part P19 retains the more precise inequality

    (2pi)^(-1) int |xi| |h_hat(xi)| dxi
             <=2K N(h)/sqrt(s), K=2595/2048.

The strain trace has multiplier -i xi_y xi_x^2/|xi|^2. Its absolute magnitude divided by |xi| is a sqrt(1-a), where a=xi_x^2/|xi|^2 belongs to [0,1]. The exact identity

    4/27-a^2(1-a)=(a-2/3)^2(a+1/3)>=0

gives the angular factor 2/(3sqrt(3)). Consequently

    |c[h]|<=[4K/(3sqrt(3))] N(h)/sqrt(s)<N(h)/sqrt(s),

because (4*2595)^2<27*2048^2. This establishes (1) on the core and then on the completion by the trace convergence just proved. No separate first-order Riesz operator bound is multiplied into the estimate. The exact strain multiplier retains its full angular structure.

#### 4. Four outputs and inverse

The existing independently verified estimates give

    L_R(h)<=N(h),
    C_ad(h)<=128 N(h)/sqrt(s),
    M(h)<=16 N(h)/sqrt(s).

Adding (1) bounds the sum by (145+sqrt(s))N(h)/sqrt(s). Since s<=2^-12, sqrt(s)<=1/64 and 145+1/64<146, proving (2). Applying the unchanged inverse norm gives the general claim. At s=3*2^-31, sqrt(s)=sqrt(6)*2^-16. The exact integer inequality

    (40*146*2^16)^2 < 6*2^56

proves 40*146/sqrt(s)<2^28, establishing (3).

The inverse is the maximal distributional realization already proved bijective in parts P17, P19, P21 and P24. No new existence, domain, semigroup or nonlinear product assertion is needed here. An actual reference still has to satisfy the coefficient contract and the forcing smallness condition; the candidates audited so far do not.

## P38. Necessary local distance of exact solutions from the projected refits

### P38.1. Necessary distance from a reference to an exact profile

Status: analytical statement proved below; candidate-specific point computations pending. This is a necessary-condition theorem and does not require coercivity or a small residual.

#### 1. Reference, correction and constants

Let bar_rho be a smooth full-plane S1 parity density with its fixed canonical sublinear velocity bar_u=U[bar_rho]. Fix c and assume c+c[bar_rho]=1 and a0=bar_rho_y(0)>0. Let

    bar_V=cX+bar_u, F=bar_V.D bar_rho-bar_rho.

Use the compact parity correction space N=N_(s,R) of part P19, for R>=1 and 0<s<=2^-12. For h in this space let n=N(h), kappa=s^(-1/2), a=4kappa, and for a point X=(x,y) with r=|X| put

    g=max(1,r)^(1/5),
    H=min(a|y|,16g),
    B=min(ar,104g).

The proved embeddings give

    |Dh(X)|<=an, |h(X)|<=Hn, |U[h](X)|<=Bn.

Here h(x,0)=0 and U[h](0)=0 follow from parity; integrating the bounded gradients gives the first entries of both minima. The second entries are the proved density and canonical-velocity growth bounds. No property of the numerical reference is used in these correction estimates.

For the normalization-dependent case let t=1, using the sharper strain estimate of part P37, or let t=4, using the older velocity-gradient trace bound alone. Set

    D_t=B+t kappa r,
    A_t=a|bar_V(X)|+H+D_t|D bar_rho(X)|,
    Q_t=a D_t.

For the fixed-exponent case use t=0, so D_0=B.

#### 2. Necessary inequality and exclusion ball

Suppose rho=bar_rho+h is an exact stationary profile for some real exponent c', with the same canonical inverse and S1 parity. If n<a0/a, then

    c'=c-c[h],
    |F(X)|<=A_t n+Q_t n^2,                    t=1 or 4.     (1)

In the fixed-exponent case c'=c, one instead has

    |F(X)|<=A_0 n+Q_0 n^2,                                  (2)

without a center-slope restriction.

Consequently, for q>0, if

    aq<a0,   |F(X)|>A_t q+Q_t q^2,                         (3)

there is no such exact profile with N(h)<=q, for any exponent c'. For fixed c the first condition can be omitted. One certified point suffices. Different references and different points have their own coefficients A_t,Q_t; these cannot be inherited from an earlier candidate.

If desired, (1) gives a positive distance bound

    N(h)>=min(a0/a, 2|F(X)|/[A_t+sqrt(A_t^2+4Q_t|F(X)|)]).

The strict test (3) is used for all reported dyadic radii, avoiding any ambiguity from a rounded root.

#### 3. Proof of normalization and residual identity

The completion embeds in C^(1,s/2) locally for h and its canonical velocity. Parity gives

    rho(X)=a_total y+o(r),
    U[rho](X)=(-c[rho]x,c[rho]y)+o(r),
    a_total=a0+h_y(0).

Incompressibility determines the first diagonal entry and parity kills the off-diagonal entries. Since |h_y(0)|<=an<a0, a_total is positive. The stationary equation has first-order term

    a_total(c'+c[rho]-1)y.

Dividing along the y axis by y and taking the limit proves c'+c[rho]=1. Linearity of the canonical strain and reference normalization give c'=c-c[h]. This proof requires no second derivative of h at the center and no assumption that the approximate reference is stationary.

Set W=U[h]-c[h]X. The exact difference of the nonlinear equations is

    0=F+bar_V.Dh-h+W.D bar_rho+W.Dh.

The strain bound gives |W(X)|<=D_t n. Taking absolute values proves (1). If c'=c, the same calculation uses W=U[h] and proves (2). Each resulting function is continuous, so the identity holds pointwise even when the equation was initially imposed distributionally. The right side of (1) is nondecreasing in n>=0. Under (3), n<=q contradicts it, proving the exclusion claim.

#### 4. Exact point certification and scope

For each supplied finite reference, independently reconstruct its exact canonical coefficients. Derivatives of the potential through order four give bar_rho, bar_u, D bar_rho and F. Evaluate them using both Cartesian Taylor jets and independently differentiated polar polynomials with outward interval arithmetic. Use upper enclosures for A_t and Q_t and a lower enclosure for |F|. The strict comparison (3), including the center-slope condition, then gives a rigorous radius. Retain source, canonical and code hashes and the exact rational radius.

This exclusion is a local statement in the explicitly chosen norm. It does not exclude a profile outside the certified ball, rule out different asymptotic normalization classes, or assert any sharp distance. Unlike failure of a sufficient residual threshold, it does exclude an exact solution within the specified ball. No global W1, W2 or W3 coefficient condition is assumed. Allowing c' in (1) accounts for its normalized variation; no exponent derivative is silently dropped.

#### Dependencies

Part P19 gives the correction growth and gradient embeddings, including the canonical velocity. Part P37 proves the improved strain constant t=1; the t=4 version follows directly from the earlier velocity-gradient bound. The canonical linearization and center identity are independently established in part P1.2, and are re-derived above for the regularity used here. Exact source reconstructions are those in part P1.1, part P20 or part P36, depending on the candidate.

## P39. A necessary annular distance of exact solutions from the checkpoint, for every exponent

### P39.1. A necessary annular distance from the original reference

Status: analytical proof and all three numerical comparisons independently CONFIRMED. This is a necessary-condition result, independent of coercivity and of sufficient residual thresholds.

A large residual norm does not by itself exclude a nearby exact solution. Here a signed residual pairing does: integrating the difference equation transfers the derivative off the correction, so the already proved growth bounds control every error term. The fixed leading tail also determines the exponent of any possible exact profile.

#### 1. Space and reference

Let R>=1 and 0<s<=2^-12. Define J=(1-Delta)^(1/2),

Use the completion of real smooth compact densities even in x and odd in y, with the canonical distributional inverse U=(-R1 R2,R1^2). Derivatives use ordered Cartesian tensors and Euclidean norms. The embeddings proved in part P19 imply that h and U[h] are locally C1 and, for n=N_(s,R)(h),

    |U[h](X)|<=104 n max(1,r)^(1/5).                 (1)

Let bar_rho be the exact original state 131 recovered from the read-only checkpoint, bar_u=U[bar_rho], and

    c=4076476460239181/2251799813685248,
    gamma=1/c, d=4/9, bar_V=cX+bar_u,
    F=bar_V.D bar_rho-bar_rho.

The independently verified source expansion and coefficient bounds give

    1/5<gamma<1,
    r^(-gamma) bar_rho(r,theta)->Theta(theta) uniformly,
    Theta not identically zero,  bar_u=O(r^gamma),
    |bar_u(X)|<=22 r^(1-d), |D bar_rho(X)|<=186 r^(-d)  (r>0). (2)

The normalization of c is the exact stored center-strain normalization. The argument below does not require positivity of the corrected center slope.

#### 2. Exponent rigidity in the weighted affine class

If rho=bar_rho+h, h in N_(s,R), is an exact canonical profile with any real exponent c', then c'=c.

To prove this, set G_T(X)=T^(-gamma)rho(TX) and U_T(X)=T^(-gamma)U[rho](TX). On each compact annulus, (1)-(2) imply uniform convergence G_T->G=|X|^gamma Theta(arg X) and uniform boundedness of U_T. In particular G is nonzero. The rescaled equation is

    c' X.D G_T-G_T+T^(gamma-1) U_T.D G_T=0.

Since div U_T=0, its weak form against any smooth compact test on the annulus contains the nonlinear term

    -T^(gamma-1) integral G_T U_T.D test.

This tends to zero by the uniform bounds and gamma<1. The other terms converge distributionally, giving c' X.DG-G=0. The homogeneous function G satisfies X.DG=gamma G distributionally, as follows by differentiating its exact scaling identity under the integral. Thus (c' gamma-1)G=0. Since G is nonzero, c'=1/gamma=c. No decay estimate for D h at infinity has been assumed.

#### 3. General compact-test inequality

Let zeta be a real compact C1 function with support in T<=r<=2T, T>=1. Suppose

    ||zeta||_infinity<=Z,
    ||D zeta||_infinity<=C/T.

Put

    H_T=16(2T)^(1/5), B_T=104(2T)^(1/5),
    V_T=2cT+22(2T)^(5/9), D_T=186 T^(-4/9),
    A_T=3pi T^2 {H_T[V_T C/T+(2c+1)Z]+B_T D_T Z},
    Q_T=3pi T H_T B_T C.

Every exact profile in the affine class, with any exponent, necessarily satisfies

    |integral F zeta|<=A_T n+Q_T n^2.                 (3)

Indeed section 2 fixes its exponent. Subtracting the two equations gives

    0=F+bar_V.Dh-h+U[h].D bar_rho+U[h].Dh.

All functions are locally C1. Integration by parts, div bar_V=2c and div U[h]=0 yield the exact identity

    integral F zeta
      = integral h [bar_V.D zeta+(2c+1)zeta]
        -integral U[h].D bar_rho zeta
        +integral h U[h].D zeta.                    (4)

The support has area 3pi T^2. Equations(1)-(2) and the two test bounds prove(3). Compact C1 tests follow either directly from the classical local regularity or by smooth approximation in C1. No derivative of h has been bounded by an unweighted residual norm.

Consequently, if a certified number P_T>0 satisfies |integral F zeta|>=P_T and

    P_T>A_T q+Q_T q^2,                              (5)

then there is no exact profile in this affine class with N_(s,R)(h)<=q. The conclusion is uniform in R>=1 and 0<s<=2^-12. It is a local distance statement and does not exclude larger corrections.

#### 4. The audited C9 test

Let e_m be the exact coefficients of the leading residual sector r^(2gamma-1) sum_m e_m sin(m theta), using positive odd harmonics. Put

    a_m=e_m/(1/35+m^2/630),
    S0=sum_m |a_m|, S1=sum_m m|a_m|,

    zeta_T(X)=(1+r^2/T^2)^(-11/10) chi(r/T) sum_m a_m sin(m theta).

This is a compact C1 test on the stated annulus. For x=t-1 in [0,1], 0<=chi<=1/16 and |chi'|=|2x(1-x)(1-2x)|<=1/2. The radial weight is at most 1 and its logarithmic derivative has size at most 11/(10T), since t/(1+t^2)<=1/2. Angular differentiation costs at most S1/r<=S1/T. Therefore

    Z=S0/16,
    C=S0/2+11S0/160+S1/16=91S0/160+S1/16             (6)

are valid. The norm of the full gradient is bounded by the sum of its radial and angular components, so no angular derivative is omitted.

The independent C9 computation, with fourth-order tail expansion and full analytic remainder, already encloses integral F zeta_T at T=2^31,2^32,2^35. Subtract its certified absolute remainder from its pairing lower endpoint to obtain P_T. That computation reconstructs the original coefficient vector again and checks the exact e_m vector against part P3. Its proof and exact source hashes are retained in section P11.4, section P11.5 and audit_c9_Q4.json. Combining these inputs with (5)-(6) requires no new quadrature.

## P41. Square tests uniform in the smoothness index

### P41.1. Compact tests give a distance uniform in the fractional exponent

Status: analytical derivation and the numerical comparisons below are independently CONFIRMED. Lead analytical This is a necessary-condition theorem, with no coercivity assumption.

#### 1. Exact statement

Let N=N_(s,R) be the real canonical S1 parity space of part P39, for R>=1 and 0<s<=2^-12. Let a smooth canonical reference bar_rho satisfy

    bar_rho(r,theta)=r^gamma Theta(theta)+o(r^gamma) uniformly,
    Theta not identically zero, 1/5<gamma<1,
    U[bar_rho]=O(r^gamma), c=1/gamma.

Write bar_V=cX+U[bar_rho], F=bar_V.D bar_rho-bar_rho. Let S be the closed square with center X0 and half side delta>0. Suppose throughout S that F has a constant sign and

    |F|>=f>0, |bar_V|<=V, |D bar_rho|<=D,
    max(1,|X|)^(1/5)<=g.

Put H=16g, B=104g, d=15/(4delta), and

    A=H[Vd+|2c+1|]+BD, Q=HBd.

Then every exact canonical profile rho=bar_rho+h in this affine space, with any prospective exponent and n=N(h), satisfies

    f<=An+Qn^2.                                          (1)

Consequently f>Aq+Qq^2 excludes every exact profile with n<=q. The statement is uniform in R and s in the specified ranges.

#### 2. Proof

The completed space has locally C1 canonical representatives and the uniform bounds

    |h(X)|<=16 max(1,|X|)^(1/5)n,
    |U[h](X)|<=104 max(1,|X|)^(1/5)n.

The proof in part P40, section 1, fixes the exponent of every exact profile in this affine class to c. More explicitly, the rescaled densities T^-gamma rho(TX) converge uniformly on compact annuli to the nonzero homogeneous leading density G, while T^-gamma U[rho](TX) stay bounded there. The nonlinear term in the rescaled weak equation is T^(gamma-1) div(G_T U_T), which tends to zero distributionally. The limit is (c'gamma-1)G=0, hence c'=c. No derivative decay of the correction is used.

Define phi(t)=(1-t^2)^2 for |t|<=1 and zero otherwise. This is nonnegative and C1, and

    integral phi=16/15, integral |phi'|=2.

For zeta(X)=phi((x-x0)/delta) phi((y-y0)/delta), its mass is M=delta^2(16/15)^2. The Euclidean gradient obeys |D zeta|<=|zeta_x|+|zeta_y|, so

    integral |D zeta|<=64delta/15=dM.

The exact correction equation, integrated against zeta, is

    integral F zeta
      =integral h[bar_V.D zeta+(2c+1)zeta]
       -integral U[h].D bar_rho zeta
       +integral h U[h].D zeta.                         (2)

This follows by ordinary compact integration by parts: div bar_V=2c and div U[h]=0. It also follows by smooth approximation of zeta in C1. The sign assumption and positivity of zeta bound the absolute left side below by fM. The two growth embeddings and the hypotheses on S bound the right side above by (An+Qn^2)M. Since M>0, (1) follows.

#### 3. Enclosure method and scope

For a finite exact regularized-power potential, all required fields are finite sums of radial powers times polynomials and trigonometric functions. A Cartesian derivative maps a summand

    r^(-d) (1+r^2)^p t^k C_n(theta), t=r^2/(1+r^2),

into a finite sum with d increased by one, angular order shifted by one, and polynomial degree increased by at most one. The recurrence is obtained from partial_x=cos(theta)partial_r-sin(theta)partial_theta/r and partial_y=sin(theta)partial_r+cos(theta)partial_theta/r. Thus it is an identity before intervals are substituted.

The verification code groups equal radial exponents and harmonics, and recenters the radial polynomials at the exact central value t0. Substituting the interval t-t0 into those polynomials is an enclosure of the original field throughout the square. On a square in y>0, theta=pi/2-arctan(x/y) is single valued; ordinary interval sine and cosine enclose every angular factor. Interval square roots and rational powers enclose the radial factors. No point sample or angular mesh is used as a uniform bound.

A separate reconstruction and evaluation must check the exact input, the polar derivatives and the strict arithmetic before a numerical exclusion is marked CONFIRMED. An unsuccessful interval sign test proves nothing about the sign of F on the square. These are local lower-distance bounds. They do not exclude larger corrections or a change of the leading angular data outside N.

#### 4. Taylor enclosure that preserves center cancellations

Direct interval evaluation can lose the cancellation between the potential's radial branches. The following alternative still encloses the entire square. Let d0=sqrt(2) delta, so |X-X0|<=d0 on S. For a scalar C3 function f, Taylor's formula along the segment from X0 to X gives

    |f(X)-f(X0)| <= d0 |Df(X0)| + d0^2 |D^2 f(X0)|/2
                       + d0^3 sup_S |D^3 f|/6.          (3)

Here and below the derivative tensors have their Euclidean Frobenius norms, which dominate contraction with unit vectors. The square is convex, so the segment stays in S. The same formula holds for vector and tensor fields, using their Frobenius norms and the integral remainder. Applying (3) to F gives a sign enclosure. Applying it to bar_V and D bar_rho gives

    sup_S |bar_V| <= |bar_V(X0)| + d0 |D bar_V(X0)|
                     + d0^2 |D^2 bar_V(X0)|/2
                     + d0^3 sup_S |D^3 bar_V|/6,
    sup_S |D bar_rho| <= |D bar_rho(X0)| + d0 |D^2 bar_rho(X0)|
                         + d0^2 |D^3 bar_rho(X0)|/2
                         + d0^3 sup_S |D^4 bar_rho|/6.   (4)

All fields in (3)-(4) require at most seven derivatives of the potential. The Cartesian Leibniz identity is

    D^(i,j) F = sum_(a<=i,b<=j) binom(i,a) binom(j,b)
       [D^(a,b) bar_V1 D^(i-a+1,j-b) bar_rho
        + D^(a,b) bar_V2 D^(i-a,j-b+1) bar_rho]
       - D^(i,j) bar_rho.

Thus the exact polar recurrence of section 3 gives interval enclosures of the highest derivatives throughout S; separately evaluating the lower derivatives at X0 retains their cancellations. The sum of binomially weighted squares gives the Frobenius norm of a symmetric derivative tensor. Taking absolute upper endpoints componentwise before this sum preserves its status as an upper bound, even when a component interval straddles zero. These formulas are the complete justification for the Taylor interval implementation. Agreement with an independent point evaluation checks the algebra; it is not used to replace a bound over S.

The potential coefficients were reconstructed from the exact generator handoffs using the three-term shifted-Legendre recurrence, independently of the producer's binomial expansion. The full leading moments and canonical velocity hypotheses are the exact checks in parts P20, P40 and P42. The Taylor box calculation uses 640-bit directed interval arithmetic. The audit uses rational endpoints and integer roots, checks all 45 strict dyadic comparisons for the two references, and checks all 80 center residual derivatives against an independent Cartesian Taylor product.
